李俊，绰号「混江龙」，应天寿星，梁山泊英雄座次第二十六位，乃水军头领之首。其人本.en:
Li Jun, known as the River Dragon, embodies the Heavenly Star of Longevity. Ranked twenty-sixth among Liangshan's heroes, he is foremost of its naval commanders. Originally from Luzhou, he trades illicitly around Jieyang Ridge on the Yangtze, making his living selling contraband salt and working as a boatman on the Xunyang River. An extraordinary swimmer, he can lie beneath the water for seven days and nights, appearing amid wind and waves like a dragon in the depths; thus the wandering world calls him the River Dragon. His face is smooth as jade, his brows thick and eyes large. Bold, shrewd, and experienced, he lacks the rashness of ordinary sailors and ranks among Liangshan's commanders who combine wisdom with courage. His companions are mostly outlaw heroes. He is especially close to the brothers Tong Wei and Tong Meng, and the three are well known around Jieyang Ridge.

Li Jun's friendship with Song Jiang begins with a life saved. Exiled to Jiangzhou after killing Yan Poxi, Song Jiang passes through Jieyang Ridge. Li Jun is working below the ridge with Tong Wei and Tong Meng. Having heard of Song Jiang's fame, he comes to meet him and treats him as a kindred spirit. Later, Song Jiang drunkenly writes a seditious poem at Xunyang Tower. Huang Wenbing denounces him; he is imprisoned under sentence of death and taken to Jiangzhou's marketplace for beheading. Liangshan's heroes storm the execution ground and rescue him, while Li Jun, Zhang Shun, Zhang Heng, the three Ruan brothers, Tong Wei, and Tong Meng provide support by water. They gather at White Dragon Temple to affirm their brotherhood. Together they then attack Wuwei, capture Huang Wenbing, cut out his heart and carve his flesh, taking vengeance for Song Jiang. Li Jun contributes greatly throughout the Jiangzhou crisis and afterward joins Song Jiang at Liangshan.

At Liangshan, Li Jun commands the navy and ranks first among its naval leaders. Water surrounds the stronghold on three sides; the marsh is its lifeline, and battles on the waterways often decide its survival when imperial armies attack. Li Jun leads Zhang Heng, Zhang Shun, the three Ruan brothers, Tong Wei, Tong Meng, and other powerful swimmers in repeatedly defeating imperial fleets. In the two victories over Tong Guan and three defeats of Gao Qiu, his ambushes beneath the water, scuttling and overturning ships and capturing officers alive, earn particular distinction. Even so high an official as Gao Qiu is captured in a naval engagement, demonstrating the strength of Liangshan's fleet. At the Grand Assembly, Li Jun takes his place among the Heavenly Stars as the Star of Longevity. His position as supreme naval commander carries great weight.

After the imperial amnesty, Li Jun follows the army against Liao, Tian Hu, and Wang Qing, serving in the vanguard whenever there is fighting on water. The campaign against Fang La in particular gives the navy its proper battlefield among the crisscrossing waterways south of the Yangtze. Li Jun and the other naval commanders sink enemy vessels and win repeated honors. Yet Liangshan suffers appalling losses in this campaign, with its brothers dead or wounded in great numbers. Seeing this, Li Jun begins to think of retirement.

Li Jun's fate is among the happiest and most legendary of the 108. During the Fang La campaign, he reaches Lake Tai and meets four heroes, Fei Bao, Ni Yun, Bu Qing, and Di Cheng. Their meeting becomes known as the Little Brotherhood of Lake Tai. They urge him to retire once his work is done and not covet wealth and rank; Li Jun agrees wholeheartedly. When the army returns, he feigns a paralyzing stroke outside Suzhou and begs Song Jiang to let him remain there to recover, with Tong Wei and Tong Meng to tend him. Song Jiang agrees in tears, leaves money for his expenses, and leads the army away. As soon as the troops have passed, Li Jun rises at once. With the Tong brothers, he goes straight to Lake Tai to join Fei Bao and the others. They build ships, set sail, and leave across the sea, reaching Siam in the southern seas. Li Jun eventually becomes its ruler, a free king who enjoys his full span of years and dies peacefully abroad. Among the Liangshan heroes, so many of whom die or scatter, the River Dragon sees through the rise and fall of fortune and has the courage to withdraw. Sailing overseas to found a kingship, he proves himself a man who understands his times and keeps clear of disaster, leaving later readers of Water Margin to close the book with sighs and envy.
李俊，绰号「混江龙」，应天寿星，梁山泊英雄座次第二十六位，乃水军头领之首。其人本.ja:
李俊、異名は「混江竜」。天寿星に応じ、梁山泊の好漢中第二十六位、水軍頭領の筆頭である。もとは廬州の人で、揚子江の掲陽嶺付近で私商を営み、塩の密売を生業としながら潯陽江の船頭も務めた。水練に非常に優れ、七日七晩も水底に潜み、風波の中を出入りする姿が淵を泳ぐ竜のようだったため、江湖で「混江竜」と呼ばれた。顔は潤った玉のようで、眉は濃く目は大きい。胆力と知略に富み、物事の扱いも老練で、普通の船乗りのような無鉄砲さはない。梁山水軍で智勇を兼ね備えた主将であった。普段交わるのは江湖の亡命好漢が多く、とりわけ童威・童猛兄弟と親しく、三人は掲陽嶺一帯で名を知られていた。

李俊と宋江の交情は、命を救う恩から始まる。閻婆惜を殺して江州へ刺配される宋江が、掲陽嶺を通った。その頃、李俊は童威・童猛と嶺の下で商売をしており、宋江の名声を聞いて、わざわざ会いに来て知己とした。のちに宋江は潯陽楼で酔って反詩を書き、黄文炳に告発され、死囚牢に入れられる。死罪が決まり、江州の市曹へ斬首のため連行された。梁山の好漢が刑場を襲って救い出すと、李俊・張順・張横・三阮・童威・童猛ら水中の豪傑が援護し、白竜廟に集って小さな聚義を行う。さらに皆で無為軍を攻め、黄文炳を生け捕りにして心臓を抉り、肉を削いで、宋江の大仇を討った。江州の危難で多くの力を尽くした李俊は、そのまま宋江に従って梁山泊の仲間となった。

梁山泊では李俊が水軍を掌り、水軍頭領の第一に列した。三方を水に囲まれる梁山にとって水泊は命脈であり、官軍が討伐に来るたび、水路の一戦がしばしば存亡を決めた。李俊は張横・張順・三阮・童威・童猛ら水中の健将を率い、幾度も官軍の水師を破る。童貫を二度、高俅を三度破った戦いでは、水中に伏せ、船底を穿ち、船を転覆させ、官将を生け捕りにするなど、特に大きな功を立てた。高俅ほどの高官さえ水陣で捕らえられており、梁山水軍の強さが分かる。大聚義で座次が定まると、李俊は天罡の「天寿星」として水軍を総べ、極めて重い役目を担った。

招安後、李俊は軍に従って遼を征し、田虎・王慶を平定した。水戦になると常に先頭に立つ。なかでも方臘への南征は、江南の水路が縦横に走る土地で、水軍が力を振るう場となった。李俊と水将たちは船を沈めて敵を破り、殊勲を重ねる。しかしこの戦いで梁山の損害は惨烈を極め、多くの兄弟が死傷した。それを目の当たりにし、李俊は早くも隠退を考えるようになる。

李俊の結末は百八人の中でも珍しく円満で、ひときわ伝奇的である。方臘征討の途中、太湖に至った李俊は費保・倪雲・卜青・狄成の四人と知り合い、「太湖の小結義」と呼ばれる契りを結んだ。四人は、功を成したら身を引き、栄華を求めるなと勧め、李俊も深くうなずく。大軍が凱旋する際、蘇州の城外で中風による麻痺を装い、宋江に、その場で養生させてほしいと懇願し、童威・童猛を世話役に残す。宋江は涙ながらに許し、路銀を置いて軍を率い去った。軍が通り過ぎると李俊はすぐに立ち上がり、兄弟と太湖へ向かって費保らと合流する。船を造って帆を上げ、海を渡り、暹羅国、すなわち南洋の地へ行った。やがて李俊はその国の主となり、自由な王として天寿を全うし、海外で安らかに没する。死ぬか離散するかで衰え尽くした梁山の好漢たちの中、この混江竜だけは興亡を見抜き、激流から勇気をもって退き、海の彼方で王業を成した。時勢を知り、身を全うして災いを避けた人物として、後世の読者に深いため息と羨望を残す。

李逵，绰号「黑旋风」，应天罡之数，乃天杀星临世。其人乃沂州沂水县百丈村人氏，因在.en:
Li Kui, the Black Whirlwind, is one of the Heavenly Stars, the Heavenly Star of Killing made flesh. A native of Baizhang Village in Yishui County, Yizhou, he flees after killing someone at home. Even after an amnesty he does not return, instead drifting to Jiangzhou, where he becomes a minor jailer. His appearance is fearsome: coarse flesh like a black bear, skin tough as an iron ox, wild hair and murderous menace. At home they call him Iron Ox. In the wandering world, his dark skin, whirlwind temper, and unrestrained killing and burning earn him the name Black Whirlwind. He wields two broad axes and loves fighting bare-chested. Immensely strong and bloodthirsty, he is also innocent, endearingly straightforward, deeply devoted to his mother, and obedient above all to Song Jiang.

Li Kui first appears at Jiangzhou, where Dai Zong introduces him to Song Jiang. From the first meeting, he gives Song Jiang his wholehearted allegiance. The three drink at Xunyang Tower. Unsatisfied with the wine and wanting fresh fish, Li Kui goes to the riverside fish market. He quarrels and fights with Zhang Shun, the White Streak in the Waves, on the bank. Zhang Shun lures him into the river, filling him with swallowed water until Li Kui learns that he cannot match him there. They become brothers afterward. When Song Jiang's rebellious poem sends him to jail and Prefect Cai Jiu orders him and Dai Zong executed, Liangshan's heroes attack the execution ground. Li Kui leaps naked from an upper-floor teahouse with his two axes and hacks ahead, killing whoever he encounters without distinguishing soldiers from civilians. Bodies cover the ground; his unstoppable ferocity wins him fame. He then follows Song Jiang to Liangshan.

After joining, Li Kui misses his aged mother and returns to Yishui to bring her to the mountain and share his good fortune. On the way he encounters Li Gui, who impersonates the Black Whirlwind to rob travelers. Li Kui exposes and kills him. Later, carrying his mother across Yi Ridge, he leaves her on a rock while he seeks water. On his return, tigers have eaten her, leaving only two legs. In fury, Li Kui kills four tigers with his bare hands: two cubs, a male, and a female. His vengeance at Yi Ridge becomes a famous tale. Yet people discover his identity through the tiger killing, and Elder Cao and the hunters nearly capture him. Zhu Gui and Zhu Fu save him, allowing him to escape disaster and return to Liangshan.

At Liangshan, Li Kui specializes in charging into enemy formations, a foremost fierce warrior among the infantry leaders. He takes part in the three assaults on Zhu Family Manor, the attack on Gaotangzhou, the breaking of the Linked Cavalry, and the disturbances at Jiangzhou and the capital, killing more than anyone. His recklessness often causes trouble and absurdity, as in the Lantern Festival uproar in the capital, his attempts to judge cases, and his penitent carrying of thorn branches. Once he believes a report that Song Jiang has abducted Elder Liu's daughter. Enraged, he cuts down the apricot-yellow banner and threatens to kill Song Jiang. Only after discovering the culprit was an impostor does he carry thorns to ask forgiveness. Yet his devotion to Song Jiang never changes, even in death. At the Grand Assembly, Li Kui is ranked twenty-second as the Heavenly Star of Killing and foremost among the infantry leaders.

After the amnesty, Li Kui follows Song Jiang against Liao, Tian Hu, Wang Qing, and Fang La, fighting north and south, killing generals and capturing banners with repeated distinction. He often forms a unit with Bao Xu, Xiang Chong, and Li Gun, using throwing knives and round shields to break formations. The Fang La campaign costs Liangshan seven or eight of every ten brothers, but Li Kui survives. On their return to court, he is appointed military commander of Runzhou in Zhenjiang.

But the treacherous Gao Qiu, Yang Jian, and others arrange to poison Song Jiang with medicated wine. Having drunk the emperor's poisoned gift, Song Jiang knows he will die. Fearing that Li Kui will rebel on learning the truth and ruin Liangshan's reputation for loyalty, he summons him from Runzhou to Chuzhou and shares poisoned wine with him. Only after Li Kui drinks does Song Jiang explain. Li Kui bears no resentment, but weeps: 'So be it! In life I served you, elder brother; in death I shall still be a little ghost under your command!' He returns to Runzhou and soon dies when the poison takes effect. His last wish is to have his coffin buried beside Song Jiang at Liao'er Hollow in Chuzhou, following him in life and death. A Heavenly Star of Killing willingly dies to preserve Song Jiang's loyal name, an act of ultimate devotion and a tragedy of blind loyalty. Later, their restless spirits often appear at Liao'er Hollow, and villagers build a temple where offerings continue year after year. Li Kui's life is fierce as a whirlwind in its slaughter and pure as a child's heart in its filial devotion and loyalty. From Jiangzhou's execution ground to Chuzhou's poisoned wine, he is among the most pitied and lamented of the 108 heroes.
李逵，绰号「黑旋风」，应天罡之数，乃天杀星临世。其人乃沂州沂水县百丈村人氏，因在.ja:
李逵、異名は「黒旋風」。天罡の数に応じ、天殺星の化身である。沂州沂水県の百丈村に生まれ、故郷で人を打ち殺して逃亡した。赦免に遭っても帰郷せず、江州に流れ着いて小牢子となる。黒熊のような粗い肉、鉄牛のように頑丈な皮膚を持ち、髪は乱れ、殺気と凶相を漂わせる。郷里では「鉄牛」と呼ばれ、江湖では肌の黒さと旋風のような気性、人殺しも放火も顧みぬことから「黒旋風」の異名を得た。二本の板斧を使い、裸で戦うのを好む。力は絶倫、殺性は激しいが、天真爛漫で愚直な愛嬌があり、母に孝行で、とりわけ宋江一人の言葉をよく聞いた。

李逵が登場するのは江州である。戴宗の紹介で宋江に会うと、初対面から心服した。三人で潯陽楼の酒を飲むが、李逵は酒に満足せず、さらに鮮魚を欲しがって川辺の魚市場へ行く。岸で浪裏白跳の張順と喧嘩し、水へ誘い込まれて腹いっぱい水を飲まされ、水中では敵わぬと悟った。これを機に張順とも兄弟になる。のちに宋江が反詩で投獄され、蔡九知府が宋江と戴宗を斬ろうとすると、梁山の好漢が刑場を襲う。李逵は二本の板斧を振るい、茶坊の楼上から裸で跳び下りて先頭を斬り進んだ。官兵か民衆かを問わず出会う人を殺し、死体を地に横たえ、その止め難い勇猛さで名を挙げる。以後、宋江と共に梁山へ上った。

入山後、李逵は老母を思い、共に富貴を享受させようと沂水県へ迎えに戻る。道中では「黒旋風」を騙って旅人を襲う李鬼に出会い、見破って殺した。母を背負って沂嶺を越える途中、岩に母を休ませて水を探しに行くが、戻ると母は虎に食われ、二本の脚しか残っていなかった。激怒した李逵は素手で、子虎二頭と雄雌の虎一頭ずつ、合わせて四頭を殺し、母の仇を討つ。沂嶺の虎退治は奇談として伝わる。しかしその一件から正体が知られ、曹太公と猟師たちに捕らえられかけた。朱貴と朱富に救われて大難を逃れ、再び梁山へ戻った。

梁山の李逵は、もっぱら先陣を切って敵陣へ突入する、歩軍頭領中でも第一等の猛将であった。三打祝家荘、高唐州攻略、連環馬攻略、江州や東京の騒動と、加わらぬ戦いはなく、最も多く人を殺した。気性の粗さで失敗も多く、元宵の東京での騒ぎ、役所での裁判、荊を負っての謝罪など、笑い話や災いを引き起こす。宋江が劉太公の娘を奪ったという話を信じ、怒って杏黄旗を斬り倒し、宋江を殺そうとしたこともある。偽者の仕業と分かり、ようやく荊を負って謝罪した。それでも宋江への赤心は死ぬまで変わらない。大聚義では天殺星として第二十二位、歩軍頭領の筆頭に列した。

招安後、李逵は宋江に従って遼・田虎・王慶・方臘を征し、南北を転戦して将を斬り旗を奪い、奇功を重ねた。鮑旭・項充・李袞らと一隊を組むことが多く、飛刀と丸盾を使って敵陣を破った。方臘征討では梁山兄弟の十中七、八が失われるが、李逵は幸いにも生還する。凱旋後、朝廷から鎮江潤州都統制に任じられた。

ところが高俅・楊戩ら奸臣が、薬酒で宋江を毒殺しようとする。御賜の毒酒を飲んだ宋江は死を覚悟し、李逵が真相を知れば再び反乱を起こし、梁山の「忠義」の名を損なうと恐れた。そこで潤州から楚州へ呼び寄せ、李逵にも毒酒を飲ませる。飲み終えた後で初めて実情を告げると、李逵は恨まず、涙を流して「もうよい、もうよい！ 生きては兄貴に仕え、死んでも兄貴の配下の小鬼になるだけだ」と言った。潤州へ戻ってほどなく毒が回って死ぬ。最期には自分の棺を楚州蓼児窪の宋江の墓の傍らに葬り、生死を共にするよう遺言した。天殺星が宋江の忠義の名を全うするため進んで死を受け入れたことは、忠烈の極みであると同時に愚忠の深さも嘆かせる。のちに二人の魂は蓼児窪でたびたび霊験を示し、村人が廟を建て、年々絶えず祀った。黒旋風の一生は、殺伐には旋風の激しさ、孝義には赤子の純真さを持つ。江州の刑場から楚州の毒酒に至る、百八人の中でも特に哀れみと無念を誘う好漢である。

李立，绰号「催命判官」，上应地奴星，梁山泊英雄座次第九十六位。其人本贯江州揭阳岭.en:
Li Li, the Death-Dealing Judge, corresponds to the Earthly Star of Servitude and ranks ninety-sixth among Liangshan's heroes. Originally from the Jieyang Ridge area near Jiangzhou, he runs a tavern on the ridge, ostensibly making a living from wine. But this is no ordinary business: it is one of the murderous inns dreaded throughout the wandering world. Li Li slips sedative powder into food and drink. When traveling merchants eat and drink there, he drugs them unconscious, robs them, and kills them. The fat become filling for meat buns, the thin are dumped in a ditch, and every possession goes into his pocket. This vicious trade cuts travelers' lives short like a judge of the underworld summoning their souls before their time, earning him his name.

The Jieyang region is said to have three local powers. The first consists of the brothers Mu Hong, the Unrestrained, and Mu Chun, the Lesser Unrestrained, who use their great family wealth to dominate Jieyang Town. The second is Li Li and his murderous inn on Jieyang Ridge. The third is Zhang Heng the Boatman and Zhang Shun the White Streak in the Waves, engaged in illicit dealings on the Xunyang River. These powers keep in close contact and are also friendly with Li Jun the River Dragon and his companions, acting without restraint throughout the region. Li Li is rough and imposing, strong of arm, and accustomed to a sharp knife. He seems simple and straightforward in ordinary dealings, but shows no mercy once he acts: a man with a blade behind his smile, waiting to claim lives.

His path to Liangshan is tied to the episode in which he almost kills Song Jiang. Timely Rain is passing Jieyang Ridge on his way into exile at Jiangzhou for killing Yan Poxi. It is late, and hunger and thirst bring him into Li Li's tavern. Li Li does not recognize him and treats him like any traveler, putting sedative powder in the wine. Song Jiang and his two escort officers drink and collapse, helpless, about to be dragged into the workshop and killed. At that moment Li Jun arrives with Tong Wei and Tong Meng. Long admiring Song Jiang's reputation, Li Jun has been searching for a chance to meet him and happens upon Li Li preparing to butcher him. Recognizing Song Jiang, he cries out in alarm, stops Li Li, and hastily administers an antidote to revive all three. Only then does Li Li learn that his captive is the famous Filial and Righteous Dark Third Brother. Breaking into a cold sweat, he bows and begs forgiveness. Through Li Jun, he now meets Song Jiang and his fellow heroes. Later, Huang Wenbing denounces the seditious poem Song Jiang writes drunk at Xunyang Tower. Condemned to death, he is taken to Jiangzhou's marketplace for execution. Liangshan's heroes throw Jiangzhou into turmoil and rescue Song Jiang and Dai Zong from the execution ground. Li Jun, Zhang Heng, Zhang Shun, Mu Hong, Mu Chun, and other Jieyang heroes support them. Together they gather at White Dragon Temple, attack Wuwei, and capture Huang Wenbing to avenge Song Jiang. Afterward, Li Li abandons his inn's murderous trade and joins this company of Jiangzhou heroes at Liangshan.

After joining, Li Li returns to innkeeping but gives up his evil ways, managing taverns and gathering intelligence for the stronghold. At the Grand Assembly, he takes the ninety-sixth chair as the Earthly Star of Servitude. With Wang Dingliu, the Living Flash, he is assigned the tavern on Liangshan's northern approach. Their duties are to learn military news, receive guests, and welcome heroes coming to join. Like Zhu Gui and Zhu Fu, they serve as Liangshan's eyes and ears beyond the mountain. Though such work takes place away from the battlefield, it is essential to good intelligence and careful defense.

After the court grants amnesty, Li Li serves in the campaigns against Liao, Tian Hu, and Wang Qing. In the fierce southern war against Fang La, as Liangshan loses many heroes, he leaves his tavern duties and fights bravely in the ranks. At Dusong Pass, Li Li, Sun Xin, Gu Dasao, and others disguise themselves as porters, creep up a side path, and set fires at night to scatter the defenders. He then works with Tang Long to capture the enemy general guarding the pass, earning a remarkable victory. Yet his doom awaits in Jiangnan. As the army closes on Fang La's stronghold at Qingxi County, fierce battles follow one another. Li Li is severely wounded in the attack on Qingxi. Treatment fails, and he dies of his injuries in royal service, never returning home. The Death-Dealing Judge once hastened the deaths of countless travelers on Jieyang Ridge; in the end his own blood stains Qingxi and his body is wrapped in a horsehide, a turn of consequence and retribution. After returning, Song Jiang remembers the fallen, and Li Li's sacrifice for the realm wins him the posthumous title Gentleman of Righteous Integrity, honored among Liangshan's martyrs. His life moves from a vicious innkeeper who kills travelers to a man who changes course after the rescue of Song Jiang and follows righteousness. His intelligence work, infiltration of the pass, and arson all bring tangible merit. Dying in the southern campaign, the murderer becomes a commander who gives his life in service: another Liangshan story of abandoning evil and meeting duty with resolve.
李立，绰号「催命判官」，上应地奴星，梁山泊英雄座次第九十六位。其人本贯江州揭阳岭.ja:
李立、異名は「催命判官」。地奴星に応じ、梁山泊の好漢中第九十六位。もとは江州掲陽嶺一帯の出身で、嶺に酒店を開き、酒を売って暮らしていた。しかし普通の商売ではなく、江湖の誰もが恐れる「黒店」である。李立は飲食物に蒙汗薬を忍ばせ、旅商人が酒を飲みに入ると眠らせて財を奪い、命を害した。太った者は肉饅頭の具に、痩せた者は溝へ捨て、財物はすべて懐に入れる。この陰険な稼業で往来の客の命を断つ様子が、冥府で魂を呼び、人を早死にさせる判官に似ることから、「催命判官」の名を得た。

掲陽一帯には「三霸」があるといわれた。一つは掲陽鎮の没遮攔穆弘・小遮攔穆春兄弟で、家の富を頼りに土地を支配する。二つ目が掲陽嶺の黒店で人を害する李立、三つ目が潯陽江で私商をする船火児張横・浪裏白跳張順であった。三霸は互いに通じ合い、混江竜李俊の一味とも親しく、掲陽一帯をはばかりなく横行した。李立は粗豪な姿で腕力もあり、尖刀を使い慣れる。日頃は愚直に見えるが、手を下すときは情け容赦がない。まさに笑顔に刃を隠し、伏して命を狙う男であった。

李立が梁山へ入る縁は、宋江を危うく殺しかけた一件に結ばれる。及時雨の宋江は閻婆惜を殺して江州へ刺配される途中、掲陽嶺を通った。日が暮れ、腹も空き喉も渇いていたため、李立の酒店へ食事に入る。李立は宋江を知らず、普通の旅客と思っていつものように酒へ蒙汗薬を入れた。宋江と二人の護送役人は薬酒を飲んで倒れ、今にも作業場へ引かれて殺されるところだった。ちょうどその時、李俊が童威・童猛と嶺へ来た。宋江の大名を慕い、会おうと探し回っていたところ、李立がその本人を屠ろうとする場に出くわしたのである。李俊は宋江を認めて驚き、慌てて李立を制し、解毒薬を飲ませて三人を蘇らせた。捕らえたのが名高い孝義黒三郎だと知った李立は冷汗を流し、平伏して詫びる。こうして李俊の縁で宋江ら豪傑と知り合った。のちに宋江は潯陽楼で酔って反詩を書き、黄文炳に告発され、死罪となって江州の市曹へ斬首に送られる。梁山の好漢が江州を騒がせて刑場を襲い、宋江と戴宗を救った。李俊・張横・張順・穆弘・穆春ら掲陽の豪傑も力を合わせて援護し、白竜廟に集った後、無為軍を攻めて黄文炳を捕らえ、宋江の大仇を討つ。事が済むと李立は黒店の稼業を捨て、江州の好漢たちと共に梁山の仲間になった。

入山後、李立は元の酒店の仕事に戻るが、悪を改め、山寨の酒店管理と情報収集に専念した。大聚義では「地奴星」として第九十六の椅子に座り、「活閃婆」王定六と共に北山路の酒店を任される。軍情を探り、客を迎え送りし、入山を望む好漢を受け入れる、耳目と門戸の役目である。朱貴・朱富と同じく、山の外へ伸びた梁山の見張りであった。戦場での仕事ではないが、消息に通じ、防備を整えるうえで欠かせない役目である。

朝廷の招安後、李立は大軍に従って遼を征し、田虎を討ち、王慶を平らげ、軍中で働いた。方臘への南征では江南の激戦で梁山の好漢が多数失われ、李立も酒店の本業を離れて自ら勇敢に戦う。独松関の攻略では孫新・顧大嫂らと人足に変装し、小道から密かに関へ上り、夜に火を放って敵軍を驚かせた。さらに湯隆と力を合わせて守将を捕らえ、奇功を立てる。しかし最期は江南で待っていた。大軍が方臘の本拠、清渓県へ迫って悪戦を重ねる中、李立は清渓攻略で重傷を負う。手当てを受けても薬は効かず、傷が癒えぬまま王事に殉じ、故郷へ生還できなかった。かつて掲陽嶺で多くの旅人の命を急がせた催命判官は、最後に自ら清渓を血に染め、馬革に包まれる。一つの因果ともいえよう。宋江の凱旋後、戦没の将士を追念し、李立は殉国の功で義節郎に追封され、梁山の英烈として祀られた。黒店で人を害した凶徒が、宋江救出の一件を経て悪を捨て、義に従う。店を守って敵情を探り、関へ忍んで放火した功は確かで、南征で身を失って殉国の将となった。悪から善へ転じ、義のために赴く、梁山らしい江湖の結末である。

李应，郓州人氏，原是李家庄的庄主，那庄子坐落在独龙冈前，与祝家庄、扈家庄鼎足而立.en:
Li Ying is a native of Yunzhou and originally lord of Li Family Manor, standing before Lone Dragon Ridge alongside Zhu Family Manor and Hu Family Manor. Bound in an offensive and defensive alliance, they are known as the Three Manors of Lone Dragon Ridge. Li Ying is wealthy and has many retainers, while his own martial skill is formidable. He is adept with an iron-shafted steel spear and carries five throwing knives hidden on his back. Released unexpectedly in battle, these can kill within a hundred paces and never miss, a deadly mastery of concealed weapons. With an eagle's nose, hawk's eyes, pale yellow complexion, full beard, and imposing frame, he has exceptional presence. His agility, courage, and raptor-like gaze lead the wandering world to call him Li Ying, the Sky-Swooping Eagle. A righteous man of great reputation around Lone Dragon Ridge, he flies the banner of Li Family Manor before his estate, and visiting heroes all respect him.

Li Ying's joining Liangshan is closely tied to the three assaults on Zhu Family Manor. It begins when Shi Qian steals the inn's crowing rooster and causes a disturbance. He, Yang Xiong, and Shi Xiu are passing through, and Zhu Manor captures him. Unable to find another solution, Shi Xiu and Yang Xiong appeal to Li Ying. As an ally of the Zhu family, he first writes a letter and sends his deputy Du Xing to ask for Shi Qian's release. But Zhu Biao, one of the three Zhu sons, is arrogant: he refuses the prisoner, tears the letter apart, and answers with abuse. Enraged, Li Ying arms himself, mounts, and leads his retainers against Zhu Biao. After more than ten exchanges, Zhu Biao feigns defeat, flees, and shoots a surprise arrow into Li Ying's arm. Li Ying returns to his manor in pain to recover. With no one left to petition, Yang Xiong and Shi Xiu go to Liangshan for help, setting in motion Song Jiang's three attacks and the bloody conquest of Lone Dragon Ridge. Now estranged from the Zhu family and wounded by its treachery, Li Ying closes his gates under the pretext of illness. He will not help Zhu Manor, but cannot openly side with Liangshan either, and waits to see what happens.

After Song Jiang takes Zhu Family Manor by stratagem, Hu Manor submits, and the bloody battle for the ridge is won, he recognizes Li Ying as a hero worth recruiting. But Li Ying has an estate he cannot easily abandon and may be reluctant to become an outlaw. Song Jiang therefore devises a plan. He has men pose as local constables, accuse Li Ying of secretly aiding Liangshan, and 'arrest' him along with Du Xing. On the road, other Liangshan heroes pose as bandits and 'rescue' them to the mountain. Meanwhile, men move the Li estate's household and possessions to Liangshan and burn down the manor, cutting off his way home. With his property reduced to ash and the authorities apparently after him, Li Ying has nowhere to go. In helpless resignation, he joins wholeheartedly with Du Xing. This ruse to recruit Li Ying resembles the scheme used on Qin Ming: Song Jiang resorts to manipulation to gain talent. Though close to forcing an innocent man into outlawry, it brings Liangshan a capable warrior who also knows how to manage wealth.

At the Grand Assembly, Li Ying ranks eleventh among the Heavenly Stars as the Heavenly Star of Wealth. Having managed a large estate, he is experienced in landholding, provisions, money, and careful accounts. Song Jiang assigns him and Chai Jin to oversee Liangshan's finances and supplies. As one of its chief household and financial managers, he holds a crucial position. Whenever war comes, his steel spear and five throwing knives also win merit in battle. Able in offense and defense, he combines administrative and martial talent.

After the amnesty, Li Ying follows Song Jiang against Liao, Tian Hu, and Wang Qing, then south against Fang La. Fighting across the land, his knives and spear claim many victories, yet he himself remains safe, one of the few Liangshan commanders to survive and reach a peaceful old age. On returning after Fang La's defeat, he is appointed military commander of Yunzhou in Zhongshan Prefecture. But long hardship, the loss of his brothers, and the ascendancy of treacherous officials have taught him that honors are uncertain and office is dangerous. He has no attachment to rank and soon resigns. Returning to Lone Dragon Ridge, he restores his lands and household and again becomes the area's wealthy manor lord. With his old deputy Du Xing, he lives at ease among woods and springs, enjoying his remaining years in prosperity: one of the few happy endings in Water Margin. From manor lord to keeper of Liangshan's treasury, then retired country gentleman, the Sky-Swooping Eagle is brave yet able to preserve what matters, skilled in both war and trade. He keeps himself clear of danger and finds a rare measure of quiet composure amid Liangshan's largely tragic fate.
李应，郓州人氏，原是李家庄的庄主，那庄子坐落在独龙冈前，与祝家庄、扈家庄鼎足而立.ja:
李応は鄆州の人で、もとは李家荘の主であった。荘は独竜岡の前にあり、祝家荘・扈家荘と鼎立して攻守同盟を結び、「独竜岡三荘」と呼ばれた。李応は家産が豊かで荘客も多く、自身も武芸に優れる。渾鉄の点鋼槍を熟練して使い、さらに背には五口の飛刀を隠した。陣中で不意に放てば百歩以内の敵を外さず倒す、恐るべき暗器の絶技である。鷲のような鼻、鷹のような目、薄黄色の肌、頬髯を備えた堂々たる体は威風に満ちる。身軽で勇猛、視線は鷹隼のようなため、江湖の人は「撲天雕李応」と呼んだ。義を重んじ、独竜岡一帯で名望があり、荘前の「李家荘」の旗を見た往来の豪客は皆敬服した。

李応の入山は「三打祝家荘」の大戦と深く結びつく。初めに時遷が祝家店の時を告げる雄鶏を盗み、騒動を引き起こした。楊雄・石秀・時遷の三人が通り掛かった際のことで、時遷は祝家荘に捕らえられる。石秀と楊雄は手立てがなく、李応に仲裁を求めた。祝家とは同盟関係にあったので、李応はまず書状を認め、副荘主の杜興を使いに送って時遷の返還を願う。ところが三傑の一人、祝彪は傲慢で、釈放しないばかりか書状を引き裂き、悪口を返した。李応は怒り、自ら武装して馬に乗り、荘客を率いて祝彪と戦う。十数合の末、祝彪は敗走を装い、不意の矢で李応の腕を射た。李応は痛みに耐えて荘へ帰り、養生する。頼る先を失った楊雄と石秀は梁山へ援兵を求め、宋江の三度の攻撃と独竜岡の激戦へつながった。李応は祝家への恨みと不意の矢傷から病を口実に門を閉ざし、祝家を助けず、かといって公然と梁山に付くこともできず、様子を見守った。

宋江が計略で祝家荘を破り、扈家荘も帰順して独竜岡の血戦が終わると、李応が英雄であることは承知していたが、家業を捨て難く、容易には落草しないとも考えた。そこで一計を案じる。手下を州の役人に変装させ、李応が梁山と内通して賊を助けたと偽って、副荘主の杜興もろとも「逮捕」する。道の途中で別の好漢を強盗に扮させ、二人を「救って」山へ連れてきた。その間に李家荘の家人と家財をすべて梁山へ移し、荘を焼いて帰路を断つ。家業は灰となり、官府にも追われる身だと思い込んだ李応は、進退に窮して諦め、杜興と共に仲間入りする。この「李応を賺す」筋は秦明への計略と似ており、人材を得るための宋江の権術である。善良な者を追い込むに近い手段ながら、武に長け財務もこなす好漢を梁山へ迎えることになった。

大聚義の際、李応は天罡第十一位、天富星に列した。大荘主として田産の経営、銭糧の調達、細かな計算に慣れていたため、宋江は柴進と共に山寨の銭糧を管理させる。梁山の「内の主」であり、帳簿と財務を預かる総頭領の一人として重要な位置を占めた。戦となれば鋼槍と五口の飛刀で敵を倒して功を立て、攻守に向き、文武を兼ね備えていた。

招安後、李応は宋江と遼を征し、田虎・王慶を破り、さらに方臘を討った。南北を転戦し、飛刀と点鋼槍で多くの敵を倒しながら、自身は無事を保つ。梁山では珍しく陣中で死なず、安らかな老後を得た将である。方臘平定後の叙勲で中山府鄆州都統制を授けられたが、長い苦難、兄弟たちの衰亡、奸臣の横行を見て、功名が守り難く官界が危険なことを知っていた。官位に執着せず、ほどなく辞職して帰郷する。独竜岡で田園と家業を立て直し、再び一帯の富裕な荘主となった。昔の副荘主杜興と共に林泉に遊び、豊かな余生を安らかに終える、水滸の結末では数少ない円満である。独竜岡の荘主から水泊の財務頭領となり、辞官隠退して郷里の富翁へ戻った撲天雕は、勇がありながら守ることもでき、戦にも商にも長けていた。身を全うして害を遠ざけ、悲しみの多い梁山の結末の中に、独自の安穏と落ち着きを得た。

青眼虎李云，沂水县人氏，原是沂水县里一名都头。此人本事不弱，生得身长七尺，淡黄面.en:
Li Yun, the Blue-Eyed Tiger, comes from Yishui County, where he serves as a constable. A capable man, he stands seven chi tall, with a pale yellow face and a short beard along his cheeks. His most unusual feature is his eyes: blue-green at the corners, with a faint green gleam in the pupils. Seeing this light and knowing his skill with fists and staff, people of the wandering world name him the Blue-Eyed Tiger. As constable, he handles arrests and patrols in the county. He favors a heavy chopping blade but can also use a broadsword or twin blades; he has some martial learning and knowledge of medicines. By status he is a dutiful official drawing government pay and catching thieves for the magistrate, not an outlaw by origin. He also has one famous pupil, Li Kui the Black Whirlwind, who learned some spear, staff, and unarmed skills from him as a child in Yishui. Li Kui therefore often calls him Master, a bond that lays the groundwork for a later episode.

Li Yun's joining Liangshan begins with Li Kui's journey to fetch his mother and his tiger killing on Yi Ridge. Song Jiang sends Li Kui back to Yishui to bring his old mother to the stronghold for a comfortable life. He carries her, blind, to Yi Ridge. When she grows terribly thirsty, he goes for water, and a tiger devours her in his absence. Li Kui kills four tigers in his rage, causing a stir throughout Yishui. Elder Cao and his companions coax the story out of him, identify him as Liangshan's Black Whirlwind, and seek to capture him for a reward while sending urgent word to the county office. The magistrate orders Li Yun to take thirty soldiers and escort Li Kui to the prefecture. But Liangshan has prepared: Zhu Gui and Zhu Fu put sedatives in the drinks at a roadside tavern, knocking out Li Yun's officers. Only Li Yun, who has not drunk the wine, remains unaffected. He draws his blade and fights them. His skill lets him hold his own against Zhu Fu and the others together. Li Kui cannot bear to hurt his former teacher, and Zhu Fu pleads earnestly with him. Li Yun finally realizes they all belong to Liangshan. His officers are drugged, he has no home to return to with his family, and no way forward or back. He steels himself, abandons his Yishui office, and joins Zhu Gui, Zhu Fu, and Li Kui at Liangshan. This dutiful constable becomes an outlaw largely because the heroes trick and pressure him into it.

Once Li Yun joins, his official background and some knowledge of crafts and construction make him useful away from charges and assaults. He is usually assigned to building and repairs, taking care of houses and camps, a steady and practical man. At the Grand Assembly, he ranks ninety-seventh among the Earthly Stars as the Star of Observation. Along with Tang Long, Tao Zongwang, and others, he supervises construction of Liangshan's buildings, a useful officer in the stronghold. In the major battles that twice defeat Tong Guan and thrice defeat Gao Qiu, he also does his part without shrinking back.

After the amnesty, Li Yun follows Song Jiang's army north and south, serving against Liao, Tian Hu, Wang Qing, and Fang La in Jiangnan. His life ends in fierce fighting at Shezhou. Wang Yin, Fang La's minister of war, is there: a warrior called the Rival of Zhang Fei, armed with a steel spear and mounted on a fine horse, of truly exceptional skill. As Liangshan's forces enter the city, they meet Wang Yin trying to break out. Li Yun bravely advances on foot with his blade to stop him. But one man is mounted and the other on the ground; Wang Yin's horse is fast and his spear faster. Within a few exchanges, he charges and knocks Li Yun underfoot, trampling him to death amid the fighting. His companion Shi Yong, the Stone General, dies beneath Wang Yin's horse that same day. Li Yun's tiger-related case in Yishui has led him into outlawry: half his life stable, half wandering. In the end he neither passes peacefully in meditation nor receives official rank, but becomes a wronged soul among blades beneath Shezhou's walls. Quietly extinguished under the name of the Earthly Star of Observation, he is another hero denied a peaceful end.
青眼虎李云，沂水县人氏，原是沂水县里一名都头。此人本事不弱，生得身长七尺，淡黄面.ja:
青眼虎の李雲は沂水県の人で、もとは同県の都頭であった。腕は悪くなく、身長七尺、淡黄色の肌に短い頬髯を蓄える。特に変わっていたのは目で、目尻は青く、瞳にはかすかに碧色が透けた。その青い光と拳棒の腕を見た江湖の人が「青眼虎」と呼んだ。都頭として県の捕縛や巡警を掌り、大砍刀を好むが、朴刀も双刀も扱えた。武芸に通じ、薬の知識も多少持つ。身分は官の俸禄を食み、知県のため賊を捕らえる実直な役人で、もとから緑林の出ではない。名高い弟子も一人いて、それが黒旋風の李逵である。李逵は幼い頃、沂水で李雲に槍棒や拳脚を習ったため、しばしば「師父」と呼ぶ。この師弟の縁が、後の事件の伏線となる。

李雲の入山は、李逵が母を迎えに戻り、沂嶺で虎を殺した一件に始まる。宋江は李逵に老母を山寨へ連れて来て幸せに暮らさせるよう言い、李逵は盲目の母を背負って沂嶺へ着いた。母がひどく喉を渇かせたため水を探しに行くと、その間に母は山の虎に食われてしまう。怒った李逵が四頭の虎を殺し、沂水県を騒がせた。曹太公らが虎退治の話を聞き出して梁山の黒旋風だと見抜き、褒賞を得ようと捕らえて県役所へ急報する。知県は李雲に兵三十人を付け、李逵を州へ護送させた。しかし梁山はすでに手を打っていた。朱貴と朱富が途中の酒店で蒙汗薬を使い、李雲の部下を眠らせる。酒を飲まなかった李雲だけは無事で、刀を提げて皆と戦った。さすがに腕があり、朱富ら数人を一人で相手にしても引けを取らない。李逵は昔の師を傷つけるに忍びず、朱富も必死に説得する。皆が梁山の一味だと悟った李雲は、部下は全員倒され、家族と帰る先もなく、進退に窮した。覚悟を決めて沂水の官身を捨て、朱貴・朱富・李逵と梁山に入る。実直な都頭が落草したのは、半ば好漢たちの計略と圧力に押されたためであった。

李雲は公門の出で、工芸や建築にも通じていたため、入山後はもっぱら突撃させるより、建築や修繕、家屋や営寨の世話を任されることが多かった。堅実で使いどころのある人物である。大聚義で座次が定まると、地煞の地察星として第九十七の椅子に座り、湯隆・陶宗旺らと梁山泊の家屋建造を監督する、有用な将校となった。童貫を二度、高俅を三度破る大戦でも、皆と共に力を尽くし、退かなかった。

招安後は宋江の大軍と南北を征し、遼・田虎・王慶を平定、江南の方臘討伐へと働き続ける。命を落としたのは歙州の激戦だった。城には方臘配下の兵部尚書、王寅がいた。「賽張飛」と呼ばれ、鋼槍を使って名馬に乗る、並外れた武芸の持ち主である。梁山軍が城内へ攻め入ると、王寅が道を奪って突破しようとしていた。李雲は勇を頼みに刀を持って徒歩で進み、阻もうとする。しかし一方は馬上、一方は徒歩。王寅の馬は速く槍は鋭く、数合のうちに騎馬で突っ込み、李雲を地面へ倒して乱軍の中で踏み殺した。同じ日に王寅の馬下で死んだ仲間には、石将軍の石勇もいる。沂水の虎の事件から計略で落草した青眼虎は、半生を安定の中、半生を漂泊に過ごした。最後は坐化するでも叙官されるでもなく、歙州城下の刀槍の中で一縷の冤魂となる。地察星の名のもと静かに没した、また一人、安らかな最期を得られなかった好漢である。

李忠者，濠州定远人氏也。其人原是一个江湖卖艺之人，平日间使枪弄棒，撂地卖膏药为生.en:
Li Zhong comes from Dingyuan in Haozhou. Originally a wandering performer, he makes his living demonstrating spear and staff techniques and selling medicinal plasters on the street. Traveling from place to place, he survives on these modest skills. He once kills a tiger during his travels and earns the name Tiger-Slaying General. Impressive though it sounds, he is really an ordinary staff performer and medicine seller, with only middling martial ability. Compared with Wu Song, who kills a tiger bare-handed on Jingyang Ridge, he falls far short. The grand name thus somewhat exceeds the reality, reflecting the boastful habits of itinerant performers.

Li Zhong appears in the second and third chapters of Water Margin. Shi Jin, the Nine-Tattooed Dragons, leaves Shi Family Village in Huayin to search for his teacher Wang Jin in Guanxi. Along the way he finds Li Zhong selling plasters and displaying his weapons. Li Zhong is Shi Jin's first teacher: as a child, Shi Jin learned his earliest spear and staff routines from him, before gaining real mastery under Wang Jin, instructor to the imperial army of eight hundred thousand. Recognizing his old teacher, Shi Jin invites him to drink. At a wine house in Weizhou they meet Garrison Officer Lu Da. While the three drink and talk in a private room, a woman's crying from next door disturbs them. Lu Da summons her and learns that the singer Jin Cuilian and her father have been abused by Butcher Zheng, the local Bully of the West, who has also falsely accused them of debt. Furious, Lu Da wants to collect money to send them home. He contributes five taels of silver and asks Shi Jin and Li Zhong for more. Shi Jin generously gives ten taels, but Li Zhong searches his clothes and produces only two. Seeing his stinginess, Lu Da says, 'Another man who cannot give freely!' He throws the two taels back and refuses them. This incident lays bare the performer's petty thrift and reluctance to part with money, leaving an indelible mark on his character.

Later, Lu Da kills Butcher Zheng with three punches and becomes a fugitive; Li Zhong and Shi Jin also go their separate ways. Li Zhong drifts to Peach Blossom Mountain, where his measure of martial skill allows him to become an outlaw leader. He and Zhou Tong, the Little Conqueror, serve as first and second chiefs, gathering followers and robbing from their mountain stronghold. After leaving Mount Wutai, Lu Zhishen passes through and meets them again, staying several days. He finds them narrow-minded bandits and miserly hosts. On leaving, he bundles up their gold and silver drinking vessels and walks down the mountain, leaving Li Zhong and Zhou Tong staring angrily, powerless to stop him. The episode once again highlights Li Zhong's stinginess.

Li Zhong remains an outlaw on Peach Blossom Mountain for a long time. Later, in the events leading to the union of the three mountains and the attack on Qingzhou, Huyan Zhuo besieges Twin Dragon, Peach Blossom, and White Tiger mountains. Isolated and unable to hold out, Li Zhong and Zhou Tong send to Liangshan for help. Song Jiang arrives with a great force, coordinating attacks from inside and outside to take Qingzhou and kill Prefect Murong. All the heroes of the three mountains then merge with Liangshan, and Li Zhong and Zhou Tong leave Peach Blossom Mountain to join them.

At Liangshan's Grand Assembly, the Heavenly and Earthly ranks are fixed. Li Zhong takes the eighty-sixth chair as the Earthly Star of Remoteness, assigned to guarding central command and the stronghold and awaiting orders. With spear and staff, he can mount a horse and fight, but remains an ordinary general with no especially notable military achievements, usually serving as part of the main force.

After the amnesty, Li Zhong serves Song Gongming against Liao, Tian Hu, and Wang Qing. The southern campaign against Fang La brings terrible fighting and countless casualties among Liangshan's leaders. Li Zhong fights the enemy around Shezhou and Yuling Pass and is killed by stray arrows and the tumult of battle, dying in Jiangnan without returning. From street performances in Dingyuan and the rejected silver in Weizhou to outlawry at Peach Blossom Mountain and allegiance to Liangshan, the Tiger-Slaying General's path ends in the Fang La campaign. His skills may be ordinary and his conduct miserly, but he still follows the greater cause and dies in service. His place among the 108 is the final resting point of a life spent wandering.
李忠者，濠州定远人氏也。其人原是一个江湖卖艺之人，平日间使枪弄棒，撂地卖膏药为生.ja:
李忠は濠州定遠の人。もとは江湖の旅芸人で、日頃は槍棒を演じ、路上で膏薬を売って暮らした。四方を漂い、ささやかな腕で糊口をしのぐ。かつて旅先で虎を一頭倒したことから、「打虎将」の異名を得た。勇ましい呼び名だが、実際は普通の棒術と薬売りの人で、武芸も並程度である。景陽岡で素手で虎を殺した武松とは、はるかに隔たりがあった。「打虎将」の名はいささか実を越え、江湖の芸人が誇張を好む気質も表している。

李忠の登場は『水滸伝』の第二回、第三回に当たる。九紋竜の史進が華陰県史家村を出て、師の王進を関西へ探しに行く途中、膏薬を売って槍棒を演じる李忠に出会った。実は李忠は史進の最初の師である。幼い史進はまず李忠からいくつかの槍棒を習い、後に八十万禁軍教頭の王進に師事して本当の腕を得た。旧師を認めた史進は酒に誘い、二人は渭州の酒楼で提轄の魯達と出会う。三人が小部屋で飲み語っていると、隣の女の泣き声が酒興を妨げた。魯達が呼んで尋ねると、歌売りの金翠蓮父娘が、地元の悪霸「鎮関西」鄭屠に奪われ虐げられ、そのうえ借金をしたと偽られているという。怒った魯達は帰郷のために銀を集めようと、自ら五両を出し、史進と李忠にも求める。史進は気前よく十両を出すが、李忠は身の回りを探してわずか二両を取り出した。魯達はその吝嗇を見て「こいつも気前の悪い男だ」と言い、二両を投げ返して受け取らなかった。この「銀を投げ返す」場面は、芸人の細かな勘定と金を惜しむ小家の気質を鋭く描き、李忠の消えない印象となった。

その後、魯達は鄭屠を三拳で殺して江湖へ逃れ、李忠と史進も別れる。李忠は桃花山へ流れ着き、多少の腕を買われて落草し、山寨の主となった。小覇王の周通と大頭領・二頭領を務め、山を占めて強盗を働き、緑林に仲間を集める。五台山を離れた魯智深が桃花山を通ると、二人に再会して数日滞在した。だが盗賊としても器量が狭く、客へのもてなしもけちだと嫌い、出発時に山寨の金銀の酒器をまとめて持ち去る。李忠と周通は怒って見送るほかなく、ここでも李忠の吝嗇が描かれた。

李忠は桃花山で長く賊を続ける。後に三山聚義と青州攻略へ至る頃、呼延灼が兵を率いて二竜山・桃花山・白虎山を討った。桃花山は孤立して支えきれず、李忠と周通は梁山へ救援を求める。宋江が大軍で到着し、内外から呼応して青州を破り、慕容知府を斬った。三山の好漢はすべて梁山へ合流し、李忠と周通も桃花山を捨てて水泊の仲間となった。

梁山の大聚義で天罡地煞の座次が定まると、李忠は地僻星として第八十六の椅子に座る。中軍や山寨の守備などを担当し、命令を待った。槍棒を使い、陣前で馬に乗って戦うこともできるが、結局は普通の将で、目立った戦功はなく、多くは大隊の一員として従軍した。

招安後、李忠は宋公明に従って遼・田虎・王慶を征し、軍中で働いた。方臘への南征は悪戦となり、梁山頭領に数知れぬ死傷者を出す。李忠も歙州や昱嶺関一帯で方臘軍と戦い、流れ矢と乱戦によって江南に戦死し、生還できなかった。定遠の旅芸、渭州での銀、桃花山の落草、梁山への帰順を経た打虎将は、方臘征討に没する。武芸は平凡で振る舞いはけちでも、大義に従って国に殉じた好漢であることは変わらない。百八人の列に入ったことが、江湖を漂った一生の行き着く先であった。

林冲，绰号「豹子头」，东京汴梁人氏。其原为东京八十万禁军枪棒教头，掌教军中枪棒武.en:
Lin Chong, Leopard Head, comes from Bianliang, the eastern capital. He originally teaches spear and staff to the imperial army of eight hundred thousand, instructing soldiers in weapon skills. With a leopard-like head, round eyes, broad jaw, tiger whiskers, and a height of eight chi, he resembles Zhang Yide, the fierce general of the Three Kingdoms, and thus earns his nickname. His martial ability is exceptional, especially with the spear. His long serpent spear moves with miraculous skill, and he is also adept with the staff, one of the finest fighters in the capital. Upright and law-abiding, he lives happily with his wife, Lady Zhang, and his father-in-law, Instructor Zhang. He has no wish to become an outlaw.

His misfortunes begin with Gao Qiu and his son. Gao Qiu's adopted son, Young Master Gao, harasses Lin Chong's wife at the Yue Temple. Lin Chong arrives but swallows his anger before Gao Qiu's power. Young Master Gao becomes lovesick, and Gao Qiu conspires with his confidant Lu Qian to frame Lin Chong. First they lure him into buying a treasured sword, then induce him to carry it into White Tiger Hall, a restricted military command chamber where unauthorized entry is punishable by death. Accusing him of entering armed with intent to assassinate, Gao Qiu has him tattooed and exiled to Cangzhou. Before leaving, Lin Chong fears implicating his wife, writes a divorce letter, and bids Lady Zhang a sorrowful farewell.

On the road, escort officers Dong Chao and Xue Ba accept Lu Qian's bribe and plan to murder Lin Chong in Wild Boar Forest. Fortunately, Lu Zhishen the Tattooed Monk has secretly followed them. He rescues Lin Chong, beats the escorts, and protects him on the way to Cangzhou. There Lin Chong is assigned to guard the army's forage depot. Gao Qiu and his son still will not relent, sending Lu Qian, Fu An, and others to burn the depot on a snowy night and kill him. But the snow collapses his hut, and he takes temporary shelter in the Mountain God Temple, escaping the fire. Believing him dead, Lu Qian and the others gloat outside the temple, revealing their entire plot. Lin Chong hears everything. Old hatred and new fury erupt together: he opens the doors and kills Lu Qian, Fu An, and the camp officer, then goes to Liangshan in the snowy night. The Mountain God Temple episode, tracing his change from endurance to eruption, is one of Water Margin's most gripping scenes.

When Lin Chong comes to Liangshan, Wang Lun is chief. Narrow-minded and afraid that Lin Chong's superior skill will cost him his position, he raises every obstacle, demanding a pledge of criminal allegiance before admitting him. Later, Chao Gai, Wu Yong, Gongsun Sheng, and their four companions come after the Birthday Tribute plot is exposed. Wang Lun also tries to turn them away. Wu Yong's words provoke Lin Chong's long-simmering resentment. He kills Wang Lun, the White-Robed Scholar, and gives Chao Gai the first chair, transforming the stronghold. This overthrow marks Liangshan's change from a small, constricted band to a broad and growing cause, making Lin Chong a true founder of its greatness.

At Liangshan, Lin Chong's courage is unmatched. When the 108 gather and take their ranks, he occupies the sixth chair as the Heavenly Star of Heroism and one of the Five Tiger Generals, commanding cavalry. He fights in the vanguard in every campaign. At Zhu Family Manor he captures Hu Sanniang alive. In attacks on Zengtou Town and Gaotangzhou, the defeat of the Linked Cavalry, the two victories over Tong Guan, and the three over Gao Qiu, he charges into the fiercest fighting. Wherever his long serpent spear goes, enemy generals scatter; he is truly a match for ten thousand men.

After the amnesty, Lin Chong follows Song Jiang against Liao, boldly leading the assault that breaks the enemy's celestial formation and earning considerable merit. Against Tian Hu and Wang Qing, he commands troops as one of the Five Tiger Generals and wins repeated victories. The southern campaign against Fang La brings perilous terrain and grievous losses among Liangshan's brothers. Lin Chong continues fighting, killing generals and earning honors. But after Fang La is subdued, as the army prepares to return to court, he suddenly suffers a paralytic stroke. Unable to accompany the army to the capital, he must remain at Six Harmonies Temple in Hangzhou, where Song Jiang entrusts his care to Wu Song nearby. Bedridden for six months, he dies there of the incurable paralysis before reaching old age. That such a hero, once instructor to eight hundred thousand imperial troops, should die of paralysis in a monastery is cause for endless sorrow.

Lin Chong begins as a dutiful, law-abiding general. Only the endless persecution of Gao Qiu and his son destroys his household, separates him from his wife, and sends him into military exile and repeated mortal peril, until he finally climbs the mountain on a snowy night to become an outlaw. Endurance reaches its limit and becomes resistance. He kills Wang Lun, establishes Chao Gai, and helps found Liangshan's great cause; after amnesty, he wins countless merits in campaigns north and south. Yet the world never truly accepts him. He dies in illness, leaving desolation behind. The name Leopard Head Lin Chong, with his life of burdens borne, humiliation endured, and blazing grief, forms one of Water Margin's most moving biographies. A thousand years later, readers still close the book with a long sigh.
林冲，绰号「豹子头」，东京汴梁人氏。其原为东京八十万禁军枪棒教头，掌教军中枪棒武.ja:
林冲、異名は「豹子頭」。東京汴梁の人。もとは東京八十万禁軍の槍棒教頭で、兵に槍棒の武芸を教えた。豹の頭に丸い目、燕の顎と虎の髯、身長八尺の姿は三国の猛将張翼徳に酷似し、江湖で豹子頭と呼ばれる。武芸は抜群で、特に槍に精通し、丈八蛇矛を神業のように操った。棍棒も得意で、東京第一等の使い手である。正直で身分を守り、妻の張氏とは仲むつまじく、岳父の張教頭と共に安楽に暮らしていた。もとより落草の心はなかった。

災いは高俅父子から起こる。高俅の養子、高衙内が岳廟で林冲の妻に絡んだ。駆けつけた林冲は高俅の権勢を恐れ、怒りを飲み込む。高衙内が恋煩いに陥ると、高俅は腹心の陸謙と林冲を陥れる策を立てた。まず宝刀を買わせ、次に刀を持ったまま白虎節堂へ誘い込む。そこは軍機の重地で、勝手に入れば死罪だった。「刀を持って白虎堂に入り、刺殺を企てた」との罪で、林冲は滄州へ刺配される。出発前、妻を巻き込むまいと離縁状を書き、張氏と別れた。その情景は痛ましい。

護送役人の董超・薛覇は陸謙から賄賂を受け、野猪林で林冲を殺そうとする。しかし花和尚の魯智深が密かに道中を追い、林内で救って役人を打ち、滄州まで護衛した。到着した林冲は軍の飼料庫の番に回されるが、高俅父子はなお諦めず、陸謙・富安らを差し向け、雪夜に庫を焼いて殺そうとした。その夜は風雪が激しく、林冲の草小屋は雪で潰れたため、山神廟へ一時避難していた。それで難を逃れる。林冲が死んだと思う陸謙らは廟の外で得意げに語り、陰謀をすべて漏らした。聞いていた林冲は新旧の恨みを一度に爆発させ、廟門を開いて陸謙・富安・差撥の三人を殺し、雪夜に梁山へ向かう。「風雪の山神廟」は、忍耐から爆発へ転じる林冲を描いた、『水滸伝』でも屈指の緊迫した名場面である。

梁山へ赴いた時、寨主は王倫だった。狭量な王倫は林冲の武芸を恐れ、地位を奪われると考えて、入山には「投名状」が要ると難題を重ねる。後に晁蓋・呉用・公孫勝ら七人も生辰綱智取の発覚で梁山へ来るが、王倫はまた拒もうとした。呉用の言葉に刺激された林冲は、積もった怒りから白衣秀士の王倫を斬り、晁蓋を第一の椅子に据える。ここから梁山の姿は一変した。林冲の王倫討ちは、小から大へ、狭さから広さへ変わる要であり、梁山の事業を開いた功臣といえる。

梁山での林冲の武勇は群を抜く。百八人が聚義して座次を定めると、天雄星として第六の椅子に座り、五虎大将の一人として馬軍を率いた。戦いでは常に前部の猛将である。祝家荘では扈三娘を生け捕りにし、曾頭市・高唐州の攻略、連環馬の撃破、童貫への二勝、高俅への三勝でも敵陣へ突撃した。丈八蛇矛の赴く先で敵将は崩れ、まさに万夫に敵なしであった。

招安後、林冲は宋江と遼を征し、混天象陣を破る戦いでも勇敢に先頭へ立ち、大きな功を得た。続く田虎・王慶征討では五虎将として兵を率いて転戦し、奇功を重ねる。方臘への南征は江南の険悪な戦場となり、梁山兄弟に惨烈な損害を出したが、林冲はなお将を斬って功を立てる。方臘を平定して帰朝しようとした時、突然風癱を患い、半身が動かず、都へ戻れなくなった。宋江は杭州六和寺に残し、近くの武松に世話と養生を頼むほかなかった。半年臥床した末、病は治らず六和寺で没し、長寿には届かなかった。一代の豪傑、八十万禁軍の教頭が、僧寺で麻痺の病に終わるとは、嘆きは尽きない。

林冲はもとは規律を守る良将だった。高俅父子に幾重にも陥れられ、妻と別れ家を失い、刺配され、九死に一生の苦難を経て、ついに雪夜の山へ登り賊となる。極限まで耐えてから立ち上がり、王倫を斬って晁蓋を立て、梁山の大業を開いた。招安後も南北を征して無数の功を立てるが、ついに世に受け入れられず、病を抱えて寂しく終わった。忍辱負重と悲憤の激しさを持つ豹子頭の名と生涯は、『水滸伝』の中でも最も胸を打つ伝となり、千載の後の読者にも本を閉じて長嘆させる。

凌振，绰号「轰天雷」，乃梁山泊一百单八将中地轴星，居地煞之列，梁山好汉总座次第五.en:
Ling Zhen, the Heaven-Shaking Thunder, is Liangshan's Earthly Star of Axis, ranked fifty-second among the 108 heroes. Originally from Yanling, he serves the Song court as deputy commissioner and gunner of the armory. He is the foremost cannon craftsman of his time, a renowned gunner none can equal, which earns him his thunderous name.

Ling Zhen's supreme art lies entirely in cannon. He builds many kinds and fires stone shot as far as fourteen or fifteen li. Where his projectiles strike, mountains seem to collapse, rocks split, and earth and sky shake with terrifying force. His designs include Wind-and-Fire Cannon, Golden Wheel Cannon, and Mother-and-Child Cannon, all astonishingly powerful, intended for siege warfare, breaking formations, and long-range bombardment. A single report sounds like thunder and lightning, terrifying enemies before battle even begins. His name is thus well deserved and known throughout the realm. As deputy armory commissioner, he oversees gunpowder and military equipment while also serving as a gunner. Combining technical administration with martial ability, he is a rare talent in the Song military establishment.

His conflict with Liangshan begins during the imperial campaign against the marsh. Gao Qiu sends Huyan Zhuo with an army, whose Linked Cavalry repeatedly defeats Liangshan. Even after Liangshan's hooked spears break that formation and Huyan Zhuo retreats, he obtains Ling Zhen from the court as a reinforcement. Ordered to accompany the army, Ling Zhen reaches the edge of Liangshan Marsh, sets up cannon opposite the water stronghold, and fires repeated volleys. Three cannon fire together: one shot strikes the stronghold wall, another the small camp by Duckbill Shoal, shaking and alarming all the leaders. Deeply worried by this firepower, Song Jiang consults Wu Yong, and they plan to lure the gunner across the water. Wu Yong sends naval commanders to entice Ling Zhen to pursue them by boat. Unaware of the trap, he crosses, only for Liangshan's naval leaders to overturn his vessel and capture him alive.

Brought bound before the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness, Ling Zhen is personally untied by Song Jiang and treated with honor. Song Jiang explains Liangshan's cause of Heaven's Justice and its wish to gather worthy men. Seeing his generosity and the harmony among the heroes, Ling Zhen changes his mind, bows, and willingly joins. From then on, he oversees the making of cannon and military equipment, giving Liangshan a unique technical skill. With his artillery, the stronghold's armies gain wings, storming cities and camps with new force.

At the Grand Assembly, when the Heavenly and Earthly ranks are fixed, Ling Zhen takes the fifty-second chair as the Earthly Star of Axis. His duty is to manufacture all sizes of signal cannon. He is the only commander among the 108 who specializes in artillery. Though ranked among the Earthly Stars, his responsibility is vital. In assaults on strong defenses and cities, his first cannon shot often seizes the initiative and wins enduring merit.

When Liangshan accepts amnesty and returns to imperial service, Ling Zhen accompanies the army against Liao, then Tian Hu and Wang Qing. Everywhere his cannon support the fighting, battering cities and fortifications and winning repeated honors. When the court orders a campaign against Fang La in Jiangnan, he crosses the river south with Song Jiang. His artillery shows its full value in taking the region's prefectures and counties. Liangshan loses many heroes in the campaign, but Ling Zhen's unique craft helps him preserve his life and survive the fighting.

After Fang La is subdued and the army returns, the court distributes rewards. Ling Zhen's gunnery keeps him in imperial favor. He remains in the capital, again serving in the imperial gunpowder establishment and overseeing cannon manufacture. He reaches a peaceful end in office, one of the more fortunate survivors. His extraordinary art earns fame across the realm; first an enemy commander, he ultimately joins the righteous cause. The thunder of his cannon contains the story of his renown and marks him as Water Margin's unique master of artillery.
凌振，绰号「轰天雷」，乃梁山泊一百单八将中地轴星，居地煞之列，梁山好汉总座次第五.ja:
凌振、異名は「轟天雷」。梁山泊百八人の地軸星で、地煞に属し、全体の座次は第五十二位。もとは燕陵の人で、大宋朝廷の甲仗庫副使兼砲手であった。当時天下第一等の火砲の名工、宋に名高い誰も及ばぬ砲手として、「轟天雷」の名を得た。

凌振の絶技は、すべて「火砲」の二字にある。各種の砲を作り、石弾を遠く十四、五里まで飛ばす。着弾すれば山が崩れ石が裂け、地が動き天が驚くほどの威力を持った。「風火砲」「金輪砲」「子母砲」など多様な砲を製し、いずれも驚異的な力で攻城・破陣・遠距離砲撃に用いる。一発の砲声は雷電のようで、敵は刃を交える前に胆を砕かれる。「轟天雷」は実に名にかなった天下周知の異名であった。甲仗庫副使として軍用火薬と兵器の製造を担当し、砲手の腕も持つ。文武を兼ねた、宋の軍備にとって貴重な技術の臣である。

梁山との対立は、朝廷の水泊討伐に始まる。高俅が呼延灼に兵を率いさせると、連環馬が梁山を幾度も苦しめた。梁山が鉤鎌槍で陣を破って呼延灼を敗走させた後も、呼延灼は朝廷から砲手の凌振を援軍に得る。命を受けて梁山泊の岸へ来た凌振は、水寨の対岸に火砲を据え、連続して撃った。三門が一斉に放たれ、一発は水寨の城壁、一発は鴨嘴灘付近の小寨に当たり、頭領たちは震撼する。宋江は強力な砲火を深く憂え、呉用と相談して凌振を水上へ誘う計を定めた。呉用は水軍頭領に命じ、凌振が兵を率いて渡り追うよう仕向ける。罠と知らず水へ出た凌振は、水軍に船を返され、生け捕りにして山へ連れられた。

忠義堂へ引かれた凌振を、宋江は自ら縄を解いて礼遇した。梁山が替天行道を掲げ、義によって賢才を集める意を詳しく説く。宋江の義気と好漢たちの和やかさを見て心を変えた凌振は、頭を下げ、進んで仲間に加わる。以後は各種の火砲と軍器の製造を掌り、水泊に独自の絶技をもたらした。凌振を得た梁山は、虎に翼を添えたように城や寨を落とし、向かうところに敵なしとなる。

大聚義で天罡地煞の座次が定まると、凌振は地軸星として第五十二の椅子に座った。職掌は「一切の大小号砲の製造」で、百八人の中で唯一、火砲を専門にする頭領である。地煞の位であっても、担う仕事は極めて重要だった。堅陣や城を攻めるたび、砲の一発で先制の勢いを奪い、消えることのない功を立てた。

招安を受けて朝廷へ帰順すると、凌振は大軍とまず遼を征し、続いて田虎・王慶を討った。どこでも砲で援護し、城と砦を崩して奇勲を重ねる。江南の方臘討伐の詔が出ると、宋江と川を渡って南へ行き、州郡を攻略する際に火砲の威力を大いに示した。方臘征討では梁山の好漢が多数失われたが、凌振は火砲の絶技によって身を守り、陣中で死なずに済んだ。

方臘が平定されて軍が戻ると、朝廷は功に応じて賞を授ける。凌振は砲手の技で引き続き重用され、都に留まって火薬局の御営で働き、軍の火砲製造を掌った。任にあるまま安らかな最期を得て、生き残った諸将の中でも良い結末を迎える。絶芸を身に持ち、天下に名を震わせ、初めは敵将、最後は大義に帰した。天を轟かす一声の雷が半生の威名を語る、『水滸伝』の群英にただ一人の火砲の宗師である。

刘唐，绰号「赤发鬼」，应天罡之数，乃天异星临世。其人籍贯东潞州人氏，自小飘荡江湖.en:
Liu Tang, the Red-Haired Devil, is one of the Heavenly Stars, the Heavenly Star of Strangeness incarnate. A native of eastern Luzhou, he has wandered since childhood, wielding a broadsword with exceptional strength and a fiery temper. His face is broad and dark purple, with a cinnabar mark at one temple sprouting black and yellow hairs, and a head of red hair. From a distance he resembles a red-haired demon, which gives him his name. Without home or family, he is a lone hero who intervenes against injustice, though not without roughness and rashness.

Liu Tang enters the story with the taking of the Birthday Tribute, setting the great affair in motion. Secretary Liang of Daming, the northern capital, is sending gold and jewels worth one hundred thousand strings of cash to the eastern capital as a birthday gift for his father-in-law, Grand Preceptor Cai. This is the Birthday Tribute. Learning of the ill-gotten wealth, Liu Tang decides it should be taken and hurries by night to Chao Gai, the Pagoda-Bearing Heavenly King, at Dongxi Village. Exhausted, he falls asleep drunk in the Lingguan Temple. Constable Lei Heng finds him on night patrol, suspects a criminal, binds him, and takes him to Chao Gai's manor. Chao Gai devises a way to redeem him, pretending he is his nephew. But Liu Tang resents the unjust arrest and Lei Heng's taking ten taels from Chao Gai. He pursues with his broadsword to demand the money back and fights Lei Heng for more than fifty exchanges on the road. Wu Yong, the Resourceful Star, arrives and parts them with copper chains. This encounter brings Chao Gai, Wu Yong, and Liu Tang together to plan.

Chao Gai, Wu Yong, Liu Tang, Gongsun Sheng, and the three Ruan brothers—Xiaoer, Xiaowu, and Xiaoqi—then unite. At Chao Gai's manor they swear a blood oath and settle their scheme. With Bai Sheng's help on Huangni Ridge, they disguise themselves as traders selling wine, put sedative powder in the drink, and incapacitate Yang Zhi and the entire tribute escort. They take the gold and jewels and walk away. This is the celebrated taking of the Birthday Tribute, with Liu Tang its original instigator. When the plot is exposed and officials come to arrest them, Song Jiang gives warning. The seven go to Liangshan, overthrow Wang Lun, and establish the stronghold's great cause. Liu Tang becomes one of its founding veterans.

Once established at Liangshan, Liu Tang remains deeply loyal, especially remembering Song Jiang's warning that saved their lives. Later, after Song Jiang's killing of Yan Poxi is exposed, Chao Gai sends Liu Tang to Yuncheng with one hundred taels of gold and a letter of thanks. Song Jiang accepts only one bar and the letter, returning the rest. When constables Zhu Tong and Lei Heng secretly release Song Jiang, Liu Tang and the other heroes remember their kindness. In Liangshan's many subsequent campaigns, he is always bravely at the front, his broadsword making him a fierce infantry commander. At the Grand Assembly, he ranks twenty-first as the Heavenly Star of Strangeness, his high place recognizing both his founding service and his courage.

After the amnesty, Liu Tang follows Song Jiang against Liao, Tian Hu, Wang Qing, and Fang La, fighting north and south without fear of death. The Fang La campaign brings Liangshan its most grievous losses, and Liu Tang dies there too. During the attack on Hangzhou, he eagerly rides ahead alone, seeking first honors by rushing through the gate. But the defenders, seeing Liangshan approach, suddenly drop the portcullis. Heavy as a mountain, it descends before he can rein in his horse. Man and mount are crushed together beneath it, dying instantly within Hangzhou's gate. His terrible death comes before he can even engage the enemy, a bitter loss.

Liu Tang's life begins in the Birthday Tribute plot and ends beneath Hangzhou's gate. Red-haired, purple-faced, and fearsome to behold, he is nevertheless full of courage and warm-hearted loyalty. From Chao Gai's first brotherhood to Song Jiang's leadership, he remains one of Liangshan's most forthright and selfless men. In arms, he has a practiced broadsword and astonishing strength; in honor, he repays kindness and willingly faces fire and boiling water. After returning, Song Jiang summons the souls of the fallen and makes offerings in the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness; Liu Tang's name is among them. This rash but faithful hero begins as an instigator and ends as a martyr to the cause, leaving his own fierce chapter among the 108, remembered in the tales of the wandering world.
刘唐，绰号「赤发鬼」，应天罡之数，乃天异星临世。其人籍贯东潞州人氏，自小飘荡江湖.ja:
劉唐、異名は「赤髪鬼」。天罡の数に応じ、天異星の化身である。東潞州の人で、幼い頃から江湖を漂い、朴刀を使い慣れ、力は人に勝り、性は烈火のようだった。紫黒色の広い顔、鬢の朱砂の痣には黒黄の毛が生え、さらに赤い髪がある。遠くから見ると赤髪の鬼に似るため、この異名を得た。家も妻子もない一人身の好漢で、不正を見れば助けに入るが、粗豪で無鉄砲なところもある。

登場は生辰綱智取の場面で、その大事の発端を作る。北京大名府の梁中書が、十万貫相当の金珠宝物を東京の岳父、蔡太師への誕生祝いに送ろうとしていた。「生辰綱」である。その不義の財を知った劉唐は奪う好機と見て、夜を急ぎ東渓村の托塔天王晁蓋を訪ねた。疲れて霊官廟で酔い潰れていたところ、夜回りの都頭雷横に怪しまれ、縛られて晁蓋の荘へ連行される。晁蓋は機転を利かせて甥だと偽り、金を払って引き取った。しかし劉唐は、理由なく捕らえられ、晁蓋の銀十両まで取られたと怒る。朴刀を持って追い、道で雷横と五十合余り戦った。智多星呉用が来て銅鎖で二人を分け、ようやく収まる。この一件から晁蓋・呉用・劉唐が集まり、策を練ることになった。

続いて晁蓋・呉用・劉唐・公孫勝と、阮小二・阮小五・阮小七の三雄、計七人が晁蓋の荘で血盟し、計画を定める。白勝の助けも得て黄泥岡で酒売りの商人に変装し、酒に蒙汗薬を入れて楊志ら護送隊を全員眠らせ、十万貫の金珠を奪って去った。これが名高い「智取生辰綱」で、劉唐こそ最初に事を提唱した者である。発覚後は官府に追われたが、宋江の知らせで七人は梁山へ上り、王倫を倒して基業を開く。劉唐はこうして山寨の古参、創業を支えた一人となった。

梁山に拠ってからも劉唐は忠実で、特に昔、報せによって命を救った宋江の恩を忘れない。宋江が閻婆惜を殺した件が発覚した後、晁蓋は劉唐に黄金百両と書状を持たせ、鄆城県へ謝礼に遣わした。宋江は金一条と手紙だけ受け取り、残りを返す。都頭の朱仝と雷横が宋江を逃がした恩も、劉唐らは胸に刻んだ。その後の戦いでは朴刀で勇敢に先陣を切り、歩軍の猛将となる。大聚義では天異星として第二十一位に座り、その高い位置は古参の功と実際の勇を示した。

招安後、劉唐は宋江と遼、田虎、王慶、方臘を征し、南北を戦って死を恐れなかった。最も惨烈な損害を出した方臘征討で、彼も命を失う。杭州城を攻めた際、手柄を急いで単騎で城門へ入り、第一の功を取ろうとした。ところが守兵は梁山軍を見て、急いで落とし戸を下ろす。山のように重い戸を前に馬を止めきれず、人馬もろとも下敷きとなり、城門の内側で即死した。敵と刃を交える前の凄惨な死は、嘆かわしく惜しい。

劉唐の一生は生辰綱の智取に始まり、杭州の城門に終わる。赤髪と紫の顔は恐ろしいが、肝胆に満ち、熱い血で人に接した。晁蓋の聚義から宋江の掌寨まで、最も忠直で命を惜しまぬ一人である。武芸では熟れた朴刀と驚くべき力、義気では恩を知って報い、火や湯へも赴く心を持つ。凱旋した宋江が忠義堂で戦没の兄弟の魂を招き祭る時、赤髪鬼の名もそこにあった。無鉄砲ながら忠烈な好漢は、事を起こす者として始まり、義に殉ずる者として終わる。百八人の中に固有の剛烈な一章を残し、江湖の人の語りに長く生きる。

吕方，绰号「小温侯」，乃梁山泊一百单八将中地佐星，居地煞之列，梁山好汉总座次第五.en:
Lu Fang, the Little Marquis, is Liangshan's Earthly Star of Assistance, ranked fifty-fourth among the 108. Originally from Tanzhou, he trades medicinal herbs until the loss of his capital leaves him adrift. He becomes an outlaw and establishes himself as chief of a stronghold.

Lu Fang has one lifelong enthusiasm: he emulates Lu Bu, the Marquis who famously shot a halberd at the camp gate in the Three Kingdoms era. Every part of his costume follows that model. He wears a worked-copper lion helmet, gilded brass armor beneath a scarlet flower-patterned robe, an intricately jeweled belt, and cloud-patterned boots. His favored weapon is a heavenly halberd decorated with a leopard tail and five-colored tassels. In battle he looks imposing, like a young Lu Bu reborn. His dress and halberd technique earn him the name Little Marquis. Marquis of Wen was Lu Bu's title; 'Little' marks a young admirer whose appearance and weapon skills resemble the elder hero's. Lu Fang is spirited, brave, competitive, and adept with his halberd, a young fighter eager to prove himself.

He becomes an outlaw on Duiying Mountain, which has two facing peaks. Taking the eastern summit, he rules a band that raids homes and robs travelers. Then another hero arrives: Guo Sheng, the Rival of Rengui, also wielding a heavenly halberd. Having lost his investment in mercury trading, Guo Sheng turns outlaw on the western peak. Both want sole control, and neither yields. They fight between the mountains every day for more than ten days without a clear victor. In one mounted duel, the leopard tails and tassels on their halberds become tangled and cannot be pulled apart. While they are deadlocked, Song Jiang and his party pass. From high ground, he sees their equal skill and their knotted weapons, and sends Hua Rong to intervene. Little Li Guang draws his bow and strikes the knot with a single arrow, cutting the decorations apart and freeing the halberds. Lu Fang and Guo Sheng are astonished and bow in admiration.

After this shot, the former rivals become acquainted through their fighting. With Song Jiang mediating, they end the contest, turn enemies into friends, and become brothers. They decide to abandon Duiying Mountain altogether and join Song Jiang at Liangshan. The combined party advances in great numbers toward the marsh. Song Jiang is delighted to gain two such skilled halberdiers, and Lu Fang thereafter takes his place among the stronghold's leaders.

At the Grand Assembly, Lu Fang takes the fifty-fourth chair as the Earthly Star of Assistance. With Guo Sheng, he guards the central command tent, standing beneath Song Jiang's great banner. Both wield heavenly halberds, wear similar attire, and possess comparable skills. Stationed to either side of the commander, their two halberds stand like a stern pair of guardian deities, among the most conspicuous figures in Liangshan's headquarters. In war they sometimes protect their chief and sometimes lead assaults, supporting each other and winning considerable merit.

After Liangshan accepts amnesty, Lu Fang serves the army first against Liao, then Tian Hu and Wang Qing, fighting loyally in the north and south. Ordered against Fang La in Jiangnan, he crosses the river with Song Jiang and fights deep in the lands of Wu and Yue. At Black Dragon Ridge, the terrain is treacherous and the enemy fierce. Lu Fang and Guo Sheng fight on without retreat amid the turmoil, but both plunge into a deep ravine and die in royal service, never returning. From rivalry on Duiying Mountain to meeting Song Jiang, joining the marsh brotherhood, and dying in the southern campaign, the Little Marquis ends as a warrior whose body returns wrapped in horsehide, living up to the valor he admired in Lu Bu.

After Song Jiang returns, the court honors the fallen commanders. Lu Fang and the other Liangshan brothers killed in battle receive posthumous offices and temples, where later generations offer incense. He admires the Marquis in youth and gains fame with a halberd, competes at Duiying and joins the brotherhood at the marsh, guards central command and dies in the south. Though ranked among the Earthly Stars, his courage strengthens Liangshan. He is one of Water Margin's spirited young battle commanders.
吕方，绰号「小温侯」，乃梁山泊一百单八将中地佐星，居地煞之列，梁山好汉总座次第五.ja:
呂方、異名は「小温侯」。梁山泊百八人の地佐星で、地煞に属し、全体の座次は第五十四位。もとは潭州の人で、生薬を売る商人だったが、元手を失って江湖に流れ、落草して一寨の主となった。

呂方には生涯を通じた好みがある。呂布のあり方を慕い、装束もすべて、三国時代に轅門で戟を射た温侯呂布に倣った。熟銅の獅子兜をかぶり、金を施した黄銅の鎧に大紅の団花袍を重ね、宝を嵌めた細工の帯、山字雲根の靴を着ける。手には方天画戟を持ち、戟に金銭豹の尾と五色の飾り紐を結んだ。陣前では威風堂々、若い呂布の再来に見える。この姿と戟の技から江湖で「小温侯」と呼ばれた。温侯は呂布の爵号で、「小」は若くして呂布を慕い、武器と装いが似ることを示す。呂方は若い気に満ち、勇敢で勝ち気、熟れた画戟を頼りに強さを競う好漢であった。

落草したのは対影山である。向かい合う二峰のうち東の峰を占め、寨主として屋敷や旅人を襲った。そこへ「賽仁貴」郭盛という、同じ方天画戟を使う好漢が来る。水銀の商売で元手を失い、西の峰に落草したのだった。二人とも対影山の独占を望み、譲らず、毎日二山の間で戦う。十数日も戟を交えて勝負がつかず、ある騎馬戦では双方の豹尾と飾り紐が絡んで引き離せなくなった。膠着しているところを宋江一行が通り掛かる。高所から互角の戟術と絡んだ武器を見た宋江は、花栄に仲裁を命じた。小李広は弓を引き、一矢で結び目を射抜いて豹尾と紐を断ち、二本の戟を分ける。呂方と郭盛は神射に驚き、平伏して服した。

この一射を経て、戦わねば知り合わなかった二人は、宋江の仲立ちで争いをやめ、敵から友、さらに兄弟となる。相談して対影山を捨て、宋江と梁山泊へ赴くことにした。一行は堂々たる隊伍で水泊へ進む。画戟を使いこなす二人の好漢が加わったことに宋江は大喜びし、呂方も以後、山寨の頭領たちに列した。

大聚義で天罡地煞が定まると、呂方は地佐星として第五十四の椅子に座る。郭盛と共に中軍帳前を守り、宋江の大将旗の下に立つ護衛の将となった。武器は共に方天画戟、装束も似て、技量も互角。主将の左右に並ぶ二本の戟は厳かで、梁山中軍でもひときわ目立つ一対の門神のようだった。戦では主帥を守ることも、先陣で敵陣へ入ることもあり、互いに支えて多くの功を立てた。

招安を受けて朝廷へ帰順すると、呂方は大軍とまず遼、次いで田虎・王慶を討ち、南北で命を尽くした。方臘征討の詔が出ると宋江と南へ渡り、呉越の奥で苦戦する。烏竜嶺では地勢が険しく敵も勇猛で、呂方と郭盛は乱軍の中で退かず力戦したが、二人とも深い崖へ落ち、王事に殉じて帰れなかった。対影山の争覇から宋江との出会い、水泊の聚義、南征での殉身へ至った小温侯は、馬革に包まれる結末を迎える。半生にわたり慕った呂布の勇烈な心に背かぬ最期であった。

宋江の凱旋後、朝廷は戦没将を追念し、呂方も他の兄弟と共に贈官と廟を受け、後世の香火に祀られる。若くして温侯を慕い、一戟で名を成し、対影で強さを争い、水泊で義を結び、中軍を守って南国に命を落とした。地煞の列でも、その勇は梁山を強めた。『水滸伝』の群英の中で英姿の輝く若い戦将である。

卢俊义，绰号「玉麒麟」，北京大名府人氏。其为河北三绝，身长一丈，气宇轩昂，膀阔三.en:
Lu Junyi, the Jade Qilin, comes from Daming, the northern capital. Celebrated for three supreme qualities in Hebei, he stands one zhang tall, broad-shouldered and imposing, his body flawless as white jade and his bearing dignified and fearsome. These qualities earn him his elegant name. A wealthy gentleman of the city, he has a great fortune, unmatched staff skill, accomplished riding and archery, and a reputation throughout the wandering world: truly peerless with the cudgel. His household includes his wife, Lady Jia, his trusted steward Li Gu, and a servant, Yan Qing the Wanderer, accomplished in music, dance, wrestling, and crossbow shooting.

Lu Junyi is content with a settled life and has no wish for outlawry. Wu Yong's scheme draws him to the mountain. Song Jiang has long heard his fame and wants to recruit him, so he sends Wu Yong disguised as a fortune-teller to the Lu house in Daming. Wu Yong falsely predicts a bloody calamity within a hundred days, avoidable only by traveling a thousand li southeast. He also instructs Lu Junyi to write four lines of divination verse on the wall. Unaware of the trap, Lu Junyi takes men toward Tai'an to burn incense and avert disaster, passing through Liangshan territory. The heroes meet him in succession: Li Kui, Lu Zhishen, Wu Song, Liu Tang, and others fight him in turn. For all his skill, he is outnumbered and ambushed, then taken to the mountain. Song Jiang treats him respectfully and repeatedly urges him to join, but Lu Junyi asks only to return home.

During the month and more he spends trapped at Liangshan, the verse on his wall becomes his undoing: its hidden message reads 'Lu Junyi rebels.' Li Gu, having an affair with Lady Jia, exploits the opportunity to denounce him for conspiring with Liangshan. Secretary Liang believes the accusation, and Lu Junyi is jailed under sentence of death. Yan Qing survives by begging, shoots his escort officers dead, and rushes to Liangshan for help. Shi Xiu attempts a rescue at the execution ground but cannot prevail alone and is captured too. Song Jiang raises a great army, attacks Daming twice, and takes the city through a night assault by water and fire. Lu Junyi and Shi Xiu are freed, and Li Gu and Lady Jia are killed in vengeance. Only now, disillusioned, does Lu Junyi become a Liangshan outlaw.

Chao Gai's dying words declare that whoever captures the man whose arrow killed him should become Liangshan's lord. In the attack on Zengtou Town, Lu Junyi captures Shi Wengong alive and is thus entitled to leadership. Song Jiang firmly offers him the position, but Lu Junyi repeatedly declines. Later, the two separately attack prefectural cities; Lu Junyi attacks Dongping. Through the outcome of these events, he ultimately takes the second chair beneath Song Jiang as deputy chief, corresponding to the Heavenly Star of Strength, foremost of the Heavenly Stars and second among the 108. He oversees military affairs, administration, and supplies, and often leads a separate force alongside Song Jiang on campaign. Among Liangshan's finest fighters, he excels with staff, spear, and mounted combat. His capture of Shi Wengong strikes fear into the enemy.

After the amnesty, Lu Junyi follows Song Jiang north against Liao. When Liao deploys the Taiyi Celestial Formation, he fights boldly in the front, displays extraordinary power within it, and routs the enemy. Against Tian Hu and Wang Qing, he leads an independent army across Hebei and Huaixi, winning wherever he goes and earning repeated distinction, a true commander of one of Liangshan's armies. In the Fang La campaign, he commands a separate force to take cities, seize land, kill generals, and capture banners. After Shi Jin and others fall at Yuling Pass, Lu Junyi personally leads the main force to break through. Throughout the Jiangnan battles he sets the example and wins the greatest merit, praised with Song Jiang as the twin jewels of command.

After Fang La's defeat, the court appoints him Grand Master of Military Achievement, Pacification Commissioner of Luzhou, and deputy military commander. Yet he cannot escape the treacherous ministers even on his way to office. Cai Jing, Gao Qiu, and others resent the former Liangshan men and arrange an imperial meal laced with mercury. Returning after the meal, Lu Junyi reaches the Huai River at Sizhou. The mercury's effects seize his waist and hips; he cannot control his limbs or stand steadily. He loses his footing, falls into the deep river, and drowns. That the peerless Jade Qilin should die through such treachery is a bitter tragedy.

Lu Junyi begins as a rich, peaceful gentleman, tricked without cause into outlawry and imprisonment. He finally joins Liangshan, where his unmatched martial skill becomes a bulwark of the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness. After the amnesty, he fights north and south with brilliant distinction, commanding independently and honoring the Jade Qilin's name. Yet success brings slander and murder, and he sinks into the Huai, sharing the grave's fate with Song Jiang, Wu Yong, and the others. When Emperor Huizong later honors Liangshan's generals by decree, Lu Junyi is among those posthumously ennobled. His heroic spirit, righteous bearing, and dignity among the leading Heavenly Stars endure in the tale of Water Margin.
卢俊义，绰号「玉麒麟」，北京大名府人氏。其为河北三绝，身长一丈，气宇轩昂，膀阔三.ja:
盧俊義、異名は「玉麒麟」。北京大名府の人。河北の三絶とされ、身長一丈、気宇軒昂、肩幅広く、全身は白玉のように瑕がない。堂々として威風に満ちるため、この美称を得た。北京城の富豪の員外で、家産は豊か、棍棒に敵なく、弓馬に熟達し、武芸の名は江湖に聞こえる。まさに棍棒天下無双であった。家には妻の賈氏、腹心の主管李固、そして「浪子」と呼ぶ僕の燕青がいる。燕青は音曲・歌舞・相撲・弩射と、できぬものがなかった。

盧俊義は安居楽業の人で、落草の意はなかったが、呉用の計で山へ誘われる。宋江はその名声を長く聞き、配下に迎えたいと考え、呉用を占い師に変装させて大名府の盧家へ送った。呉用は百日以内に血の災いがあり、東南千里へ行けば避けられると偽り、壁に四句の卦歌を書かせる。計と知らぬ盧俊義は兵を連れて泰安州へ参詣しようとし、梁山泊の領域を通る。李逵・魯智深・武松・劉唐らが次々に戦いを挑み、武芸に優れていても衆寡敵せず、伏兵にも遭って山へ捕らえられた。宋江は礼遇して何度も入伙を勧めるが、盧俊義はただ帰郷を望んだ。

一月余り山へ留められる間に、壁の四句に隠された「盧俊義反」の四字が災いとなる。主管李固は賈氏と密通しており、機に乗じて梁山と通じ反乱を企てたと訴えた。梁中書は信じ、盧俊義を死囚牢へ入れて斬ろうとする。燕青が道中で物乞いしながら生き延び、護送役を射殺して梁山へ急報した。石秀は刑場で救出を試みるが、独力では支えきれず捕らえられる。宋江が大軍を起こして大名府を二度攻め、水火による夜襲で城を破り、盧俊義と石秀を救う。李固と賈氏を殺して冤仇を晴らすと、心を冷やした盧俊義はついに梁山へ落草した。

晁蓋は臨終に「自分を射殺した者を捕らえた者を梁山泊の主にせよ」と遺言した。曾頭市を攻めた際、盧俊義が史文恭を生け捕りにし、遺言どおりなら寨主となるはずだった。宋江は固く位を譲ろうとするが、盧俊義も繰り返し辞退する。のちに二人は分かれて州城を攻略し、盧俊義は東平府を攻めた。成り行きの末、宋江の下、第二の椅子に座り、梁山副都頭領となる。天罡星に応じ、天罡の首に位置して百八人の第二位である。山寨では軍政と銭糧を掌り、出征時は宋江と別の一路を率いて一方面を任された。棍棒・槍・騎馬戦のすべてに通じ、史文恭の捕縛で敵を震え上がらせた、梁山屈指の武人である。

招安後、盧俊義は宋江と北の遼を征した。遼の太乙混天象陣へ勇敢に先行し、陣内で神威を示して敵兵を大敗させる。田虎・王慶征討では独立の一軍を率いて河北・淮西を転戦し、行く先々で勝利と奇功を得た。まさしく梁山の一軍の帥である。方臘への南征では別働隊を率い、城と土地を奪い、将を斬り旗を取る。昱嶺関で史進らが失われると、自ら大軍を率いて関を突破した。江南の諸戦で率先して功を重ね、宋江と双璧と称された。

方臘平定後、朝廷は武功大夫・廬州安撫使・兵馬副総管に任じる。しかし赴任の道でも奸臣の毒手から逃れられなかった。梁山の旧人を憎む蔡京・高俅らが御膳に水銀を入れて賜る。食後の帰路、泗州の淮河に至ると、水銀の害が腰や股に及び、手足が動かず、立っていられなくなった。足を滑らせて淮河の深みに落ち、溺死する。棍棒無双の一代の豪傑が奸佞の暗算で死ぬとは、無念なことである。

盧俊義はもと富貴で安閑な員外だった。理由もなく計略で落草へ追い込まれ、牢獄に落ち、最後に梁山で義を結んで、蓋世の武芸を忠義堂の守りとした。招安後は南北を征し、輝かしい功勲で一方面を支え、玉麒麟の名に背かない。だが成功の日にかえって害され、淮水に沈み、宋江や呉用らと黄泉へ帰る。後に徽宗が梁山の諸将を勅封した際、盧俊義も追封に列した。その英風と義概、天罡の首に連なる尊さは、水滸の伝に永く垂れられる。

鲁智深者，本名鲁达，关西人氏，原在渭州小种经略相公帐下做提辖。其人身长八尺，腰阔.en:
Lu Zhishen was originally Lu Da, a man of Guanxi serving as a garrison officer under the Younger Commander Zhong in Weizhou. Eight chi tall and ten spans around the waist, he has a round face, large ears, a straight nose, square mouth, and full beard. Fierce and robust in appearance, he is warm-hearted within. Later the wandering world calls him the Tattooed Monk, for the elaborate tattoos across his back and for taking the tonsure without observing monastic discipline.

When Lu Da first appears, he is drinking with Shi Jin, the Nine-Tattooed Dragons, and Li Zhong, the Tiger-Slaying General, when a woman's crying comes from the next room. The singer Jin Cuilian and her father explain that the local bully, Butcher Zheng, known as the Bully of the West, has forcibly taken her as a concubine and then falsely charged them with debt. Enraged, Lu Da first gives them silver to escape. The next day he goes straight to Zheng's butcher shop at Champion Bridge. He torments Zheng until the butcher attacks with a knife, then lands three punches: one to the nose, like opening an oil-and-sauce shop; one to the eye, like opening a shop of colored silks; and one to the temple, like a full ceremonial orchestra of Buddhist rites. Unexpectedly, the three blows kill Zheng. Fearing prosecution, Lu Da pretends to accuse him of feigning death, then slips away and becomes a fugitive. His beating of the Bully of the West is the novel's first great scene of satisfying justice.

Lu Da flees to Yanmen in Daizhou, where Jin Cuilian and her father repay his kindness. Through Squire Zhao's recommendation, he enters Manjusri Monastery on Mount Wutai. Elder Zhizhen shaves his head and gives him the religious name Zhishen. Yet his love of drink remains. Twice he causes drunken uproar at the monastery, breaking a pavilion on one occasion and damaging a guardian statue on another, disturbing the entire community. Knowing he is no ordinary man, the elder writes a recommendation to the Great Xiangguo Temple in the capital and sends him away, giving four prophetic lines that conceal his life's destination. Assigned to guard the vegetable garden there, Zhishen faces a group of ruffians looking for trouble. He kicks them down one by one, winning their submission. Then he uproots an entire willow in the garden, leaving them astonished as if before a heavenly being. This famous feat fully displays his supernatural strength.

At Xiangguo Temple, Zhishen befriends Lin Chong, instructor to the imperial army of eight hundred thousand. When Gao Qiu frames Lin Chong and sends him into exile at Cangzhou, the bribed escorts Dong Chao and Xue Ba plan to kill him in Wild Boar Forest. Zhishen follows secretly and, at the last possible moment, leaps from behind a tree. His monk's staff scatters the officers and saves Lin Chong. He escorts his friend all the way to Cangzhou before returning. The Wild Boar Forest rescue reveals his boundless loyalty and willingness to face danger for a friend. Once his whereabouts are exposed, he can no longer return to the temple. He goes to Twin Dragon Mountain, joins Yang Zhi, Wu Song, and others in taking Baozhu Monastery, and becomes a stronghold chief. At the union of the three mountains against Qingzhou, they combine with Liangshan's forces and then join the marsh brotherhood.

Lu Zhishen's polished monk's staff weighs sixty-two jin. He swings it like a gale, and his tremendous bodily strength makes him renowned among both mounted and foot troops. At the Grand Assembly, he ranks thirteenth among the Heavenly Stars as the Heavenly Star of Solitude, foremost of the infantry commanders and, with Wu Song, a pillar of the foot army. After amnesty he follows Song Jiang north against Liao and south against Fang La, earning repeated honors. At Black Dragon Ridge in the Fang La campaign, he single-handedly captures an enemy general in the Forest of Ten Thousand Pines, then presses deeper into the mountains and captures the fleeing Fang La himself. This foremost achievement completes his fame and success.

On the return march, the army stays at Six Harmonies Temple in Hangzhou. That night the Qiantang tidal bore roars like thunderous drums. Zhishen wakes in alarm and reaches for his staff to fight, but the monks explain that this is the tide, arriving at its appointed time. He suddenly remembers Elder Zhizhen's prophecy: 'Hear the tide and be fulfilled; see its coming and be stilled.' Enlightened, he knows the moment of his passing has arrived. He bathes, changes clothes, burns incense, and sits upright in a meditation chair, leaving a verse: 'All my life I sought no virtuous fruit, loving only slaughter and flame. Suddenly the golden cangue breaks open; here the jade fetters snap. Ah! The Qiantang tide has come; only today do I know who I am.' With these words he passes peacefully while seated. This rough monk, who has killed and burned, ends by understanding the tide and attaining Buddhahood in meditation, one of the finest peaceful endings among Water Margin's heroes.
鲁智深者，本名鲁达，关西人氏，原在渭州小种经略相公帐下做提辖。其人身长八尺，腰阔.ja:
魯智深は本名を魯達といい、関西の人。もとは渭州の小種経略相公の帳下で提轄を務めた。身長八尺、腰は十囲、丸い顔に大きな耳、まっすぐな鼻と四角い口、頬髯を備える。荒々しく豪壮な姿ながら、内には熱い心があった。背に一面の花の刺青があり、剃髪して僧となっても戒律を守らなかったため、のちに江湖で「花和尚」と呼ばれた。

初登場の魯達は九紋竜史進、打虎将李忠と酒楼で飲んでいた。隣で女の泣く声がし、尋ねると歌売りの金翠蓮父娘で、地元の悪霸「鎮関西」鄭屠に無理やり妾とされ、逆に借金をしたと偽られていた。怒り心頭の魯達は、まず銀を与えて父娘を逃がし、翌日、状元橋の肉屋へ鄭屠を訪ねる。散々からかって刀を持って向かってこさせ、その勢いで三拳を打った。鼻への一拳は油醤の店を開いたよう、眼窩への一拳は色絹の店を開いたよう、こめかみへの一拳は水陸の法会を総出で催したようだった。思わず三拳で鄭屠を殺してしまい、訴追を恐れた魯達は死んだふりをするなと罵るふりをして逃れ、江湖を流浪する。この「拳打鎮関西」は、一書で最初の、胸のすく恩讐の名場面である。

代州雁門へ逃れた魯達は、金翠蓮父娘の恩返しを受け、趙員外の推薦で五台山文殊院に出家した。智真長老が頭を剃って授記し、「智深」の法名を与える。しかし酒癖は変わらず、二度も酔って山門を騒がせた。一度は亭を壊し、一度は金剛像を傷つけ、寺中を落ち着かなくする。凡人ではないと知る長老は、東京の大相国寺への推薦状を書き、別れに生涯の帰着を隠した四句の偈を贈った。相国寺では菜園番を任され、騒ぎを起こしに来た無頼者を一人ずつ蹴り倒し、服従させる。さらに柳の大木を根ごと引き抜き、一同は天人の業かと驚いた。「倒抜垂楊柳」は、その神力を余すところなく描く。

相国寺で智深は八十万禁軍教頭の林冲と知り合う。のちに高俅に陥れられた林冲が滄州へ刺配され、賄賂を受けた董超・薛覇が野猪林で殺そうとした。智深は密かに後を追い、危機一髪で木陰から跳び出し、禅杖で役人を散らして林冲を救う。滄州まで護送してようやく戻った。この「大鬧野猪林」は、天にも届く義と、友のため危難へ赴く心を示している。居場所が漏れて相国寺へ戻れなくなると、二竜山へ行き、楊志・武松らと宝珠寺を攻略して山寨の主となった。三山聚義で青州を攻めた際に梁山と合兵し、皆で入山する。

魯智深の水磨禅杖は六十二斤の重さがあり、陣前で振るえば疾風の勢いとなる。鍛え抜いた神力も加わり、馬軍・歩軍の双方で勇名を得た。大聚義では天罡第十三位、「天孤星」となり、歩軍頭領の筆頭として武松と中核を担う。招安後は宋江と北の遼、南の方臘を征し、戦功を重ねた。方臘征討の烏竜嶺では万松林で敵の大将を一人で捕らえ、さらに山中深く入って逃亡中の方臘本人を生け捕りにした。平定の第一の功を立て、功名を成したといえる。

凱旋の途中、大軍は杭州六和寺に泊まる。その夜、銭塘江の潮が雷鼓のように鳴った。驚いて起きた智深が杖を持って戦いに出ようとすると、僧たちは時刻どおりに来る潮信だと教えた。その瞬間、五台山で智真長老から贈られた「潮を聞いて円かになり、信を見て寂す」の偈を思い出し、悟りを得て入寂の時を知る。沐浴して着替え、香を焚き、禅椅に端座して一篇の頌を残した。「生涯、善果を修めず、ただ殺人放火を好んだ。突然、金の枷を開き、ここに玉の鎖を断つ。ああ、銭塘江の潮信が来る。今日初めて我が我であると知る」。言い終えて、静かに坐化した。殺し火を放った荒僧が、最後は潮を悟って成仏に至る。水滸の群雄の中でも第一等の善終である。

马麟，江南建康府人氏，乃六朝金粉之地所出的一条好汉。其人生得唇红齿白，眉目清秀，.en:
Ma Lin comes from Jiankang in Jiangnan, a hero born in the splendor of the old Six Dynasties capital. Red-lipped, white-toothed, and fine-featured, he carries some of a street performer's easy freedom. He begins as a young loafer: one of the city men who run errands for officials or trade on their appearance and singing in the markets, neither farmers nor soldiers, living by cleverness and a flute. Yet beneath that frivolous profession lies a hard spirit. He favors a great rolling blade, skillfully spinning it like a wheel, and also throws darts and concealed weapons, rarely missing a man within a hundred paces. Most remarkable is his ability to hold two iron flutes in his mouth and sound both in one breath. Their plaintive music rises into the clouds as though an immortal has descended. His blend of culture and arms, wildness and chivalry, wins the elegant name Iron-Flute Immortal, honoring both his instruments and his free-spirited, peerless artistry.

Ma Lin becomes an outlaw on Huangmen Mountain. He swears brotherhood with Ou Peng, the Cloud-Touching Golden Wings, Jiang Jing, the Divine Calculator, and Tao Zongwang, the Nine-Tailed Turtle. The four occupy the mountain, raiding households and passing merchants in a stronghold of their own. All have long admired Song Gongming of Yuncheng for his generosity and fame. When Song Jiang's drunken seditious poem at Xunyang Tower leads Prefect Cai Jiu to condemn him to death, the four are filled with indignation. They plan to muster their men and raid Jiangzhou's execution ground for a hero they have never met. Before they can leave, Chao Gai's Liangshan force has already rescued him. Returning to the mountain after his escape, Song Jiang passes Huangmen. The four line up to welcome him, invite him to stay several days, and entertain him lavishly. He explains the scale of Liangshan's brotherhood and the sincerity with which its Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness welcomes talent. They readily accept his invitation, burn their Huangmen stronghold, and take everyone to the marsh. The iron flute now sounds across Liangshan's eight hundred li of misty water.

After joining, Ma Lin shows his ability on campaign. In the second attack on Zhu Family Manor, he serves as a vanguard with Ou Peng, Deng Fei, and Wang Ying. He rides out against Zhu Long, but after only a few exchanges Qin Ming, the Thunderbolt, takes his place. Ma Lin then meets Hu Sanniang, Ten-Foot Green. Both use twin blades: four steel edges flash and whirl around them like scattered jade and snow-blown blossoms, a dazzling sight. At the Grand Assembly, Ma Lin takes the sixty-seventh chair as the Earthly Star of Brightness, becoming a junior cavalry commander and leader of distant scouting patrols. His role is not among the most prestigious, but it is highly dangerous: before the armies meet, he must penetrate enemy territory to learn its strength and weakness. Only unusual courage and agility can do this, showing Liangshan's regard for his abilities.

After amnesty, Ma Lin follows Song Jiang north against Liao and south against Fang La without respite. In the latter campaign, he earns a notable success by personally questioning villagers near Black Dragon Ridge and learning of a small path across it. This lets the Song army advance by a detour to Dongguan, threatening the natural fortress from both sides and opening the way to victory. Yet fate grants him no long life. During the great battle of Muzhou, Song Jiang orders him and Yan Shun, the Multicolored Tiger, to guard the main road at Black Dragon Ridge against a rear attack by Shi Bao and Bai Qin. Ma Lin fights fiercely with his blade, but Bai Qin finds an opening and hurls a javelin that knocks him from his horse. Shi Bao rushes in and cuts him in two. His heroic soul is lost in the blood and turmoil of Black Dragon Ridge, and the Iron-Flute Immortal's music falls silent forever.
