Later, the court posthumously grants him the title Gentleman of Righteous Integrity for his loyalty and courage. From a roving youth of Jinling to Huangmen chief, then Liangshan commander, he finally dies in royal service. The dashing flutist and swordsman ends wrapped in a horsehide, leaving later readers to close the book with a sigh.
马麟，江南建康府人氏，乃六朝金粉之地所出的一条好汉。其人生得唇红齿白，眉目清秀，.ja:
馬麟は江南建康府の人、六朝の華やかな地が生んだ好漢である。紅い唇に白い歯、端正な眉目を持ち、所作には江湖の芸人らしい洒脱さがあった。もとは小番子閑漢の出身で、これは城下で官府の使い走りをしたり、街で容姿と歌を売ったりする浮浪の若者をいう。農にも兵にも就かず、機転と笛一本で暮らす者だが、馬麟はその浮華な仕事の中に硬い骨を隠していた。大滾刀を好み、車輪のように上下に旋回させる技に優れる。飛鏢や暗器も得意で、百歩以内の相手をほとんど外さない。最も奇とされたのは、二本の鉄笛を口に含んで一息に両方を吹くことだった。もの悲しく澄んだ音が雲へ上り、仙人が降りたかのように響く。文武を備え、狂にして侠の振る舞いから「鉄笛仙」の雅号を得た。二本の笛の由来と、自由奔放で群を抜く芸への憧れを含む名である。

馬麟は黄門山に落草した。摩雲金翅の欧鵬、神算子の蒋敬、九尾亀の陶宗旺と四人で義を結び、山に拠って屋敷や商人を襲った。四人とも鄆城の宋公明の仗義疏財と江湖の名声を聞き、心から慕っていた。宋江が江州潯陽楼で酔って反詩を書き、蔡九知府に捕らえられて斬罪となったと知ると、義憤に駆られ、会ったこともない好漢を救うため兵を集めて刑場を襲おうとする。しかし出陣前に晁天王の梁山軍がすでに救出していた。難を逃れた宋江は帰山の道で黄門山を通り、四人は隊を並べて迎え、数日滞在を願って厚くもてなす。宋江は梁山の聚義の大きさと、忠義堂が賢才を招く誠意を語り、共に入山するよう誘った。馬麟らは快く承知し、黄門山寨を焼いて全員で水泊へ向かう。こうして鉄笛の音は八百里の梁山の煙波へ入った。

入伙後、馬麟は従軍して腕を示す。二打祝家荘では欧鵬・鄧飛・王英と先鋒を務め、祝竜に挑むが、数合で霹靂火の秦明が代わった。次に一丈青の扈三娘と出会う。双方が双刀を使い、四本の鋼刀が上下に舞い、体を巡る寒光は玉片や雪の花が散るような見事さだった。大聚義では第六十七の椅子、地明星となり、馬軍小彪将兼遠探出哨頭領として偵察の先鋒を担う。最上位の役ではないが、両軍が接する前に敵地へ深く入り、虚実を探る危険な任である。並外れた胆力と身軽さがなければ務まらず、梁山がその本領を重く見たことが分かる。

招安後、宋江と北の遼、南の方臘を征して転戦を続けた。方臘征討では烏竜嶺の山民を自ら訪ねて小道を探り当て、宋軍を迂回させて東管へ至らせた。天険を両面から挟む形となり、攻略の機を開いた奇功である。しかし天は長い命を与えなかった。睦州の大戦で宋江は馬麟と錦毛虎燕順に烏竜嶺の大路を守らせ、石宝・白欽の背後への襲撃を防がせる。馬麟が刀を振るって戦う最中、白欽が隙を見て標槍を放ち、馬上から射落とした。石宝が駆け寄り、一刀で二つに斬る。英魂は烏竜嶺の乱軍の血溜まりに消え、鉄笛仙の笛は永遠に止んだ。後に朝廷は忠勇を称えて義節郎を追贈する。金陵の浮浪の若者から黄門山の寨主、梁山の頭領へと変わり、最後に王事へ殉じた。笛と刀の風流人が馬革に包まれる結末は、後世の読者にも長嘆させる。

孟康，真定州人氏，水浒一百单八将中一员身材魁伟、技艺独擅的好汉。其人生得身长一丈.en:
Meng Kang of Zhending is a towering, uniquely skilled hero among the 108. One zhang tall, handsome, and pale-skinned, he stands out in a crowd like a jade flagstaff reaching into the sky, earning the name Jade Banner Pole. A banner pole is the long staff raising a flag before a temple; the name captures both his upright height and his jade-white complexion with fitting precision. His martial courage is unexceptional, but few can match his shipbuilding. Large vessels and small craft, tower ships and fast boats emerge quickly and sturdily under his skillful tools and measured direction. He knows every detail of river navigation. In a world where strongholds depend on water and boats are life itself, such mastery is worth more than gold.

A killing drives Meng Kang into outlawry. When the court organizes the Flower-and-Stone Convoy, conscripting laborers and craftsmen to transport rare flowers and ornamental rocks to the capital, he is selected to oversee construction of the great cargo boats. The supervising official abuses his authority and humiliates him repeatedly. A fierce-tempered man unable to tolerate such insults, Meng Kang kills the officer in anger. Guilty of a major crime, he must flee. He eventually reaches Yinma River, where he swears brotherhood with Deng Fei, the Fiery-Eyed Lion, and Pei Xuan, the Iron-Faced Clerk. They occupy a stronghold and rob households and travelers. Surrounded by hills and water with a post road running through, the place is easy to defend. Later, Dai Zong passes on Liangshan business and meets them, describing the thriving brotherhood. Yang Xiong, Shi Xiu, and their companions also happen to be active nearby. These connections bring Meng Kang, Deng Fei, Pei Xuan, and all their followers away from Yinma River to Liangshan.

At Liangshan, Meng Kang's craft at last finds its proper use. Three sides of the stronghold face water, with eight hundred li of misty marsh. Naval vessels are fundamental to its survival and victories, and only an expert can supervise their construction. He is assigned every kind of warship, from armored assault boats to fast craft, fighting vessels, and tower ships. At the Grand Assembly, he takes the seventieth chair as the Earthly Star of Abundance, continuing to oversee all shipbuilding. This is no front-line dueling post, yet it supports the entire naval establishment. Equipment for water warfare and fire attacks depends on his hands: a tireless, capable officer of great merit who does not boast of his skill.

After amnesty, Meng Kang follows the army north and south. His warships carry Liangshan's heroes against Liao and other enemies across rivers and seas. Fang La's territory is dense with waterways and frequent naval battles, offering another chance for his fleet to show its value. But fate is inconstant. At Deqing County, the army faces Fang La's four naval commanders, Cheng Gui, Di Yuan, Qiao Zheng, and Xie Fu. Experienced in water warfare, they lay an ambush and attack with cannon. In the fierce fighting, one shot strikes Meng Kang squarely in the helmet. The towering man's head and helmet are crushed together, killing him instantly in a scene too terrible to contemplate. The sky-reaching Jade Banner Pole snaps in a moment under Deqing's guns. The court later awards him the posthumous title Gentleman of Righteous Integrity. From shipwright in Zhending, fleeing after resisting official abuse, to outlaw at Yinma River and brother at Liangshan, he builds a thousand warships before dying amid the guns and weapons of Jiangnan. He wins distinction through craftsmanship rather than prowess; though he does not seize banners in combat, he shares the generals' sacrifice. His name endures with that cannon shot among Water Margin's misty waters.
孟康，真定州人氏，水浒一百单八将中一员身材魁伟、技艺独擅的好汉。其人生得身长一丈.ja:
孟康は真定州の人。百八人の中でも魁偉な体と独自の技を持つ好漢である。身長一丈、堂々たる容姿と白い肌で、人々の中に立つと天へ届く玉の旗竿のように目立ったため、「玉幡竿」と呼ばれた。幡竿とは寺社の前で旗を高く掲げる長い竿であり、名の半分はすらりと高い体、半分は玉のような肌を描く。姿にも気配にもよく合う異名である。驚くべき武勇はないが、造船には他人の及ばぬ技があった。大小の船、楼船や快速艇も、巧みな斧と確かな寸法で速く丈夫に造り、川の船の要点はすべて胸に収めていた。水に拠って寨を築き、舟を命とする世で、千金にも代え難い稀な本領であった。

落草の原因は一件の殺人だった。朝廷が花石綱のため人夫や職人を徴発し、珍しい花石を都へ運ばせた時、孟康は造船の技によって大船の監造を命じられた。監督官が権勢を頼りに幾度も侮辱するので、剛烈な孟康は耐えられず、怒ってその官を殺す。重罪を犯して江湖へ逃れ、やがて飲馬川に至り、火眼狻猊の鄧飛、鉄面孔目の裴宣と義を結んだ。三人は山寨を拠点に屋敷や旅人を襲う。山と水に囲まれ、駅路が通る飲馬川は、守りやすく攻め難い場所である。のちに用務で通った戴宗が三人と会い、梁山泊の盛んな聚義を語った。楊雄・石秀らも付近を往来し、その縁が重なって、孟康・鄧飛・裴宣は手勢ごと飲馬川を捨て、水泊梁山へ赴く。

入伙すると、造船の絶芸にようやく活躍の場ができた。梁山は三方を水に囲まれ、八百里の煙波を持つ。水軍の船は寨を立て敵を破る根本であり、大小戦船の監督は孟康ほどの専門家でなければ務まらない。山寨は蒙衝・闘艦・快船・楼櫓など、すべての戦船を彼に造らせた。大聚義では第七十の椅子、地満星に座り、諸船の監造を掌る。陣前の戦闘ではなくとも、水泊の軍備の基礎を支える役である。水戦の資材も火攻めの道具も、その巧みな手に頼っていた。労苦と功は大きく、腕を誇らぬ有能な将であった。

招安後、孟康は大軍と南北を征し、彼の戦船は梁山の好漢を乗せて遼や賊を討ち、江海を走った。方臘への南征は水路が密で水戦が多く、監造した舟師が力を示す時だった。しかし天道は定まらず、英雄にも避けられぬ運がある。軍が徳清県へ至ると、方臘の水軍総管、成貴・翟源・喬正・謝福の四将と対した。水戦を熟知する四人は伏兵を置き、火砲で攻める。激戦中、一発が孟康の兜を正確に捉えた。一丈の好漢の頭と兜は砕かれ、即座に命を落とす。見るに忍びぬ惨状だった。天を支える玉幡竿が徳清水寨の砲火で一瞬に折れたのである。朝廷は後に義節郎を追贈して功を称えた。真定の船大工から官吏の虐待に抗して逃れ、飲馬川に落草し、梁山で千艘の軍船を造った末、江南の砲火に殉じる。武勇ではなく匠の心で功を立て、陣前で旗を奪わなくとも諸将と国難に赴いた。その名は一声の砲音と共に、水滸の煙波に永く残る。

穆春者,江州揭阳镇人氏也。家本豪富,世居揭阳一霸,与其兄没遮拦穆弘,并称揭阳镇上.en:
Mu Chun comes from Jieyang Town in Jiangzhou. His wealthy family has long dominated the area, and he and his elder brother Mu Hong, the Unrestrained, are called the town's two tyrants. His name, Lesser Unrestrained, follows his brother's. Both names signify that the Mu brothers roam Jieyang without anyone daring to stop them. Though younger, Mu Chun is imposing, carries a staff, and knows several weapon routines. His local influence is considerable, and ordinary people dare not challenge him.

The wider Jieyang region is said to have three powers: the Mu brothers in town; Li Li and his murderous inn on Jieyang Ridge; and Zhang Heng and Zhang Shun, engaged in illicit business on the Xunyang River. With wealth and many retainers, the Mu family controls the town. Every visiting merchant or performer must first pay respects to them. If someone fails to do so, no townsman may buy his goods or watch his performance. They are truly the local bullies.

Mu Chun first appears in the episode of Xue Yong, the Sick Tiger, performing in the street. Song Jiang reaches Jieyang and sees Xue Yong demonstrating spear and staff while selling medicinal plasters. After a full routine, no one applauds or gives him money. New to the town, Xue Yong has not visited the Mu brothers, and fear of them keeps everyone silent. Unaware of this rule and impressed by his skill, Song Jiang gives him five taels of silver. Mu Chun leaps out to challenge him: this is Jieyang, so how can an outsider ignore its customs and give money without permission? His words provoke a quarrel with Song Jiang and Xue Yong. He tells Mu Hong, and the brothers lead a large body of retainers to seize Song Jiang and settle the matter. Alone and vulnerable, Song Jiang flees through the night. They pursue him to the Xunyang River, with no way ahead and pursuers behind, nearly costing him his life. His encounters with Zhang Heng, Li Jun, and the others allow him to escape. Later he befriends these heroes. When the Jiangzhou execution ground is stormed and Song Jiang and Dai Zong are rescued, the Jieyang heroes—Mu Hong, Mu Chun, Li Jun, Zhang Heng, Zhang Shun, Tong Wei, Tong Meng, Xue Yong, Bai Sheng, and others—follow Song Jiang to Liangshan and unite in the great cause. Mu Chun abandons his family estate and becomes a stronghold leader.

At the Grand Assembly, Mu Chun takes the eightieth chair as the Earthly Star of Suppression, joining his brother in Liangshan's ranks. Mu Hong belongs to the thirty-six Heavenly Stars, while Mu Chun is an Earthly Star and infantry officer awaiting orders. At different ranks, both brothers serve the cause. Mu Chun's spear and staff skills and willingness to charge make him a brave fighter, but his reputation and position never equal his elder brother's.

After imperial amnesty, Mu Chun remains with Song Gongming's army against Liao, Tian Hu, and Wang Qing, enduring many battles. The campaign against Fang La kills or wounds more than half of Liangshan's leaders. His brother Mu Hong contracts an epidemic illness and dies at Hangzhou, unable to return. Mu Chun survives several fierce battles without being killed. After victory and the army's return to court, he receives a military appointment. But seeing his brothers nearly all lost and his own elder brother dead, he no longer desires fame, wealth, or office. He returns his commission and goes home to Jieyang, restores the family business, and lives as a peaceful commoner until the end of his days. Such an ending is rare among the 108.

Mu Chun begins as a bully of Jieyang, abusing his family's power. Xue Yong's performance and the pursuit of Song Jiang bring him into Liangshan's orbit, and he ultimately gives up evil for the righteous brotherhood. His martial ability is not outstanding, yet he always follows his brother faithfully, showing the strength of their bond. Retiring after success and ending his days at home, unburdened by rank and wealth, he receives a generous fate compared with the heroes who die in royal service.
穆春者,江州揭阳镇人氏也。家本豪富,世居揭阳一霸,与其兄没遮拦穆弘,并称揭阳镇上.ja:
穆春は江州掲陽鎮の人。家は富豪で、代々掲陽を支配し、兄の没遮攔穆弘と「二霸」と呼ばれた。異名の「小遮攔」は兄の「没遮攔」に倣う。「遮攔」とは、兄弟が一帯ではばかりなく横行し、誰も遮って止められないという意味である。弟ながら凛々しい体つきで棒を使い、いくつかの槍棒を心得、鎮では勢威があり、普通の者は逆らえなかった。

掲陽一帯には三霸の説がある。鎮の穆弘・穆春兄弟、掲陽嶺で黒店を開く李立、潯陽江で私商を営む張横・張順である。穆家は財産と多くの手勢を頼りに鎮を押さえ、商人も芸人も、来ればまず挨拶に行かなければならなかった。行かぬ者の品を買うことも芸を見ることも、鎮の人には一切許されない。まさに土地の顔役であった。

登場は病大虫薛永の大道芸の場面である。掲陽鎮へ来た宋江は、膏薬売りの薛永が槍棒を演じても、誰も喝采せず、金も出さないのを見た。初めて来た薛永が穆家兄弟へ挨拶をしなかったため、皆が恐れて報酬を与えられないのだった。事情を知らぬ宋江は腕を認めて銀五両を与える。これが穆家の掟に触れ、穆春が飛び出し、ここは自分たちの掲陽鎮だ、よそ者がなぜ勝手に金を出す、と詰め寄った。こうして宋江・薛永と不和になる。穆春は兄へ告げ、兄弟は大勢の荘客を率いて宋江を捕らえ、話をつけようとした。孤立した宋江は夜逃げするしかなく、潯陽江まで追い詰められる。前に道なく、後ろに追手があり、危うく死ぬところを張横や李俊らとの出会いで救われた。のちに宋江は豪傑たちと知り合い、江州の刑場襲撃で宋江・戴宗が救出されると、穆弘・穆春、李俊・張横・張順・童威・童猛・薛永・白勝ら掲陽の好漢は宋江と梁山へ赴き、大義に集う。穆春は家業を捨て、梁山の頭領となった。

大聚義で天罡地煞の座次が定まると、穆春は地鎮星として第八十の椅子に座り、兄と共に列した。穆弘は三十六天罡の内に入り、穆春は地煞の歩軍将校として命令を待つ。位は前後しても二人とも梁山のため働いた。穆春は槍棒で突撃する勇ある将だが、名声と地位は兄ほど華々しくなかった。

招安後、宋公明の遼・田虎・王慶征討にも従い、大隊と共に幾度も戦った。方臘への南征では頭領の半数以上が死傷し、兄穆弘も疫病を患って杭州で死ぬ。穆春は数度の悪戦を生き延びた。平定後、軍が朝廷へ戻って論功行賞を受けると、武官に任じられる。しかし兄弟がほぼ失われ、実兄も亡くなり、功名利禄に未練はなかった。官誥を辞退して掲陽鎮へ帰り、家業を整え直し、良民として天寿を終える。百八人の中では貴重な善終といえる。

一生を見れば、初めは権勢で横行する掲陽の霸だった。薛永の芸と宋江追跡の一件で梁山に縁ができ、悪を捨てて善へ向かい、聚義した。武芸は抜群でなくとも、終始兄に従って離れず仕えたところに、兄弟の情の厚さが見える。功成って退き、爵禄に縛られず故郷で老いた結末は、王事に殉じた好漢たちに比べ、恵まれた運命であった。

穆弘，绰号「没遮拦」，应天罡之数，乃天究星临世。其人乃江州揭阳镇人氏，与兄弟穆春.en:
Mu Hong, the Unrestrained, belongs to the Heavenly Stars as the Heavenly Star of Inquiry. He comes from Jieyang Town in Jiangzhou and lives with his younger brother Mu Chun, a local power. The brothers and their mother own extensive estates, an established wealthy family. Strong-willed, competitive, and overbearing, Mu Hong will yield in nothing. His words and deeds press ahead without anything to restrain him, giving him his name. Mu Chun is called the Lesser Unrestrained, and together they are the two fearsome brothers whom none in Jieyang dares provoke. Mu Hong has a dignified, imposing appearance and uses a broadsword. Equally capable on horseback, he is no weak fighter.

His story begins with Song Jiang at Jieyang Town. Exiled to Jiangzhou, Song Jiang passes through and sees Xue Yong, the Sick Tiger, giving a spear-and-staff performance. Everyone fears the Mu family and dares not reward him. Unaware of the situation, Song Jiang freely gives five taels of silver. Seeing the family rule broken, Mu Chun turns hostile and seeks trouble with Song Jiang and Xue Yong. Song Jiang can find no lodging, since innkeepers are afraid to receive him. The Mu brothers lead their retainers in pursuit through the night, intending to kill him.

With nowhere to turn, Song Jiang reaches the Xunyang River, water ahead and pursuers behind. Zhang Heng the Boatman happens to be there with a fishing boat, and Song Jiang hurriedly boards to cross. But Zhang Heng is himself a robber. In midstream, he threatens Song Jiang with a choice of the blade or drowning. At the critical moment, Li Jun the River Dragon arrives with Tong Wei, the Cave-Emerging Dragon, and Tong Meng, the River-Churning Clam. Recognizing Song Jiang's name, Li Jun stops Zhang Heng and saves him. He then mediates and introduces the Mu brothers. Astonished and delighted to learn that this is the celebrated Timely Rain, Song Gongming, they hastily apologize and invite him to their manor with generous hospitality. They become devoted friends. The quarrel in Jieyang thus forges their ties with Song Jiang and the Jiangzhou heroes Li Jun, Zhang Heng, Zhang Shun, Tong Wei, and Tong Meng.

Later, Song Jiang's rebellious poem in Jiangzhou leads to imprisonment and a death sentence. Liangshan's heroes and the local men work together to storm the execution ground, rescuing Song Jiang and Dai Zong. Mu Hong, Mu Chun, Li Jun, Zhang Heng, Zhang Shun, Tong Wei, Tong Meng, Xue Yong, Hou Jian, Bai Sheng, and the others fight their way to White Dragon Temple and unite. They then attack Wuwei and capture Huang Wenbing to avenge Song Jiang. Afterward, the Mu brothers abandon their Jieyang estates and follow Song Jiang to join Liangshan.

At Liangshan, Mu Hong's ability on horse and foot makes him one of the Eight Cavalry Vanguards and assault commanders, alongside Yang Zhi, Suo Chao, Xu Ning, Shi Jin, Hua Rong, Zhu Tong, and others. His task is to break into enemy formations. At the Grand Assembly he takes the twenty-fourth chair as the Heavenly Star of Inquiry, reflecting his importance among the Jiangzhou heroes. In the three attacks on Daming, the two victories over Tong Guan, and the three defeats of Gao Qiu, he serves in the vanguard, competing to be first and earning repeated honors. His fierce broadsword and bold assaults fit the name Unrestrained exactly.

After amnesty, Mu Hong follows Song Jiang against Liao, Tian Hu, Wang Qing, and Fang La, campaigning north and south. Fang La's war leaves the Liangshan brothers terribly reduced. Mu Hong escapes the blades of battle but dies of epidemic disease. At Hangzhou in the summer heat, illness spreads through the army and strikes many leaders. He falls sick, remains bedridden, and dies while being cared for at Six Harmonies Temple. His younger brother Mu Chun survives the campaign, later returns his official commission, and goes home to Jieyang to live as a peaceful citizen and reach a natural end.

Mu Hong begins as Jieyang's powerful bully. Meeting Song Jiang leads him to abandon his estate for the cause, transforming a local tyrant into a valiant Liangshan commander. From pursuing Song Jiang in anger to submitting, swearing brotherhood, supporting the cause, fighting across the land, and dying in Hangzhou, he remains a pillar of the Jiangzhou group. Proud, forceful, and unrestrained, once won by Song Jiang's righteousness he follows loyally until death. The strongman whose name once ruled Jieyang dies on a royal campaign as a true Heavenly Star commander. Among the 108, his story traces the passage from domination to righteousness and wholehearted allegiance.
穆弘，绰号「没遮拦」，应天罡之数，乃天究星临世。其人乃江州揭阳镇人氏，与兄弟穆春.ja:
穆弘、異名は「没遮攔」。天罡の数に応じ、天究星の化身である。江州掲陽鎮の人で、弟穆春と共に住む一帯の霸だった。兄弟と母の家には多くの田荘があり、根を張った富豪である。性格は剛強で勝ち気、横暴で何事も譲らず、言動は遮るものなく突き進む。そのため江湖で「没遮攔」と呼ばれた。弟は「小遮攔」、二人合わせて遮攔双煞とされ、掲陽では誰も手を出せない。穆弘は堂々とした姿と気宇を持ち、朴刀を使い、馬上でも戦える確かな武芸者であった。

物語は掲陽鎮の宋江の一件から始まる。江州へ刺配される途中、宋江は病大虫薛永の槍棒の芸を見る。皆が穆家を恐れて褒美を出せない中、事情を知らず銀五両を気前よく与えた。掟を破られた穆春はその場で態度を変え、宋江と薛永に難癖をつける。店も穆家を恐れて宋江を泊めず、兄弟は荘客を率い、殺そうと夜通し追い掛けた。

逃げ場を失った宋江は、前に大河、後ろに追手を抱えて潯陽江へ着く。船火児の張横が漁船を出しており、急いで乗って渡しを求めた。しかし張横も追剥で、川の中央へ漕ぐと、刀を食らうか川へ飛び込んで死ぬかと迫る。命の瀬戸際に、混江竜李俊、出洞蛟童威、翻江蜃童猛の舟が来た。宋江の名を知る李俊が張横を制して救い、さらに仲裁して穆弘・穆春と対面させる。名高い及時雨宋公明だと聞くと兄弟は驚き喜び、慌てて詫び、荘へ招いて厚くもてなした。これから心を寄せて交わる。掲陽の恩怨はかえって、宋江と李俊・張横・張順・童威・童猛ら江州の豪傑との友情を成就した。

のちに宋江は江州で反詩を書いて投獄され、死罪となる。梁山の好漢と江州の豪傑が心を合わせて刑場を襲い、宋江・戴宗を救った。穆弘・穆春、李俊・張横・張順・童威・童猛・薛永・侯健・白勝らは宋江と白竜廟へ進んで聚義し、さらに無為軍を攻めて黄文炳を捕らえ、冤仇を晴らした。事後、穆家兄弟は掲陽の家業を捨て、宋江と梁山へ入って義を結ぶ。

梁山では馬歩の両方に優れる腕を買われ、馬軍八驃騎兼先鋒使の一人となった。楊志・索超・徐寧・史進・花栄・朱仝らと並び、突撃と破陣を担う。大聚義では天究星として第二十四の椅子に座り、江州系豪傑の中での重さを示した。続く大名府への三攻、童貫への二勝、高俅への三勝でも前部の先鋒として勇を競い、功を重ねる。剛猛な朴刀で陣前に立つ姿は、まさに「没遮攔」の名どおりであった。

招安後は宋江と遼・田虎・王慶・方臘を征し、南北を転戦した。方臘の役は梁山兄弟に惨烈な死傷を出す。穆弘は陣前の刀兵には倒れなかったが、疫病に没した。大軍が杭州へ来た暑い月、疫病で頭領が相次いで倒れ、穆弘も罹患して起き上がれなくなる。六和寺に残って療養したものの、ついに病死した。弟穆春は生還し、のちに官誥を返して掲陽へ戻り、良民として天寿を全うする。

穆弘はもと掲陽の豪霸であったが、宋江と知り合い、家を捨てて従い、梁山の驍将へ変わる。宋江を追って恨みを結んだ始まりから、帰服と結義、聚義の支援、南北の戦い、杭州の病没まで、江州系豪傑の中核であり続けた。剛強で覇気に満ち、何にも遮られぬ男だが、宋江の義に服すると死ぬまで忠実に従った。「没遮攔」の名で掲陽を縦横にした豪強は、天罡の正将として王事の旅に没する。百八人の中に、霸から義へ、慨然と従う一編の江湖の文章を残した。

欧鹏，黄州人氏，原是大江边上守把军户出身。其人因不堪军中盘剥、世道艰难，遂弃了军.en:
Ou Peng of Huangzhou comes from a hereditary military household guarding the great river. Unable to endure army exploitation and the hardships of the age, he abandons military registration and gathers outlaws in the hills. Tall, exceptionally strong, and skilled in arms, he is especially good at leaping, climbing, and crossing dangerous ground. Moving as swiftly as flight and charging with great agility, he resembles a golden-winged roc rising into the clouds, earning the magnificent name Cloud-Touching Golden Wings. He is a practiced spearman and brave, experienced fighter. Among Liangshan's 108, he corresponds to the Earthly Star of Vastness, takes the forty-eighth chair, and serves as junior cavalry commander and leader of distant scouting patrols.

His path to Liangshan begins at Huangmen Mountain. After his rescue in Jiangzhou, Song Jiang travels with the heroes toward Liangshan. Four outlaw chiefs block the route beneath Huangmen: their leader Ou Peng, Jiang Jing the Divine Calculator, Ma Lin the Iron-Flute Immortal, and Tao Zongwang the Nine-Tailed Turtle. They have sworn brotherhood there and live by raiding. Seeing the great company pass below, they come to meet it. Learning that this is the long-admired Timely Rain, Song Gongming, and seeing the strength and righteousness of Liangshan's heroes, they are overjoyed. They bow and willingly abandon Huangmen, taking their own followers to the marsh stronghold. Thus the four join the greater company and add their abilities to Liangshan.

Ou Peng thereafter accompanies the army north and south, always eager to fight first, storming formations, cities, and camps and earning much merit. His skillful spear and agile courage honor his name. His Huangmen brothers retain their own specialties: Jiang Jing calculates money and grain accounts, Ma Lin plays the iron flute and uses twin blades, and Tao Zongwang works the earth with a powerful shovel. Bound by life and death before joining, they remain close afterward. Ou Peng often fights beside Ma Lin, each covering the other. At the Grand Assembly, his Earthly Star rank and cavalry scouting duties place him among the brave commanders without dimming his reputation. His ability to traverse perilous ground and his boldness make him a valuable officer. In sieges and open battles, he is commonly at the forward outposts, discovering enemy dispositions, finding paths through mountains, and leading when foes appear. Song Jiang and Lu Junyi rely heavily on him.

After amnesty, Ou Peng serves Song Jiang against Liao, Tian Hu in Hebei, and Wang Qing in Huaixi. Fighting everywhere, he earns repeated honors and preserves his old reputation. Whenever the army marches, he is in the scouting vanguard, reconnoitering and charging beside his comrades through dozens of battles without retreat. In the Jiangnan campaign against Fang La, more than half of Liangshan's heroes are lost, and Ou Peng falls too. Fang La holds difficult terrain and has many able generals; every city and tract of land costs heaps of dead and streams of blood. Ou Peng bravely presses into the enemy ranks. As he rides with spear leveled, charging left and right, a skilled enemy archer waits concealed within the formation. The archer finds his aim and releases. Ou Peng cannot dodge; struck in a vital place amid the arrows, he falls from his horse and dies on the field. A vigorous warrior named for touching the clouds thus falls in Jiangnan. From military household to outlaw and then righteous brotherhood, he campaigns across the land and finally gives his body to the battlefield. When Song Jiang returns after victory, the court posthumously honors Ou Peng as Gentleman of Loyal Martial Service, sending his soul home. His agility, courage, and sincere allegiance remain a moving and remembered Liangshan story.
欧鹏，黄州人氏，原是大江边上守把军户出身。其人因不堪军中盘剥、世道艰难，遂弃了军.ja:
欧鵬は黄州の人。もとは大河沿いを守る軍戸の出身だった。軍の搾取と世の苦難に耐えられず、軍籍を捨てて落草し、山林に仲間を集める。背が高く力は抜群、武芸に優れ、特に跳躍や高所登攀、険地越えを得意とした。飛ぶように身軽に動き、陣中の突撃も俊敏で、雲へ舞い上がる金翅大鵬に似るため、「摩雲金翅」の雄壮な異名を得る。槍を熟練して使い、敵に勇敢な歴戦の猛将である。百八人では地闊星、第四十八の椅子に座り、馬軍小彪将兼遠探出哨頭領を務めた。

梁山への道は黄門山から始まる。江州で救われた宋江が好漢たちと入山へ向かい、黄門山を通ると、四人の寨主が道を遮った。筆頭が摩雲金翅欧鵬、残りは神算子蒋敬、鉄笛仙馬麟、九尾亀陶宗旺である。四人は山で義を結び、略奪して暮らしていた。大隊が通るのを見て迎えに下り、長く名を聞いていた及時雨宋公明だと知る。梁山の勢いと義気にも喜び、平伏し、黄門山を捨てて手勢を連れ、水泊の大寨へ赴くと申し出た。こうして四人が加わり、梁山はまた幾人もの好漢を得る。

入山後、欧鵬は大軍と南北を征し、戦えば必ず先へ立ち、敵陣へ突入し、城や寨を抜いて多くの功を立てた。熟れた槍と俊敏な勇は摩雲金翅の名に背かない。黄門山以来の兄弟にはそれぞれ本領があり、蒋敬は大量の銭糧を計算して出納を掌り、馬麟は鉄笛と双刀、陶宗旺は鉄鍬で土地を拓く力を持った。以前から生死を共にした四人は入山後も親しく、欧鵬は馬麟らと力を合わせ、互いを援護して戦う。大聚義では地煞として馬軍先鋒の偵察を任され、猛将の列にあって威名も衰えなかった。険地を越える身軽さと勇気は、百八人の中でも有用である。攻城や野戦では前哨に立って敵の虚実を探り、山に道を開き、敵と会えば先を争うため、宋江と盧俊義に深く頼られた。

招安後も宋江に従い、遼、河北の田虎、淮西の王慶を破って各地で戦功を重ね、昔の名声を保った。出征すれば常に先鋒偵察に入り、道を調べて突撃し、諸将と数十の戦場を血戦して退いたことがない。方臘を討つ江南では梁山の半数以上が失われ、欧鵬も戦没する。方臘は険要に拠り、能戦の将も多く、梁山は一城一地を取るたび死傷を重ね、血を流した。欧鵬が勇んで陣へ突入し、馬上で槍を構えて左右へ攻めていると、敵陣に潜む弓の名手が狙いを定める。不意の一矢をかわしきれず、乱矢の中で急所を射られ、落馬してその場で命を落とした。飛ぶように健やかで雲に届く名を持つ猛将が、江南に墜ちる。軍戸から落草、帰義を経て南北を戦い、最後は馬革に包まれて沙場へ身を捧げた。方臘平定後、朝廷は忠武郎を追贈し、その魂は故郷へ帰る。飛越の技、陣前の勇、義へ帰した誠は、今も語られる梁山の感慨深い物語である。

裴宣，京兆府人氏，原是本府六案孔目出身。所谓孔目，乃官府中掌管案牍、文书、刑名之.en:
Pei Xuan was a native of Jingzhao Prefecture, where he originally served as chief clerk of the six administrative offices. Such a clerk managed case records, official documents, and criminal matters, overseeing judicial files in a post that demanded particular respect for the law. Pei Xuan had studied from childhood and knew the classics and histories, but he was also an accomplished administrator and legal writer. Meticulous in his work, clear in rewards and punishments, and utterly fair in his judgments, he never bent the law for personal affection or advantage. For this the rivers and lakes gave him the name “Iron-Faced Clerk.” Though a civil functionary by background, he had also learned spear and staff techniques and wielded a pair of swords. He possessed considerable strength and was no ordinary frail scholar. Among Liangshan Marsh's 108 heroes, he corresponded to the Earthly Star of Uprightness and occupied the forty-seventh seat. His particular responsibility was the military administration office that assessed merit and assigned rewards and punishments, an essential civil post that judged the stronghold's achievements and faults.

Pei Xuan's road to Liangshan began when a corrupt official framed him, eventually driving him to outlawry at Yinma River. Upright by nature, he administered the law impartially and refused to flatter his superiors, thereby offending the prefect. The prefect found a pretext to have him tattooed as a criminal and exiled to Shamen Island. While his guards were escorting him through Yinma River, they encountered two heroes who ruled a mountain stronghold there: Yang Lin, the “Patterned Leopard,” and Deng Fei, the “Fiery-Eyed Lion.” Impressed by Pei Xuan's dignified appearance and cultivated speech, they asked about his misfortune. Respecting his incorruptibility, they killed or scattered the guards and rescued him, taking him up the mountain. Grateful to them for saving his life, Pei Xuan became an outlaw at Yinma River. His exceptional ability and fairness led Yang Lin and Deng Fei to make him the stronghold's chief, with both of them serving beneath him.

Later, the Liangshan heroes Dai Zong and Yang Lin passed through Yinma River while seeking news of Gongsun Sheng and met the stronghold's leaders. Pei Xuan and Deng Fei had long heard Liangshan's fame and already knew Yang Lin, so they readily reached an agreement. They willingly brought all their followers, abandoned Yinma River, and joined Liangshan's great stronghold together. Pei Xuan and his companions thus became part of the Liangshan company, adding several more heroes to its ranks.

Once Pei Xuan joined Liangshan, Song Jiang and Wu Yong entrusted him with assessing merit and administering rewards and punishments because of his established impartiality, clear judgment, and refusal to bow to influence. After every campaign, great or small, Pei Xuan fairly determined rewards for achievements and penalties for faults, missing nothing. Every leader accepted his decisions wholeheartedly. When the great assembly fixed Liangshan's ranks, he took his place as the Earthly Star of Uprightness, directing the office of military rewards and punishments and managing stronghold affairs alongside the other civil leaders. He played a crucial part in maintaining discipline and encouraging morale. His ability to enforce the rules impartially gave him a distinctive responsibility among the 108.

After the court granted amnesty, Pei Xuan accompanied Song Jiang's army against the Great Liao, then Tian Hu in Hebei and Wang Qing in Huaixi, and finally Fang La south of the Yangtze. Throughout these campaigns he managed military administration, rewards, and punishments rather than fighting personally at the front. More than half of Liangshan's heroes were killed or wounded in the bloody southern war, but his civil duties fortunately enabled him to survive, and his name remained among those who returned. When the victorious army reached court, Pei Xuan received an official rank in recognition of his service. Yet he was naturally indifferent to ambition. Seeing loyal men such as Song Jiang and Lu Junyi ultimately fall victim to treacherous ministers, and disheartened by the corruption of the world, he began to desire retirement. Unwilling to remain burdened by official life, he resigned and returned to Yinma River, where he lived freely in the mountains with his old acquaintance Yang Lin and came to a peaceful end. From an impartial chief clerk, to an unjustly condemned outlaw, to a pardoned servant of the court, he finally preserved himself through modest desires and retired among woods and streams. Among so many Liangshan heroes who died on the battlefield, such a fortunate ending was rare. The fairness of his judgments and the integrity of his character remain worthy of remembrance.
裴宣，京兆府人氏，原是本府六案孔目出身。所谓孔目，乃官府中掌管案牍、文书、刑名之.ja:
裴宣は京兆府の出身で、もとは同府の六案孔目を務めていた。孔目とは官庁の記録、文書、刑事案件を扱う吏員で、刑獄の書類を管理するため、とりわけ法を重んじる役目である。裴宣は幼い頃から学問に励み、経書や史書に通じていただけでなく、吏務にも熟達し、法律文書にも明るかった。仕事は緻密で賞罰は明確、裁断はどこまでも公正で、私情によって法を曲げることがない。そのため江湖では「鉄面孔目」と呼ばれた。文官の出ではあるが槍棒の武芸も習い、二振りの宝剣を使いこなす。腕力も強く、ただの文弱な書生ではなかった。梁山泊百八人のうちでは地正星に応じ、第四十七位に座す。功績を定め、賞罰を行う軍政司を専ら担当し、山寨の功罪を考課する重要な文職を担った。

裴宣が梁山泊へ入ったきっかけは、貪官に陥れられ、飲馬川で山賊となった一件にある。もともと正直な人物で、公平に法を執行し、上役におもねろうとしなかったため、府の知府の恨みを買った。知府は口実を設け、裴宣に罪人の入れ墨を施して沙門島への流刑に処した。護送の役人に連れられて飲馬川へ差しかかったところ、そこを根城とする二人の好漢に出会う。「錦豹子」の楊林と「火眼狻猊」の鄧飛である。二人は裴宣の堂々たる容貌と品のある物腰に目を留め、事情を聞くと、その私情に流されぬ人柄に敬意を抱いた。そして護送役人を討ち散らし、裴宣を救って山へ連れ帰った。命を救われた恩に感じた裴宣は飲馬川に身を落としたが、才略に優れ、処置も公平だったため、楊林と鄧飛はかえって彼を山寨の主に推した。こうして裴宣が大頭領となり、鄧飛と楊林はその下に座した。

のちに梁山泊の好漢、戴宗と楊林が公孫勝の行方を探して飲馬川を通り、山の頭領たちと出会った。裴宣と鄧飛はかねて梁山泊の名声を聞き、楊林とも旧知の間柄だったので、話はすぐにまとまった。二人は配下をすべて率いて飲馬川を捨て、共に梁山泊の大寨へ身を寄せることを願い出た。こうして裴宣らが仲間に加わり、梁山泊にはさらに数人の好漢が増えた。

入山した裴宣に対し、宋江と呉用は、その鉄面無私で賞罰を明らかにし、権勢にも屈しない人柄を認め、「定功賞罰」の任を専ら委ねた。山寨の大小の戦について、功に応じた褒賞も、過失に応じた処罰も、すべて裴宣が公平に裁定し、少しの誤りもなかったため、頭領たちは皆心から服した。梁山泊の大集会で序列が定まると、地正星に列せられ、軍政賞罰司を掌り、他の文職頭領と共に山寨の政務を取り仕切った。軍紀を保ち、士気を高めるうえで欠かせない人物であり、情けに左右されず法を守る働きは、百八人の中でも一つの役割を独力で担うものであった。

朝廷の招安後、裴宣は宋江の大軍に従い、まず大遼を破り、続いて河北の田虎、淮西の王慶を平定し、さらに江南の方臘を討った。各地を転戦する間も軍中の賞罰と軍政を掌り、自ら最前線で斬り合うことはなかった。江南の血戦では梁山泊の好漢の半数以上が死傷したが、裴宣は文職の軍政担当であったため幸いにも生き残り、南征から帰還した者の名簿に加わった。凱旋後、朝廷から功に応じて官位を授けられたものの、本来名利に淡泊であり、宋江や盧俊義のような忠義の士がついには奸臣に害されるのを見て、世の薄情さに隠退の思いを抱いた。これ以上官界に煩わされることを望まず、官職を辞し、旧地の飲馬川へ戻り、昔なじみの楊林と山林に隠れ住んだ。自由に暮らし、安らかな最期を迎えたのである。六案孔目から罪を着せられて山賊となり、山賊から帰順して朝廷に仕え、最後は淡泊な心で身を保ち、林泉に帰った。戦場に命を散らした梁山泊の多くの好漢に比べれば、まことに得難い幸福な結末だった。その法を執行する公平さと人としての正しさは、後世にも語り継がれている。

彭玘，颍州人氏，原系大宋朝廷军官，累世将门之后，因得祖上余荫，官拜团练使。其人面.en:
Peng Qi was a native of Yingzhou and originally an officer of the Great Song. Descended from generations of military commanders, he received an appointment as a militia commissioner through his family's inherited privilege. His face was dark red like ripe dates, and his eyes flashed coldly. On the battlefield they shone with an almost divine power to intimidate the enemy, earning him the name “Heavenly-Eyed General” both in the army and among the rivers and lakes. Fierce and proud, Peng Qi took great confidence in his military ancestry. An accomplished horseman and archer, he habitually wielded a three-pointed, double-edged saber with disciplined technique. Its blade flashed with a chilling presence when he faced an enemy, marking him as a formidable veteran. Among Liangshan Marsh's 108 heroes, he corresponded to the Earthly Star of Excellence, occupied the forty-third seat, and served among the junior cavalry commanders who also led distant scouting patrols.

The reason for Peng Qi's arrival at Liangshan begins with Huyan Zhuo's campaign against the stronghold. Liangshan Marsh was growing more powerful and had repeatedly defeated government troops, alarming the Eastern Capital. Marshal Gao recommended Huyan Zhuo, the military commander of Runing, to lead a punitive expedition. Huyan Zhuo in turn requested two deputies: Han Tao, the “Hundred-Victory General” and militia commissioner of Chenzhou, and Peng Qi, the “Heavenly-Eyed General” and militia commissioner of Yingzhou. The three commanders led elite troops against Liangshan Marsh. Huyan Zhuo deployed his linked cavalry, sending armored horses chained together to break the enemy formation. For a time Liangshan's forces could not withstand them and suffered heavily. Yet in the individual contests when the armies first faced each other, Peng Qi, brave as he was, proved no match for Liangshan's fierce champions.

Peng Qi rode forward to challenge the enemy, and Hu Sanniang, the “Ten-Foot Green,” galloped out from Liangshan's ranks to meet him. After a dozen or more exchanges, she deliberately exposed an opening, turned her horse, and fled. Eager to claim the first victory, Peng Qi boldly pursued. Unexpectedly, Hu Sanniang untied her red brocade lasso, spun around, and cast it straight over him. Taken completely by surprise, he was dragged down from his horse. Soldiers rushed forward, captured him alive, and brought him up the mountain. Peng Qi assumed he would be killed. Instead, Chao Gai and Song Jiang came down from the hall to greet him, personally untied his bonds, and honored him as a distinguished guest. They explained at length that they upheld Heaven's justice and opposed corrupt officials rather than the court itself. Song Jiang humbled himself and spoke earnestly. Moved by Liangshan's deep sense of loyalty and grateful that Song Jiang had spared him, Peng Qi changed his mind, bowed to the ground, and willingly joined. He abandoned his official position and became a Liangshan outlaw, serving alongside Han Tao and the others. Huyan Zhuo's formidable linked cavalry was later broken by the hooked-spear techniques of Xu Ning, the “Golden Spear.” Huyan Zhuo suffered a crushing defeat and eventually joined Liangshan too. The reunion of the three commanders in the Hall of Loyalty became a celebrated story.

After joining, Peng Qi repeatedly accompanied the army on campaign and always fought at the front. Often partnered with Han Tao, he charged enemy formations, stormed cities and strongholds, and earned considerable merit. At Liangshan's great assembly he was ranked among the Earthly Stars and assigned to cavalry vanguard and reconnaissance duties. Standing among the company's formidable generals, he retained his former reputation. With his three-pointed, double-edged saber in battle, he remained an experienced and fearless cavalry commander.

After the court granted amnesty, Song Jiang led Liangshan's forces against the Great Liao, then Tian Hu in Hebei and Wang Qing in Huaixi, campaigning far and wide. Peng Qi served throughout, bravely striving to be first and never diminishing the reputation of the “Heavenly-Eyed General.” When the army marched against Fang La south of the Yangtze, more than half of Liangshan's heroes were lost, and Peng Qi did not escape. During the siege of Changzhou, Fang La's defenders resisted desperately, showering arrows and stones from the walls. Peng Qi hurled himself into the assault. Amid the fierce fighting, a javelin cast down by an enemy commander struck a vital spot and killed him outright beneath the city walls. A fierce warrior from a military family, he had gone from militia commissioner to outlaw, then returned to loyal service. After campaigning north and south, he finally shed his blood on the battlefield and died a soldier's death. When Song Jiang later returned, the court granted posthumous honors to the fallen, Peng Qi among them. He received the title of Gentleman of Loyal Valor, and his spirit returned to Yingzhou. He could be said to have fulfilled his chosen duty and lived without betraying his ideals. Though his place among Liangshan's stars was not especially high, the courage inherited from his military family, the sincerity of his allegiance, and the devotion of his final sacrifice all deserved the admiration of later generations.
彭玘，颍州人氏，原系大宋朝廷军官，累世将门之后，因得祖上余荫，官拜团练使。其人面.ja:
彭玘は潁州の出身で、もとは大宋の軍官であった。代々武将を出した家柄に生まれ、祖先の蔭によって団練使に任じられた。顔は熟した棗のように赤く、目には冷たい光が宿っていた。戦場で両眼を輝かせる姿は、神威によって敵を威圧するかのようで、江湖でも軍中でも「天目将」と呼ばれた。気性は激しく誇り高く、将門の血筋を自負していた。弓馬に熟達し、三尖両刃刀を得物とする。厳密な刀法で刃を翻し、敵に迫る姿には冷気さえ感じられ、まさしく長く軍伍を経た猛将であった。梁山泊百八人のうちでは地英星に応じ、第四十三位に座し、馬軍の小彪将にして遠方の偵察を兼ねる頭領となった。

彭玘が山へ入った事情は、呼延灼の梁山泊征討から始まる。当時、梁山泊は勢いを増し、官軍を相次いで破って東京を驚かせていた。高太尉は汝寧郡の都統制、呼延灼を討伐軍の大将に推挙した。呼延灼はさらに補佐する副将として、陳州団練使の「百勝将」韓滔と、潁州団練使の「天目将」彭玘を願い出た。三将はそれぞれ精兵を率い、梁山泊へ攻め寄せた。呼延灼が連環馬の陣を敷き、鉄の鎧をまとわせた馬を連ねて突撃すると、梁山泊の軍勢はたちまち苦戦に陥り、大きな損害を受けた。しかし、両軍が初めて対峙し、武勇を競った個々の勝負では、彭玘は勇敢ではあっても、梁山泊の猛者たちには及ばなかった。

陣前で彭玘が馬を進めて挑戦すると、梁山泊から一丈青の扈三娘が駆け出して迎えた。十数合ほど打ち合ったところで、扈三娘はわざと隙を見せ、馬首を返して逃げた。彭玘は一番手柄を立てようと勇みに任せて追いかける。ところが扈三娘は紅錦の投げ縄を解き、突然振り向いて投げつけ、見事に彭玘を捕らえた。不意を突かれた彭玘は馬上から引き落とされ、押し寄せた兵に生け捕られて山へ連行された。死を覚悟していたが、晁蓋と宋江は堂を降りて出迎え、自ら縄を解き、上客の礼をもって遇した。そして天に代わって道を行い、貪官にのみ抗い、朝廷そのものに背くつもりはないと詳しく説いた。宋江は身を低くして誠実に語りかけた。彭玘は梁山泊の厚い義気を知り、命を奪われなかった恩にも感じ、心を改めてひれ伏し、仲間入りを願った。こうして官職を捨てて梁山泊に身を落とし、韓滔らと共に働くようになった。のちに呼延灼の強力な連環馬も、金槍手の徐寧が伝えた鉤鎌槍法に破られた。大敗した呼延灼もやがて帰順し、三将が聚義庁で再会したことは一つの美談となった。

入山後、彭玘は幾度も大軍に従って出征し、戦いでは必ず先頭に立った。韓滔と組むことが多く、敵陣へ突入し、城や砦を落として、多くの戦功を立てた。梁山泊の大集会で序列が定まると地煞に列せられ、馬軍の先鋒と斥候を担った。猛将たちと肩を並べ、その威名は昔にも劣らなかった。三尖両刃刀を振るって戦う姿は、なお梁山泊の馬軍を支える歴戦の勇将そのものであった。

朝廷の招安後、宋江は梁山泊の軍勢を率い、まず大遼を破り、次いで河北の田虎、淮西の王慶を平定し、各地を転戦した。彭玘はそのすべてに従軍し、勇んで先を争い、「天目将」の威名を落とすことはなかった。だが江南の方臘征討では、梁山泊の好漢が半数以上も失われ、彭玘も難を免れなかった。常州の戦いで梁山泊軍が城を囲むと、方臘配下の守将は必死に抵抗し、城壁から矢や石を雨のように降らせた。彭玘は身を挺して攻城に当たったが、激戦のさなか、敵将の投げ下ろした標槍が急所に命中し、その場で息絶え、常州城下に命を落とした。将門の猛将が団練使から山賊となり、山賊から帰順して南北を転戦し、最後は戦場に血を流して軍人としての死を迎えたのである。のちに宋江が帰還すると、朝廷は戦死した諸将に追贈を行い、彭玘にも忠武郎の官が贈られた。その魂は故郷の潁州へ帰った。自ら求めた義を貫き、一生に背かなかったといえよう。梁山泊の星々の中で位は高くなくとも、将門の勇、帰義の誠、身命を捧げた烈しさは、いずれも後世の称賛に値する。

秦明，表字不传，原系开州人氏，乃后周大将秦彦之后，世居青州，做青州指挥司总管本州.en:
Qin Ming, whose courtesy name is unrecorded, was originally from Kaizhou and descended from Qin Yan, a great general of the Later Zhou. His family had long lived in Qingzhou, where he became commander of the prefecture's troops under its military headquarters. Fiery by nature, impatient and bluntly upright, he raged like racing thunder and flashing lightning whenever angered. Thus the rivers and lakes called him “Thunderbolt.” He stood an imposing eight chi tall, with thick brows, fierce eyes, a broad mouth, and a curling beard: every inch a formidable warrior. Qin Ming wielded a wolf-toothed mace heavier than the usual kind. It roared through the air when he swung it, and no host seemed able to withstand his charges. His ferocity was renowned throughout the regional armies.

Below Qingfeng Mountain, Hua Rong incurred the enmity of Liu Gao, the civil commandant of Qingfeng Fort, while trying to rescue Song Jiang. The affair grew ever more serious after some outlaws captured Liu Gao's wife and Song Jiang narrowly escaped being framed. On receiving the report, Qingzhou's prefect, Murong Yanda, sent Qin Ming with government troops to suppress them. Impatient and trusting too much in his courage, Qin Ming advanced rashly. Hua Rong, Yan Shun, and the others lured him into a mountain hollow. However formidable his mace, it could not defeat trip ropes, hidden pits, rolling logs, and falling stones. Exhausted with his horse, he tumbled into a pit and was captured alive and taken up the mountain. Song Jiang and Hua Rong treated him courteously and urged him to join them, but Qin Ming declared that a man who received his sovereign's salary must serve him loyally. He would rather die than rebel and insisted on returning to Qingzhou. Unable to persuade him to stay, they let him descend. Yet Song Jiang had secretly arranged a scheme. That night he sent a man disguised as Qin Ming, riding Qin Ming's horse and carrying his wolf-toothed mace, to kill and burn around Qingzhou. Houses outside the city were reduced to ashes, and the people suffered terribly. When Qin Ming returned the next day, Prefect Murong stood on the wall, pointed at the scorched land, and cursed him as a rebel who had harmed the people. He had also beheaded Qin Ming's entire family, displaying his wife's severed head above the city. Qin Ming could not make his innocence heard and had nowhere to go. His family and home destroyed, utterly alone and without recourse, he returned to the mountain stronghold and committed himself to outlawry. Seeing him homeless, Song Jiang arranged for him to marry Hua Rong's younger sister, binding him through a generous favor. The deception that won Qin Ming was ruthless, yet it also brought Liangshan a warrior capable of facing ten thousand. It is an episode in the tale that inspires both dismay and astonishment.

After joining Liangshan, Qin Ming repeatedly won distinction, often serving in the vanguard in sieges and open battle. Later, the bands from Qingfeng Mountain, Duiying Mountain, and other places merged, and he accompanied the combined force to the marsh, winning merit in campaigns north and south. When Liangshan's great assembly brought together the full company of thirty-six Heavenly and seventy-two Earthly Stars, Qin Ming ranked seventh among the Heavenly Stars, corresponding to the Heavenly Star of Ferocity. He became one of the Five Tiger Generals of the cavalry alongside Guan Sheng, Lin Chong, Huyan Zhuo, and Dong Ping. This showed how highly his courage was valued and how firmly he stood among the stronghold's pillars. In every major battle his wolf-toothed mace swept back and forth at the front. His desperate single combats with celebrated government commanders were often decided by the narrowest margin and made for especially thrilling encounters.

After Song Jiang accepted the court's amnesty, Qin Ming fought in the campaign against Liao and helped defeat Tian Hu and Wang Qing. He campaigned north and south, felling countless enemy commanders with his mace and earning great merit for the state. In this way he fulfilled his original resolve to serve his sovereign and country. This time he fought beneath the true emperor's banners and no longer faced the divided loyalties he had suffered at Qingfeng Mountain. During the expedition against Fang La south of the Yangtze, however, Liangshan's heroes fell in terrible numbers, with more than half killed or wounded. Qin Ming reached Bangyuan Cave near Qingxi and faced Fang Jie, Fang La's nephew and a leading general. Young, brave, and highly skilled, Fang Jie wielded a painted crescent halberd. He and Qin Ming fought more than thirty exchanges without a victor. Then Fang La's state preceptor, the sorcerer Zheng Biao, known as Demon Lord Zheng, secretly intervened with magic. Momentarily distracted, Qin Ming exposed an opening. Fang Jie drove his halberd into him and followed with another thrust. The heroic “Thunderbolt” thus died amid the battle through sorcery, his end both valiant and desolate. Qin Ming was among the loyal warriors later honored posthumously by the court. From Qingzhou's troop commander to one of the marsh's Five Tiger Generals, then a renowned southern campaign commander who gave his life for the country, this true hero lived with a courage as fierce as his name: a thunderclap whose blaze shone upon all.
秦明，表字不传，原系开州人氏，乃后周大将秦彦之后，世居青州，做青州指挥司总管本州.ja:
秦明は字を伝えられていない。もとは開州の人で、後周の大将、秦彦の末裔に当たり、代々青州に住み、青州指揮司で同州の兵馬を総管する統制を務めていた。火のように烈しく、短気で実直な性格で、ひとたび怒ると雷が走り稲妻が交わるようだったため、江湖では「霹靂火」と呼ばれた。堂々たる体は八尺に達し、濃い眉、怒りを含んだ目、大きな口、巻いた髭を持つ、威風あふれる猛将である。得物は普通よりも重い狼牙棒で、振るえば風を切って唸り、戦場を突き進めば万夫も当たることができなかった。その勇猛さは各地の軍中に知られていた。

清風山の麓で、花栄は宋江を救うため清風寨の知寨、劉高と対立した。さらに手下が劉高の妻を捕らえ、宋江が危うく陥れられるなどして、事件はますます大きくなった。報告を受けた青州知府の慕容彦達は、秦明に官軍を率いて討伐するよう命じた。短気な秦明は武勇を頼みに軽々しく進み、花栄や燕順らの計略によって山の窪地へ誘い込まれた。狼牙棒がどれほど強くても、好漢たちの馬を倒す縄、落とし穴、転がす丸太や落石には抗えない。人馬とも疲れ果てた末、馬もろとも落とし穴に落ち、生け捕られて山へ連行された。宋江や花栄は礼をもって遇し、仲間に加わるよう勧めたが、秦明は君の禄を食む者は君に忠を尽くすべきだと言い、死んでも背くことはできないと青州への帰還を言い張った。引き留めきれず、皆は山を下りることを許した。しかし宋江は密かに策を仕込んでいた。その夜、人を秦明に変装させ、秦明の馬に乗せ、狼牙棒を持たせて、青州城外で殺人と放火を働かせたのである。周辺の家々は灰となり、民は惨禍を受けた。翌日、秦明が城下へ戻ると、慕容知府は城壁の上から焼け野原を指して罵り、民を害した謀反人だと決めつけた。さらに一家をことごとく斬首し、妻の首を城頭に高くさらしていた。秦明は無実を訴えることもできず、進退の道を失った。家も家族も失って独りとなり、ほかにすべもなく山寨へ戻り、以後は心を定めて山賊となった。宋江は帰る家のない彼のため、花栄の妹を妻に迎えさせ、厚意によって結びつきを強めた。この「秦明を陥れて引き入れる」一件は、手段こそ苛烈であったが、梁山泊に万人敵の猛将をもたらした。物語の中でも、痛惜と驚きを同時に覚えさせる場面である。

梁山泊に加わった秦明はたびたび戦功を挙げ、攻城でも野戦でも先鋒を務めることが多かった。のちに清風山、対影山など各地の軍勢が合流すると、大部隊に従って水泊へ向かい、南北の征戦で功を重ねた。梁山泊の大集会で天罡三十六、地煞七十二の数がそろうと、秦明は天罡の第七位、天猛星に列せられた。馬軍五虎将の一人となり、関勝、林冲、呼延灼、董平と並び称されたことは、その武勇が群を抜き、山寨の柱として重んじられていた証である。大きな戦いのたび、秦明の狼牙棒は陣前を縦横に走った。官軍の名将との一騎打ちは死力を尽くすもので、勝敗が紙一重で決まることも多く、ことに手に汗握る戦いであった。

宋江が朝廷の招安を受けた後、秦明は遼国征討に従い、さらに田虎と王慶を破った。南北を転戦し、狼牙棒で数知れぬ敵将を倒し、国のために大きな功を立てた。かつて抱いた「君に忠を尽くして国に報いる」という初心を、ここで果たしたともいえる。この時は真の天子の旗の下にあり、清風山で味わったような板挟みに悩む必要もなかった。だが江南の方臘征討では、梁山泊の好漢が次々と死傷し、その半数以上が失われた。秦明は清渓の幇源洞前まで攻め進み、方臘配下の大将で皇甥に当たる方傑と戦った。方傑は方天画戟を使い、若く勇猛で武芸に熟達しており、三十余合を戦っても勝負はつかなかった。その時、方臘の国師である妖術使いの鄭彪、すなわち鄭魔君が、陣中から密かに妖法で加勢した。秦明が一瞬気を取られると、方傑は隙を見抜いて戟を突き込み、さらに追い打ちを加えた。あわれ、一代の英雄「霹靂火」は乱軍と妖術の中で陣前に倒れ、壮烈にして寂しい最期を遂げた。のちに朝廷が義士たちを追封した際、秦明もその列に加わった。雷火のような気性を持つ真の豪傑は、青州の兵馬総管から水泊の五虎上将となり、最後は国に命を捧げる征南の名将となった。その勇烈な生涯は、まさに異名のとおり、一声の霹靂とともに光を放つものであった。

阮小二，绰号「立地太岁」，应天剑星，梁山泊英雄座次第二十七位，乃水军头领之一。其.en:
Ruan Xiaoer, nicknamed “Earthbound Tai Sui,” corresponded to the Heavenly Star of Sword and ranked twenty-seventh among Liangshan Marsh's heroes, serving as one of its naval commanders. He came from Shijie Village beside Liangshan Marsh in Jizhou and lived with his brothers Ruan Xiaowu and Ruan Xiaoqi. Their family had fished for generations, while also engaging in some less respectable activities on the marsh. The three Ruan brothers were desperate heroes, risking their lives by the blade both on land and in the water. Ruan Xiaoer, the eldest, was steady and experienced, extraordinarily strong, and fiery in temper, yet possessed a mind of his own. People throughout the rivers and lakes regarded him with awe and gave him the fearsome name “Earthbound Tai Sui.” Tai Sui was a baleful deity whose domain must never be disturbed, a measure of the dread his presence inspired. All three brothers went bare-chested in the water, could remain submerged for long periods, and moved through waves and over billows as easily as on level ground. They were born masters of the water.

Ruan Xiaoer's road to Liangshan began with the great affair of the birthday convoy robbery. Chao Gai, the village headman of Dongxi, joined Wu Yong, Gongsun Sheng, and others in plotting to seize birthday gifts worth one hundred thousand strings of cash, sent by Secretary Liang from Daming Prefecture in the Northern Capital to the Eastern Capital. They needed several strong, courageous men willing to risk their lives. Wu Yong thought of the three Ruan brothers of Shijie Village and went there personally to recruit them. The episode in which Wu Yong persuaded the brothers to join the scheme revealed their heroic spirit in full. Government restrictions on fishing, together with bandits' control of the marsh, had made their livelihood difficult and left their households impoverished. They were seething with frustration. Wu Yong provoked them with his words, and they readily agreed, declaring together that it was better to stake everything on one venture than go on living so miserably. Thus Chao Gai, Wu Yong, Gongsun Sheng, Liu Tang, Bai Sheng, and the three Ruan brothers, seven men in all, joined forces at Yellow Mud Ridge. Disguised as jujube merchants, they drugged Yang Zhi and his escort, seized the birthday convoy, and made off. This was the first earthshaking crime that opened Liangshan's enterprise, and Ruan Xiaoer and his two brothers were central to that gathering of seven stars.

When the robbery came to light, the authorities sent men to make arrests. Chao Gai's party clashed with Lin Chong, outwitted Wang Lun, and took possession of Liangshan Marsh. Ruan Xiaoer then assumed joint command of the navy with Ruan Xiaowu and Ruan Xiaoqi, forming the foundation of Liangshan's water stronghold. Government troops attacked repeatedly thereafter, and the defense of the waterways depended on the brothers' desperate fighting. When He Tao of Jizhou led troops to capture them, the brothers destroyed his force in the marshes. In the later campaigns that twice defeated Tong Guan and three times defeated Gao Qiu, they laid ambushes underwater, pierced hulls, and overturned boats, earning countless achievements. When the great assembly fixed the ranks, Ruan Xiaoer was assigned the Heavenly Star of Sword among the Heavenly Stars. As a naval commander, he directed the stronghold's fleet together with Li Jun, Zhang Heng, Zhang Shun, and others, holding a position of great importance.

After the amnesty, Ruan Xiaoer followed the army against Liao, Tian Hu, and Wang Qing, always taking the vanguard in naval engagements. The expedition against Fang La brought them to the waterways south of the Yangtze, ideal ground for naval warfare. The three Ruan brothers and the other naval commanders sank enemy vessels and launched successive fire attacks, repeatedly winning remarkable victories, but also suffering cruel turns of fortune. Ruan Xiaoer met his end in one of these terrible naval battles. While the army attacked the Wulong Ridge and Qingxi area held by Fang La, he and the navy took their boats deep into enemy waters and fell into an ambush. The enemy blocked the channels with iron chains and fire rafts, setting fires on every side. Ruan Xiaoer's boat was surrounded by burning rafts, with no way forward or back, and capture appeared inevitable. Rather than endure humiliation in enemy hands, the hard man of Shijie Village drew the saber at his waist. Amid raging flames and thick smoke, he cut his own throat and plunged into the water, preserving a hero's integrity through death. Beginning with the birthday convoy robbery and ranging through the marshes for decades, “Earthbound Tai Sui” finally perished amid the storms and fires of the south. When Song Jiang returned, the navy's achievements were recalled, and Ruan Xiaoer received posthumous honors as one of the fallen, joining Liangshan's heroic dead in commemoration. Of the three brothers, only Ruan Xiaoqi survived; the other two died in the campaign against Fang La. The brothers who once roamed Shijie Village together were forever separated by death, a cause for bitter regret.
阮小二，绰号「立地太岁」，应天剑星，梁山泊英雄座次第二十七位，乃水军头领之一。其.ja:
阮小二は「立地太歳」の異名を持ち、天剣星に応じる梁山泊第二十七位の英雄で、水軍頭領の一人である。済州の梁山泊近くにある石碣村の出身で、弟の阮小五、阮小七と共に暮らしていた。家は代々漁を生業とし、そのかたわら水泊で堅気とはいえない稼業にも手を染めていた。阮氏の三兄弟はいずれも水陸を問わず刃の上に命を懸ける無頼の好漢だった。長兄の阮小二は落ち着きと経験があり、並外れた腕力を持ち、火のような気性の中にも自分の考えを備えていた。江湖の者たちは彼を畏れ、「立地太歳」という恐ろしげな渾名をつけた。太歳とは、そのいる場所を犯してはならない凶神であり、この名からも彼の威圧の強さが知れる。三兄弟は皆、裸の上半身で水中を自在に行き来し、長く潜っていられた。波をくぐり、うねりを踏むこと平地を歩くがごとく、まさに生まれつきの水の強者であった。

阮小二が梁山泊へ向かう縁は、「生辰綱を智取する」という大事件に始まった。東渓村の保正、晁蓋は呉用、公孫勝らと共に、北京大名府の梁中書が東京へ送る十万貫の誕生祝いの荷を奪おうと計画した。そのためには、力と胆力があり、命を惜しまぬ好漢が数人必要だった。呉用は石碣村の阮氏三兄弟を思い出し、自ら村へ説得に赴いた。「呉用が知略をもって三阮を仲間に引き入れる」くだりには、三兄弟の英雄らしい気概がよく表れている。当時は役所が漁を制限し、水泊も賊に占められていたため、漁猟は難しく、家計も苦しくなり、三兄弟は鬱屈を抱えていた。呉用に言葉で奮い立たされると、三人は快く承知し、こんな惨めな暮らしを続けるくらいなら一勝負してみようと声をそろえた。こうして晁蓋、呉用、公孫勝、劉唐、白勝と三阮は、合わせて七人で結義し、黄泥岡に集まった。棗を売る商人に化け、護送役の楊志一行をしびれ薬で眠らせ、生辰綱を奪って悠々と立ち去った。これは梁山泊の事業の幕開けを告げる最初の大事件であり、阮小二と二人の弟は、この七星の結義の中核を担っていた。

事件が発覚すると、官府は捕り手を差し向けた。晁蓋の一行は林冲と内紛で争い、王倫を計略にかけて梁山泊を奪った。阮小二は阮小五、阮小七と共に水軍を掌り、梁山泊の水寨の基礎となった。その後、官軍が繰り返し討伐に来るたび、水路の守りは三阮の奮戦に頼った。済州府の何涛が兵を率いて捕らえに来た時には、水辺でその軍を壊滅させた。さらに童貫を二度破り、高俅を三度退けた戦いでも、水中に伏兵を置き、船底を穿ち、舟を覆して、数多くの功を挙げた。大集会で序列が定まると、阮小二は「天剣星」として天罡に列せられ、水軍頭領となった。李俊、張横、張順らと共に山寨の水師を統べる、重い地位であった。

招安後、阮小二は大軍に従って遼を征し、田虎と王慶を討ち、水戦では必ず先鋒を務めた。方臘への南征では、江南の水郷が水軍の力を発揮する舞台となった。三阮と他の水軍将領は敵艦を沈め、火攻めを重ねて奇功を挙げたが、同時に苛酷な運命にも見舞われた。阮小二も、この凄惨な水戦で最期を迎えた。大軍が方臘の烏竜嶺、清渓一帯を攻めた際、阮小二は水軍と船で深く入り込み、伏兵に遭った。敵は鉄鎖と火筏で水路を塞ぎ、四方から火を放った。乗船は火筏に囲まれ、進退の道がなく、捕虜となるのは目前だった。石碣村の剛勇な男は、敵の手に落ちて辱めを受けるくらいなら死を選ぶと、腰刀を抜いた。烈火と濃煙の中で自ら喉を切り、水に身を投じ、死をもって好漢の節義を守ったのである。「立地太歳」は生辰綱の智取から身を起こし、幾十年も水泊を縦横に駆けた末、江南の風波と炎の中に葬られた。のちに宋江が帰還して水軍の功を追叙した際、阮小二も戦死者として追封され、梁山泊の英烈と共に祀られた。三兄弟のうち生還したのは阮小七だけで、他の二人は方臘戦で死んだ。かつて石碣村を連れ立って行き来した兄弟は、ここに生死を隔てて永遠に別れることとなり、痛惜を禁じ得ない。

阮小七，济州梁山泊石碣村人氏，阮氏三雄中排行最末，故乡邻唤作阮小七。其家世代以打.en:
Ruan Xiaoqi came from Shijie Village at Liangshan Marsh in Jizhou. He was the youngest of the three Ruan heroes, known in his home village as Ruan Xiaoqi. His family had fished for generations, living among lakes and waterways with boats for their homes and wind and waves for companions. All three brothers, Ruan Xiaoer, Ruan Xiaowu, and Ruan Xiaoqi, were heroes of the water: tall, powerful, and thoroughly at ease in it. They could remain beneath the surface for seven days and seven nights and travel over the water as if on level ground, men truly born in the waves and sustained by the billows. Although the youngest, Ruan Xiaoqi was the most hot-tempered and unyielding. Fearless in danger, he dared to fight and kill. His ferocity, willingness to face death, and fiery nature earned him the nickname “Living King of Hell.” It likened his murderous presence to the underworld king who ruled over life and death, appearing in the mortal world: meeting him was like meeting a judge come to claim one's life.

Ruan Xiaoqi was rugged and imposing, with thick brows, large eyes, broad shoulders and arms, and a bare body knotted with muscle. He was equally capable in and out of the water. In everyday life he wore a green bamboo-leaf hat and straw rain cape, stood barefoot on the bow with a fishing spear in hand, and traveled through Liangshan's eight-hundred-li marsh. He loved freedom above all and could not tolerate restraint. Long angered by official extortion and burdensome fishing taxes, he had already accumulated a deep sense of injustice.

Before the birthday convoy robbery, Chao Gai, Wu Yong, and their companions planned to seize the gold, pearls, and other treasures worth one hundred thousand strings of cash offered by Secretary Liang. They needed trustworthy heroes with strength and courage, and Wu Yong recommended the three Ruan brothers of Shijie Village. He went there himself to invite them, drinking and discussing affairs with them to test their resolve. When the conversation turned to official injustice and the lack of any path for able men, Ruan Xiaoqi struck the table and rose, declaring, “This hot blood of mine is only for someone who knows its worth!” The brothers joined the company. Together with Chao Gai, Wu Yong, Gongsun Sheng, Liu Tang, and Bai Sheng, the seven men drugged Yang Zhi, the “Blue-Faced Beast,” and his escort at Yellow Mud Ridge and cleverly seized the birthday convoy. When the crime was discovered, the authorities ordered Jizhou to make arrests, and He Tao led government troops into the countryside. The brothers were ready. They lured the troops deep into the marsh and ambushed them among the reeds. Ruan Xiaoqi handled his boat and the water with mastery, helping throw the soldiers into complete confusion and annihilate them. The brothers then followed Chao Gai and the others in overthrowing Wang Lun, entered Liangshan, and became leaders of the stronghold.

When Liangshan's 108 commanders assembled, Ruan Xiaoqi ranked thirty-first among the Heavenly Stars, corresponding to the Heavenly Star of Defeat. He shared naval command with Ruan Xiaoer and Ruan Xiaowu, overseeing the stronghold's harbors, channels, and boats. Fighting on the water, patrols, and support operations all depended on the brothers. Many of Liangshan's victories over government armies involved naval combat. The brothers steered boats through the tides, pierced enemy hulls, captured commanders, and won countless distinctions. One especially satisfying victory came when Gao Qiu led a great army against Liangshan aboard large sea-loach warships. Ruan Xiaoqi dived underwater, breached the government ships, captured Marshal Gao alive, and took him up the mountain. Song Jiang then insisted on seeking amnesty and treated the captive to a banquet. This deeply displeased Ruan Xiaoqi, who had been utterly opposed to amnesty from the beginning.

After the amnesty, Ruan Xiaoqi followed the army against Liao, then Tian Hu and Wang Qing, repeatedly winning exceptional merit in naval battles. During the campaign against Fang La, the dense waterways south of the Yangtze offered the brothers ample scope for their skill, but the war was brutal. Ruan Xiaoer and Ruan Xiaowu were killed in succession, leaving Ruan Xiaoqi the sole survivor of the three. At Wulong Ridge, Qingxi Cave, and elsewhere, he continued to fight bravely at the front, avenging his elder brothers. Once Fang La had been defeated, Ruan Xiaoqi seized the ocher-yellow imperial dragon robe and ceremonial flat-topped crown that the rebel had assumed for himself at Wulong Ridge. On a playful impulse he put them on and pretended to be the emperor. It was simply the mischievous spirit of a child of the waterways, without any intention of usurping the throne. Treacherous ministers nevertheless took offense. On his return, the court rewarded his service by appointing him commander of Gaitian Army, but old enemies such as Tong Guan and Cai Jing accused him of privately wearing an imperial robe and harboring rebellious intentions. Their impeachment led to the removal of his commission and his reduction to commoner status.

Broad-minded as he was, Ruan Xiaoqi took no offense. Instead, he felt he had escaped the prison of official life, a change perfectly suited to his love of freedom. He took his aged mother back to their old home in Shijie Village and resumed fishing. Wearing his straw cape and bamboo-leaf hat, he sailed Liangshan Marsh and lived freely into old age, dying a natural death at sixty. Of the three brothers, he alone reached a peaceful end, returning to the misty waters of the rivers and lakes. The life of the “Living King of Hell” began and ended on the water. Fierce as the underworld king in battle, yet free as a drifting cloud in the wider world, he enjoyed one of the rare untroubled endings among the heroes of Water Margin.
阮小七，济州梁山泊石碣村人氏，阮氏三雄中排行最末，故乡邻唤作阮小七。其家世代以打.ja:
阮小七は済州梁山泊の石碣村の出身である。阮氏三兄弟の末弟に当たり、故郷の人々から阮小七と呼ばれていた。家は代々漁を生業とし、水郷に暮らして舟を住まいとし、風と波を友としてきた。阮小二、阮小五、阮小七はいずれも水中の豪傑で、背が高く力が強く、水性に慣れていた。水底に七日七夜も潜み、水面を平地のように行き来することができ、まさしく波の中に生まれ、波の中に生きる好漢だった。阮小七は最も若かったが、気性は誰よりも激しく剛直で、何事も恐れず、命を懸けて戦い、斬り合うことをためらわなかった。その凶猛さと死をも恐れぬ火のような性格から、郷里では「活閻羅」と呼ばれた。殺気をみなぎらせる姿が、人の生死を司る冥府の閻魔王が現世へ現れたかのようで、彼に出くわすことは、命を取り立てる判官に出会うようなものだという意味である。

阮小七は粗野ながら豪壮な姿で、眉は濃く目は大きく、肩や腕は幅広く、裸の体には筋肉が盛り上がっていた。水中でも陸上でも優れた働き手である。普段は青い竹の葉の笠をかぶり、蓑をまとい、裸足で舳先に立って魚叉を持ち、八百里の梁山泊を行き来していた。何よりも自由を好み、束縛を嫌った。役所の搾取や重い漁税にいつも憤り、胸には早くから不平の火が積もっていた。

生辰綱の智取に先立ち、晁蓋や呉用らは梁中書の献上する十万貫の金珠財宝を奪おうと企て、力と胆力があり、信頼できる好漢を探していた。呉用は石碣村の三阮を推し、自ら村へ誘いに赴いた。酒を酌み交わしながら世のことを語り、三兄弟の志を試したのである。役所の不公正や、英雄に進む道がないことに話が及ぶと、阮小七は卓を叩いて立ち上がり、「この熱い血は、その値打ちを知る相手にこそ売るのだ！」と言い放った。三阮は仲間に加わり、晁蓋、呉用、公孫勝、劉唐、白勝と合わせて七人で、黄泥岡において青面獣の楊志一行をしびれ薬で眠らせ、生辰綱を奪った。事件が発覚すると、官府は済州府に捕縛を命じ、何涛が官兵を率いて村へ来た。三阮はすでに備えており、官軍を水泊の奥へ誘い、葦原に伏兵を置いた。阮小七は舟と水を自在に操り、官兵を散々に打ち破って壊滅させた。その後、三阮は晁蓋らと共に王倫を倒して梁山泊へ入り、山寨の頭領となった。

梁山泊の百八将が集まると、阮小七は天罡の天敗星に応じ、第三十一位に座した。阮小二、阮小五と共に水軍頭領を務め、水寨の港、分流、船を管理した。水上の戦、巡回、味方の迎接や支援は、いずれも三阮の力に頼っていた。梁山泊が官軍を破った戦いには水戦が多く、三兄弟は舟で潮を乗りこなし、船底を穿ち、将を捕らえて、数多くの功を立てた。とりわけ痛快だったのは、高俅が海鰍の大船に乗り、大軍を率いて梁山泊を囲んだ時のことである。阮小七は水底へ潜って官船に穴を開け、高太尉を生け捕りにして山へ送った。ところが宋江は招安を強く主張し、酒宴を設けて高俅をもてなした。もともと招安にまったく気乗りしていなかった阮小七は、これを大いに不満に思った。

招安後、阮小七は大軍に従って遼国を征し、さらに田虎、王慶を討ち、水戦で幾度も奇功を挙げた。方臘征討では、水路が縦横に走る江南が三阮の働く舞台となったが、戦いは惨烈だった。阮小二と阮小五が相次いで戦死し、三兄弟のうち阮小七だけが残った。烏竜嶺や清渓洞などの戦いでも勇んで先頭に立ち、兄たちの仇を討った。方臘が平定されると、阮小七は烏竜嶺で、方臘が勝手に作らせた赭黄色の龍袍と平天冠を手に入れた。一時の悪ふざけでそれを身につけ、天子の真似をしたのである。水郷育ちのいたずらっ子の気質が出ただけで、帝位を侵す心はなかった。しかし奸臣たちはこのことを問題視した。帰朝後、朝廷は功に応じて阮小七を蓋天軍都統制に任じたが、童貫や蔡京ら旧来の敵は、「私に龍袍を着て不軌を企てた」として弾劾した。ついに官の辞令を取り上げられ、庶民へ落とされてしまった。

阮小七は度量が広く、さほど気にしなかった。むしろ官界の牢から抜け出せたと感じ、自由を好む本性には好都合だった。老母を連れて石碣村の旧居へ戻り、再び漁を生業とした。蓑と竹の葉の笠を身につけて梁山泊に舟を浮かべ、のびやかに老い、六十歳で天寿を全うした。三阮のうち安らかな最期を得たのは彼だけであり、江湖の霞む水辺へ帰ったのである。「活閻羅」の一生は水に始まり、水に帰した。戦場では閻魔のように凶猛でありながら、江湖では流れる雲のように自由であった。水滸の群雄の中でも、まれに見る清らかでおおらかな結末といえよう。

阮小五，绰号「短命二郎」，应天罪星，梁山泊英雄座次第二十九位，乃水军头领之一。其.en:
Ruan Xiaowu, nicknamed “Short-Lived Second Brother,” corresponded to the Heavenly Star of Guilt and ranked twenty-ninth among Liangshan Marsh's heroes, serving as one of its naval commanders. He came from Shijie Village beside Liangshan Marsh in Jizhou and lived with his elder brother Ruan Xiaoer and younger brother Ruan Xiaoqi. Their family had fished for generations, while also pursuing illicit business on the marsh, including murder and robbery. The three Ruan brothers were desperate heroes who risked their lives without hesitation on land or in the water. Ruan Xiaowu, the middle brother, was alert and fierce, with a murderous gleam in his eyes. He loved gambling and displays of temper and was especially ruthless and decisive in action. His nickname, “Short-Lived Second Brother,” meant that anyone who encountered him was as unlikely to survive as someone meeting a baleful star come to claim a life, a measure of his deadly presence. He had a blue mark on his forehead and a dark blue leopard tattooed on his chest. Habitually wearing a ragged headcloth askew, he went bare-chested in the water, could remain submerged for long periods, and moved freely through waves and billows: a born master of the water. When Wu Yong first visited Shijie Village to find the brothers, he saw Ruan Xiaowu gambling away everything he had, a glimpse of his willful love of the gaming table.

Like his brothers, Ruan Xiaowu came to Liangshan through the great affair of the birthday convoy robbery. Chao Gai, the village headman of Dongxi, and Wu Yong planned to seize birthday gifts worth one hundred thousand strings of cash, sent by Secretary Liang of Daming Prefecture to Grand Preceptor Cai in the Eastern Capital. They needed several strong, courageous heroes to help them. Wu Yong therefore went personally to Shijie Village to persuade the brothers. The episode in which he cleverly recruited the three revealed their courage and spirit in full. Government bans on fishing and bandits' occupation of the marsh had made their livelihood difficult and impoverished their households. Their hearts were full of frustration. Ruan Xiaowu spoke with particular fervor, declaring that he would dare to take a chance even on a venture of such immense consequence, since it was better than living so wretchedly. Thus Chao Gai, Wu Yong, Gongsun Sheng, Liu Tang, Bai Sheng, and the three brothers, seven men in all, disguised themselves as jujube merchants at Yellow Mud Ridge. They drugged Yang Zhi and his escort, seized the birthday convoy, and made off. This was the first earthshaking crime that opened Liangshan's enterprise, and Ruan Xiaowu was one of the central figures in that gathering of seven stars.

When the affair was exposed, the authorities sent He Tao of Jizhou with troops to arrest them. The three brothers crushed the soldiers among the reeds and marshes, throwing them into total confusion and leaving the force destroyed. Chao Gai's party then overthrew Wang Lun and took Liangshan by strategy, gaining control of the marsh. Ruan Xiaowu shared command of the navy with Ruan Xiaoer and Ruan Xiaoqi, forming the foundation of Liangshan's water stronghold. In the subsequent campaigns that twice defeated Tong Guan and three times defeated Gao Qiu, the brothers laid underwater ambushes, pierced hulls, overturned boats, and captured government commanders alive, earning countless distinctions. When the great assembly fixed the ranks, Ruan Xiaowu was assigned the Heavenly Star of Guilt among the Heavenly Stars. As a naval commander, he directed the stronghold's fleet together with Li Jun, Zhang Heng, Zhang Shun, and others.

After the amnesty, Ruan Xiaowu accompanied the army against Liao, Tian Hu, and Wang Qing, always taking the vanguard in naval engagements. The southern expedition against Fang La brought them to Jiangnan's intricate network of waterways, ideal ground for the navy. The three Ruan brothers and the other naval commanders sank enemy warships and launched successive fire attacks, repeatedly winning remarkable victories, yet fortune treated them cruelly. Ruan Xiaowu met his end in this terrible campaign. When the army attacked Qingxi and the Bangyuan Cave area held by Fang La, he accompanied the advance by boat into enemy territory and fought the opposing commanders. During one chaotic engagement he was surrounded by the troops of one of Fang La's leading officials, identified in the commonly circulated edition as Chancellor Lou. Hopelessly outnumbered, he was killed amid the fighting. Thus “Short-Lived Second Brother” died in royal service, meeting a soldier's death and departing the world forever. The three brothers had joined Liangshan together, commanded the navy together, and campaigned against Fang La together, but only Ruan Xiaoqi survived. Ruan Xiaoer cut his own throat, and Ruan Xiaowu fell in battle. The brothers who had once roamed Shijie Village together, gambling and flaunting their tempers, were now forever separated by death. When Song Jiang returned, the navy's achievements were assessed and recalled. Ruan Xiaowu received posthumous honors as one of the fallen and was commemorated among Liangshan's heroic dead, leaving later generations to remember the ferocity, courage, and bold spirit of “Short-Lived Second Brother.”
阮小五，绰号「短命二郎」，应天罪星，梁山泊英雄座次第二十九位，乃水军头领之一。其.ja:
阮小五は「短命二郎」の異名を持ち、天罪星に応じる梁山泊第二十九位の英雄で、水軍頭領の一人である。済州の梁山泊近くにある石碣村の出身で、兄の阮小二、弟の阮小七と共に暮らしていた。家は代々漁を生業とし、そのかたわら水泊で人を殺して荷を奪うなど、堅気ならぬ稼業にも手を染めていた。阮氏三兄弟はいずれも水陸を問わず命を惜しまぬ無頼の好漢であった。次兄の阮小五は機敏で凶猛、目には凶光が宿り、賭博を好んでは気勢を上げ、行動はとりわけ苛烈で果断だった。江湖でつけられた「短命二郎」という渾名は、彼に出くわした者は命を奪う凶星に出会ったも同然で、生きては帰れないという意味であり、その殺気の強さを物語っている。額には青い痣があり、胸には青黒い豹の入れ墨をしていた。普段は破れた頭巾を斜めにかぶり、裸の上半身で水中を行き来した。長く水底に潜み、波をくぐって進む、生まれつきの水の強者だった。呉用が初めて三阮を訪ねて石碣村へ来た時にも、阮小五は賭場ですべてをすっていた。その姿には、賭け好きで気ままな本性がよく表れている。

阮小五が梁山泊へ入ったのも、二人の兄弟と同じく「生辰綱を智取する」という大事件による。東渓村の保正、晁蓋と呉用は、大名府の梁中書が東京の蔡太師へ送る十万貫の誕生祝いの荷を奪おうと計画し、力と胆力のある好漢を求めた。呉用は自ら石碣村へ下り、三阮を説いた。「呉用が知略をもって三阮を仲間に引き入れる」くだりには、三兄弟の英雄らしい肝胆が余すところなく描かれている。当時、官府は漁を禁じ、水泊も賊に占められていたため、三阮は漁猟に苦しみ、家計は衰え、胸には不満が満ちていた。阮小五はとりわけ熱く語り、たとえ天をも揺るがす大事であろうと一勝負してみる、こんな惨めな暮らしよりはましだと言った。こうして晁蓋、呉用、公孫勝、劉唐、白勝と三阮の合わせて七人は、黄泥岡で棗売りの商人に化けた。楊志の護送隊をしびれ薬で眠らせ、生辰綱を奪って悠々と去ったのである。これは梁山泊の事業の幕開けを告げる最初の大事件であり、阮小五は七星の結義の中核を担う一人だった。

事件が発覚すると、官府は済州府の何涛に兵を率いて捕縛へ向かわせたが、三阮は水辺の葦原で官兵を散々に打ち破り、壊滅させた。晁蓋の一行は続いて王倫を倒し、計略によって梁山泊を手に入れ、水泊を占めた。阮小五は阮小二、阮小七と共に水軍を掌り、梁山泊の水寨の根幹となった。その後、童貫を二度破り、高俅を三度退けた戦いでも、三兄弟は水中に伏兵を置き、船底を穿ち、舟を覆し、官軍の将を生け捕りにして、多くの功を挙げた。大集会で序列が定まると、阮小五は「天罪星」として天罡に列せられ、水軍頭領となった。李俊、張横、張順らと共に山寨の水師を統べたのである。

招安後、阮小五は大軍に従って遼を征し、田虎と王慶を討ち、水戦では必ず先鋒を務めた。方臘への南征では、水路が縦横に走る江南が水軍の力を発揮する舞台となった。三阮と他の水軍将領は敵艦を沈め、火攻めを重ね、幾度も奇功を挙げたが、運命は苛酷だった。阮小五も、この惨烈な征戦で最期を迎えた。大軍が方臘の清渓、幇源洞一帯を攻めた時、阮小五は船で奥深く進み、敵将と斬り合った。ある混戦の中、方臘配下の大将の部隊、通行本では婁丞相の軍勢に囲まれた。衆寡敵せず、乱軍の中で斬り殺され、「短命二郎」は王事に殉じ、戦士として世を去った。三兄弟は共に梁山泊へ入り、共に水軍を掌り、共に方臘を征したが、最後に生還したのは阮小七だけだった。阮小二は自刎し、阮小五は戦死した。かつて石碣村を連れ立って行き来し、賭けに興じて気勢を上げた兄弟は、ここに生死を隔てて永遠に別れたのである。のちに宋江が帰還して水軍の功を追叙した際、阮小五も戦死者として追封され、梁山泊の英烈と共に祀られた。後世の人々は、短命二郎の一生を貫いた凶勇と豪烈を偲ぶこととなった。

单廷珪，凌州人氏，原系大宋凌州团练使，乃一方知名的统军之将。其人精熟水战之术，临.en:
Shan Tinggui was a native of Lingzhou and originally served the Great Song as that prefecture's militia commissioner, a locally renowned military commander. He was thoroughly skilled in water warfare and excelled at using water to trap the enemy. Flooding cities or releasing torrents against battle formations came readily to him. Soldiers even said he could summon wind and rain and command the waters, earning him the name “Sacred Water General.” Among Liangshan Marsh's 108 heroes, he corresponded to the Earthly Star of Wonder and occupied the forty-fourth seat, serving as a junior cavalry commander and leader of distant scouting patrols. Together with his fellow officer Wei Dingguo from the same prefecture, he was known as one of the two generals of Lingzhou, one commanding water and the other fire. They had always been as close as brothers, sharing life and death.

Shan Tinggui's road to Liangshan was bound up with Guan Sheng's punitive expedition. When Liangshan's heroes attacked Daming Prefecture to rescue Lu Junyi and Shi Xiu, they shook Hebei and alarmed the Eastern Capital. Hearing the news, Grand Preceptor Cai recommended Guan Sheng, the “Great Blade,” patrol inspector of Pudong and descendant of the Marquis of Hanshou, to lead an expedition against Liangshan and relieve the siege of Daming. Guan Sheng requested the militia commissioners Shan Tinggui and Wei Dingguo as his two supporting commanders. Both had long-established reputations, one for attacks by water and the other for attacks by fire, making them valuable weapons against Liangshan Marsh's water stronghold. Yet when Guan Sheng reached Liangshan, he fell into Song Jiang's trap, and the two commanders were caught in the fighting with him. After Guan Sheng was captured, Song Jiang's sense of loyalty moved him to join Liangshan. Valuing Shan Tinggui and Wei Dingguo's abilities and wishing to recruit them, Song Jiang then sent the newly surrendered Guan Sheng personally to Lingzhou to bring the two over.

Guan Sheng accepted the order and led a force straight toward Lingzhou. When Shan Tinggui and Wei Dingguo heard he was coming, they were shocked and angry, denouncing him for betraying his master and joining bandits. As the armies faced each other, Shan Tinggui rode out first to fight him. Guan Sheng's great blade moved with uncanny skill. Despite all his ability as the Water General, Shan Tinggui could not overcome him. During the combat, Guan Sheng deliberately exposed an opening. Shan Tinggui spurred his horse in pursuit, only for Guan Sheng to seize the opportunity to grab him and pull him across onto his own horse, capturing him alive. Rather than harm his captive, Guan Sheng personally removed his bonds and treated him as a brother. He explained in full Song Gongming's generosity, devotion to justice, and commitment to carrying out Heaven's will. Shan Tinggui already had longstanding ties with Guan Sheng. Seeing his sincerity, he reconsidered and willingly surrendered. He then persuaded Wei Dingguo, who was still holding out, and the two went up the mountain together to join Liangshan. With the two generals of Lingzhou on their side, Liangshan's forces on land and water grew even more formidable.

After joining Liangshan, Shan Tinggui accompanied the army on campaigns in every direction. His mastery of water attacks proved especially effective when storming cities and strongholds or facing an enemy beside a river. He and Wei Dingguo worked together, water and fire complementing one another, and became a capable pair of commanders in Liangshan's army. When the great assembly fixed the ranks, Shan Tinggui was placed among the Earthly Stars and assigned cavalry reconnaissance and vanguard duties. His reputation remained undiminished.

After the amnesty, Shan Tinggui followed Song Jiang on campaigns north and south, first defeating Liao and then helping pacify Tian Hu and Wang Qing. Across thousands of li he repeatedly earned distinction. When the army turned south against Fang La, Liangshan's heroes were killed and wounded in dreadful numbers, and Shan Tinggui also fell in the campaign. The army was attacking Shezhou, where Fang La's commanders used the difficult terrain to hold their defenses through one fierce battle after another. While Shan Tinggui fought outside the city, enemy commanders suddenly charged. In the resulting melee his horse stumbled and fell into a pit or trench, and hostile cavalry rushing through the confused battle trampled him to death. The “Sacred Water General,” master of water attacks and famous throughout Lingzhou, had gone from militia commissioner to Liangshan commander and fought north and south, only to die exhausted in battle instead of reaching a peaceful end. After Song Jiang defeated Fang La and returned to court, the fallen officers received posthumous honors. Shan Tinggui was among them, receiving the title of Gentleman of Loyal Valor, and his spirit returned to his native home. His mastery of water warfare, the sincerity of his allegiance, and the bond through life and death that he shared with Wei Dingguo form another poignant chapter in Liangshan's story.
单廷珪，凌州人氏，原系大宋凌州团练使，乃一方知名的统军之将。其人精熟水战之术，临.ja:
単廷珪は凌州の出身で、もとは大宋の凌州団練使を務め、その地方に名を知られた統軍の将であった。水戦の術に熟達し、戦場では水を用いて敵を窮地に追い込むことを得意とした。城へ水を引いて浸し、堤を切って敵陣を押し流すなど、思いのままに行った。軍中では風雨を呼び、水勢を使役できるとさえ噂され、「聖水将」の異名を得た。梁山泊百八人のうちでは地奇星に応じ、第四十四位に座し、馬軍の小彪将にして遠方の偵察を兼ねる頭領となった。同郡の戦友、魏定国とは、一人が水、一人が火を得意とする凌州二将として並び称された。常に兄弟のように親しく、生死を共にする間柄であった。

単廷珪が梁山泊へ入ったのは、関勝の征討に関わる一件による。梁山泊の好漢が盧俊義と石秀を救うため大名府を攻めると、河北は動揺し、東京にも衝撃が伝わった。報告を聞いた蔡太師は、蒲東の巡検で漢寿亭侯の末裔に当たる「大刀」関勝を推挙し、梁山泊を討って大名府の包囲を解かせようとした。関勝はさらに凌州団練使の単廷珪と魏定国を左右の補佐として願い出た。二将は以前から名高く、一方は水攻め、他方は火攻めを得意とし、梁山泊の水寨を攻めるには格好の戦力であった。ところが梁山泊へ迫った関勝は、かえって宋江の計略にかかり、二将と共に陣中へ陥った。のちに捕らえられた関勝は宋江の義気に感じ、梁山泊へ帰順した。宋江は単廷珪と魏定国の才を惜しんで味方にしたいと考え、降ったばかりの関勝を自ら凌州へ赴かせ、二将を招くよう命じた。

命令を受けた関勝は、一隊を率いてまっすぐ凌州へ向かった。関勝が来たと聞いた単廷珪と魏定国は驚き怒り、主君を裏切って賊に投じたと罵った。両軍が対峙すると、単廷珪が先に馬を進め、関勝と戦った。関勝の大刀は神出鬼没で、水将の力を振るう単廷珪も及ばなかった。斬り合いの途中、関勝がわざと隙を見せると、単廷珪は馬を走らせて追った。その機を捉えた関勝に引っつかまれ、相手の馬上へ引き寄せられて、生け捕りにされてしまった。関勝は捕らえた単廷珪を傷つけるどころか、自ら縄を解き、兄弟の礼をもって遇した。そして宋公明が義を重んじ、財を惜しまず、天に代わって道を行う人物であることを詳しく説いた。もともと関勝とは深い縁があり、その誠意も見えたため、単廷珪は心を改め、進んで帰順した。さらに、なお守りを固めていた魏定国も説得し、二人そろって山へ登り、梁山泊の仲間となった。凌州二将の帰順によって、梁山泊の水陸の軍容はいっそう盛んになった。

梁山泊に加わった単廷珪は、大軍に従って各地を征戦した。水攻めの術は城や砦を落とす時、川を挟んで敵と対陣する時にとりわけ力を発揮した。魏定国と左右に並び、水と火を互いに補わせ、梁山泊軍の有能な一組の将となった。大集会で序列が定まると、単廷珪は地煞に列せられ、馬軍の斥候と先鋒の責任を担い、その威名を落とすことはなかった。

招安後、単廷珪は宋江に従って南北を征し、まず遼国を破り、次いで田虎と王慶を平定した。数千里を転戦して、幾度も戦功を立てた。だが江南へ軍を進めて方臘を討った時、梁山泊の好漢は夥しい死傷者を出し、単廷珪もこの戦役で命を落とした。その時、大軍は歙州を攻めており、方臘配下の守将は険しい地形を頼みに守り、激戦が続いていた。歙州城外で単廷珪が敵軍と斬り合っていると、不意に敵将が勇んで突っ込んできた。混戦の中で乗馬が前足を踏み外し、溝へ転落したところへ敵の騎兵が押し寄せ、踏み殺されて戦場に倒れたのである。水の術に優れ、凌州に名を轟かせた「聖水将」は、団練使から梁山泊へ帰し、南北を転戦した末、力尽きて死に、安らかな最期を得られなかった。宋江が方臘を平定して帰朝すると、朝廷は戦死した将佐を追封し、単廷珪にも忠武郎を贈った。その魂は故郷へ帰った。水攻めの才、帰義の誠、そして魏定国と生死を共にした情誼は、梁山泊の物語の中でも深い感慨を誘う一節である。
